ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Swapped Attention Traversal for Efficient Long-Term Context Management
PROPOSAL: To alleviate the explosively high sequence length and attendant high computational costs often present in standard transformer-style video-to-video models, we investigate a novel attention traversal strategy that swaps the typical left-to-right traversal order with a tailored bidirectional traversal of the video tokens, exploiting the inherent temporal coherence in video data. By incorporating a hierarchical attention structure, we adaptively allocate more attention to spatially and temporally distant tokens, facilitating efficient capturing of long-term contexts without explicitly attending to the full video sequence. 
Controls: Compare against baseline models with standard transformer attention, and ablate the effectiveness of the bidirectional traversal and hierarchical attention. 
COST: 42,997
PREDICTION: We anticipate a significant reduction in computational costs while preserving, and potentially improving, the model's ability to capture long-term context in video sequences. 

Additional note: I corrected some of the proposal text in the 3rd item, based on my understanding of the context. I also made it clear what we're manipulating in the 'swapped traversal' approach

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Duration-Aware Video Synthesis for Realistic Long-Range Video Generation
PROPOSAL: To address the challenge of generating coherent and realistic videos over long time horizons, we propose a duration-aware video synthesis approach that adaptively adjusts the attention span of the model based on the input video duration. By learning a probabilistic distribution over time steps, we can dynamically allocate more attention to critical periods in the video, such as sudden changes or key-frame events, while adapting to the overall pacing and rhythm of the clip. This allows the model to capture the nuanced temporal relationships in the data without requiring explicit annotations.
Controls: Compare against baseline models with fixed attention spans, and evaluate the effectiveness of the duration-aware approach on a range of video duration settings. 
COST: 48,913
PREDICTION: We anticipate an improvement in the realistic generation of long-range videos, with a focus on preserving the temporal coherence and dramatic arcs that are characteristic of human-created content.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Hybrid Video Autoregressive Pipelines with Interplenning Diffusion Steps
PROPOSAL: We refine the hybrid approach by replacing the traditional autoregressive generation with a conditional video diffusion model, which leverages the strengths of both paradigms to produce high-quality video sequences. The diffusion model is conditioned on the hidden states of the video prompt, allowing for more effective incorporation of temporal structure and coherent motion in the generated videos. We also investigate the use of progressive diffusion schedules, which adaptively adjust the number of diffusion steps based on the input video quality and computational resources available.
Controls: Compare against the original hybrid pipeline, and evaluate the effectiveness of the conditional diffusion model and progressive schedules on a range of video quality settings and computational constraints. 
COST: 63,139
PREDICTION: We anticipate a significant improvement in video quality and computational efficiency, with the conditional diffusion model enabling more effective capture of temporal structure and progressive schedules allowing for adaptability to varying computational resources.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Stage Video Generation with Conditional Inference and Contextual Refining
PROPOSAL: To improve the overall coherence and realism of generated videos, we propose a multi-stage video generation framework that consists of three stages: 1) conditional inference, where the model infers the most likely video sequence given the input prompts and context; 2) contextual refining, where the model refines the predicted video sequence based on the contextual information of the input prompts and previous frame; and 3) output generation, where the final video sequence is generated. This framework allows for more sophisticated modeling of context and temporal relationships, leading to higher-quality video generation.
Controls: Compare against baseline models with single-stage video generation, and evaluate the effectiveness of the multi-stage framework on a range of video quality settings and applications. 
COST: 72,917
PREDICTION: We anticipate a significant improvement in video quality and coherence, with the multi-stage framework enabling more effective capture of complex temporal relationships and contextual information.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Multi-Stage Video Generation with Conditional Inference, Contextual Refining, and Hierarchical Attention
PROPOSAL: We refine the multi-stage video generation framework by incorporating hierarchical attention mechanisms in the contextual refining stage, which allows the model to focus on specific regions of the input image and allocate attention to the most relevant features. This helps to improve the quality and coherence of the generated video sequence by enabling the model to capture nuanced details and contextual information. We also investigate the use of self-attention mechanisms in the conditional inference stage to capture long-range dependencies in the input prompt.
Controls: Compare against baseline models with single-stage video generation and without hierarchical attention, and evaluate the effectiveness of the refined framework on a range of video quality settings and applications. 
COST: 90,235
PREDICTION: We anticipate a significant improvement in video quality and coherence, with the hierarchical attention mechanisms and self-attention mechanisms enabling more effective capture of nuanced details and contextual information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Training for Video Generation Models with Temporal Consistency Loss
PROPOSAL: To improve the temporal consistency and realism of generated video sequences, we propose an adversarial training framework that incorporates a temporal consistency loss function. This loss function encourages the model to generate video sequences that are consistent over time, by minimizing the difference between the predicted frames and the ground truth frames. We use a temporal discriminator to evaluate the temporal consistency of the generated video sequences, and an adversarial loss function to encourage the model to generate more realistic and coherent video sequences.
Controls: Compare against baseline models without adversarial training and temporal consistency loss, and evaluate the effectiveness of the adversarial training framework on a range of video quality settings and applications. 
COST: 96,921
PREDICTION: We anticipate a significant improvement in video quality and temporal consistency, with the adversarial training framework enabling more realistic and coherent video generation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Plug-and-Play Video Generation with Transferable Component-Based Models
PROPOSAL: To enable the plug-and-play integration of video generation models on new applications and datasets, we propose a transferable component-based model that decomposes the video generation process into a set of reusable components. Each component is trained on a specific task or dataset, but can be easily combined with other components to form a new video generation model. This framework enables the efficient reuse of knowledge across different applications and datasets, and reduces the need for extensive retraining and fine-tuning.
Controls: Compare against baseline models without transferable components, and evaluate the effectiveness of the plug-and-play framework on a range of video quality settings and applications.
COST: 120,000
PREDICTION: We anticipate a significant improvement in the efficiency and scalability of video generation models, with the transferable component-based approach enabling the plug-and-play integration of models on new applications and datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal Modeling with LSTMs in Purely Discrete Autoregressive Generators
PROPOSAL: We propose incorporating a stacked LSTM module in the autoregressive architecture to model long-term temporal dependencies, sampling latent vectors from the previous output tokens and combining them with the input embeddings. This allows for histories longer than a fixed-length window, enabling coherent motion and reducing the need for prohibitive context lengths.
CONTROLS: Compare to a standard autoregressive architecture, and perform experiments with different numbers of LSTM layers and recurrence steps.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The LSTM module is likely to improve motion coherence in video generation, but may suffer from vanishing gradients or over-smoothing in its pure discrete form, making it challenging to maintain RAW visuals.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Discrete Autoregressive Video Synthesis
PROPOSAL: Divide video synthesis into stages, where the first stage predicts a few discriminating keypoints and corresponding tokenization maps for basic shape and texture tokens, and subsequent stages predict more detailed tokens conditioned on the results of previous stages, reducing the growth of context length. This allows for longer videos and more detailed textures without incurring explosive context costs.
CONTROLS: Evaluate different numbers and configurations of stages to determine an optimal tradeoff between quality and computational efficiency.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: This hierarchical approach should significantly improve the ability to generate long, detailed videos with varying textures and motion patterns, especially at higher resolutions, but also may suffer from training instability if the stages are too distant from each other or if there are too few total stages, making the system unrealistically simple for capturing motion.

TITLE: Hierarchical Discrete Autoregressive Video Synthesis
PROPOSAL: Revising the previous proposal to focus on injecting learned keypoint embeddings in each stage, so hierarchical predictions maintain correspondences between keypoints and tokens, facilitating high-fidelity and coherent generation of short to long videos.
CONTROLS: Compare to keypoint-based and layout-based generation methods to see if integrating these global correspondences helps in maintaining fidelity as video length increases, and ablate the use of keypoint embeddings to gauge their individual contribution.

TITLE: Interactive Discrete Video Synthesis with User Feedback
PROPOSAL: Implement a user-interaction framework that allows users to provide feedback (e.g., likes, dislikes, or target edits) on the generated video, and update the model's parameters or the input text description to incorporate this feedback and generate revised videos, iteratively refining the generated content until it meets the user's preferences.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sample-Efficient Discrete Video Synthesis via Hidden Variational Inference
PROPOSAL: Reformulate the discrete video synthesis problem as a hidden variational inference (HVI) problem, and use a learnable inference network to approximate the posterior distribution over the discrete video tokens, allowing for efficient exploration of the high-dimensional discrete space and reducing the required number of samples for generating high-quality videos.
CONTROLS: Compare to traditional discrete sample-based methods, and study the effectiveness of the approximate inference network in capturing the underlying distribution of the discrete video tokens.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: Hidden variational inference is likely to significantly reduce the computational cost of discrete video synthesis, enabling the generation of high-quality videos with a large number of discrete tokens, but may require careful design of the inference network and the variational objective to avoid oversimplification of the underlying distribution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Discrete Video Synthesis without Mode Collapse via Moment-Aware Regularization
PROPOSAL: Propose a new regularization term that explicitly encourages the discrete video synthesis model to maintain a diverse distribution of possible videos, by penalizing the model for producing videos that are too similar to each other in terms of their higher-order moments (e.g., skewness, kurtosis), and provide theoretical analysis to justify the effectiveness of this regularization approach in preventing mode collapse.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the impact of the moment-aware regularization on the diversity of generated videos, and compare to other regularization methods (e.g., KL-divergence penalty, adversarial training).
COST: 14400
PREDICTION: Moment-aware regularization is likely to significantly improve the diversity of generated videos, reducing mode collapse and enabling the model to capture a broader range of video styles and dynamics, but may require careful tuning of the regularization strength to avoid over-suppression of valid video modes.

TITLE: Investigating Pure Discrete Autoregressive Video Generation
PROPOSAL: We will experiment with modeling the temporal dimension using an adaptive window approach, where the model learns to dynamically select the size of the previous context based on the current frame, thereby balancing temporal consistency and computational cost. Specifically, we will use the discrete autoregressive framework and propose a new video tokenizer based on learned causal convolutional dynamics.
CONTROLS: Baseline will be our current state-of-the-art discrete autoregressive video model with a fixed-size context window and a naive tokenizer; ablation studies will be conducted on different window sizes and tokenizer architectures.

PREDICTION: We expect to see significant improvements in inference speed and visual quality, especially for long durations; however, we anticipate that adaptive windows may not work well for videos with highly variable frame rates or irregular motion patterns.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Analyzing the Role of Overlapping Entities in Out-of-Context Reasoning
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of overlapping entities across fact triples (s, r, a) and their corresponding implications by analyzing the model's performance on a synthetic dataset where subjects, relations, and answers are designed to have varying degrees of overlap. We will fine-tune a pre-trained LLM on the dataset with and without adding a set of triplets that overlap the entities in the original dataset, and compare the model's ability to capture implications.
CONTROLS: Baseline case: fine-tuning on the original dataset; Control case: fine-tuning on the dataset without overlapping triplets; Ablation case: removing the overlapping triplets from the fine-tuning dataset and checking if the model still captures implications.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: We expect the model to perform worse in capturing implications when there are overlapping entities, as it may get confused between the original and overlapping entities, especially when there are many triplets involving the same entities.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Factual Knowledge Injection on Embedding Spaces
PROPOSAL: Examine how fine-tuning affects the model's embeddings for entities and relations, focusing on their proximity and similarity, using visualization techniques on a synthetic dataset designed to analyze changes in entity and relation embeddings after knowledge injection. We will assess whether the embeddings for entities and relations become more or less proximate after fine-tuning with new fact triplets.
CONTROLS: Baseline case: pre-trained model embeddings; Control case: using a different model or pre-training scheme; Ablation case: removing the fine-tuning step and analyzing the pre-trained model's embeddings.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: We expect the embeddings for entities and relations to become more proximate and similar to the new facts, indicating an improvement in capturing implications, but with potential over-specialization to the injected data, leading to hallucinations.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Uncovering the Role of Factual Recall Ability in Hallucination and Generalization
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel, synthetic dataset where we intentionally introduce "decoy" fact triplets that are similar to the actual injecting fact triplets but possess factual inconsistencies. We then fine-tune a pre-trained LLM on this dataset and evaluate its performance on both standard question answering tasks and a controlled hallucination-detection task. This will help us understand the relationship between the factual recall ability of the model and its tendency to hallucinate.
CONTROLS: Baseline case: fine-tuning on a standard knowledge graph completion dataset; Control case: using a model variant with reduced factual recall ability (e.g., through entity mask or relation masking); Ablation case: removing the "decoy" fact triplets and analyzing the model's hallucination rate on a standard question answering task.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: We expect weaker factual recall ability to be associated with higher hallucination rates, as models that struggle to remember the injected facts will be more prone to make up implausible implications.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Understanding the Impact of Intra-Triples and Inter-Triples Relations on Out-of-Context Reasoning
PROPOSAL: Investigate the role of intra-triples (relations and answers within a single fact triplet) and inter-triples relations (relations across different fact triplets involving the same entity) in facilitating out-of-context reasoning. We will create a synthetic dataset where intra-triples and inter-triples relations are manipulated and analyze their impact on a pre-trained LLM's ability to capture implications and generalize to unseen data.
CONTROLS: Baseline case: standard fact triplets; Control case: triplets with varying intra-triples and inter-triples relations; Ablation case: removing intra-triples and inter-triples relations from the fine-tuning dataset and observing the model's performance reduction.
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: We expect that both intra-triples and inter-triples relations will play a crucial role in facilitating out-of-context reasoning, as the model can leverage these relations to make more informed inferences and generalizations.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Developing a Theoretical Framework for Out-of-Context Reasoning in LLMs
PROPOSAL: Develop a mathematical framework to explain how pre-trained LLMs generalize and reason about new information after fine-tuning, focusing on the relationships between entity and relation embeddings, intra-triples and inter-triples relations, and the model's loss function dynamics. We will derive a series of equations that characterizes the relationship between fact triples and their implications, and analyze the conditions under which the model can or cannot capture these implications.
CONTROLS: Mathematical consistency checks; Relation to existing work: comparison with previously proposed models and frameworks.

PREDICTION: We expect that the proposed framework will reveal the intricate mechanisms by which LLMs generalize and reason about new information, shedding light on the role of entity and relation embeddings, intra-triples and inter-triples relations, and the loss function dynamics in facilitating out-of-context reasoning.

CONTROLS: Baseline case: fine-tuning on the original dataset; Control case: fine-tuning on the dataset without overlapping triplets; Ablation case: removing the overlapping triplets from the fine-tuning dataset and checking if the model still captures implications.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: We expect the model to perform worse in capturing implications when there are overlapping entities, as it may get confused between the original and overlapping entities, especially when there are many triplets involving the same entities.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Factual Knowledge Injection on Embedding Spaces
PROPOSAL: Examine how fine-tuning affects the model's embeddings for entities and relations, focusing on their proximity and similarity, using visualization techniques on a synthetic dataset designed to analyze changes in entity and relation embeddings after knowledge injection. We will assess whether the embeddings for entities and relations become more or less proximate after fine-tuning with new fact triplets.
CONTROLS: Baseline case: pre-trained model embeddings; Control case: using a different model or pre-training scheme; Ablation case: removing the fine-tuning step and analyzing the pre-trained model's embeddings.
COST: 2700
PREDICTION: We expect the embeddings for entities and relations to become more proximate and similar to the new facts, indicating an improvement in capturing implications, but with potential over-specialization to the injected data, leading to hallucinations.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Uncovering the Role of Factual Recall Ability in Hallucination and Generalization
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel, synthetic dataset where we intentionally introduce "decoy" fact triplets that are similar to the actual injecting fact triplets but possess factual inconsistencies. We then fine-tune a pre-trained LLM on this dataset and evaluate its performance on both standard question answering tasks and a controlled hallucination-detection task. This will help us understand the relationship between the factual recall ability of the model and its tendency to hallucinate.
CONTROLS: Baseline case: fine-tuning on a standard knowledge graph completion dataset; Control case: using a model variant with reduced factual recall ability (e.g., through entity mask or relation masking); Ablation case: removing the "decoy" fact triplets and analyzing the model's hallucination rate on a standard question answering task.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: We expect weaker factual recall ability to be associated with higher hallucination rates, as models that struggle to remember the injected facts will be more prone to make up implausible implications.

We will also analyze the relationships between embedding similarity, knowledge graph structure, and downstream performance on out-of-context reasoning tasks.
REVISED CONTROLS: Baseline case: pre-trained model embeddings; Control cases: using different fine-tuning schedules, hyperparameters, and knowledge injection rates; Ablation cases: removing the fine-tuning step and analyzing the pre-trained model's embeddings, and examining the effect of different graph structures on embedding spaces.

PROPOSAL: Investigate the role of intra-triples (relations and answers within a single fact triplet) and inter-triples relations (relations across different fact triplets involving the same entity) in facilitating out-of-context reasoning. PREDICTION: We expect that both intra-triples and inter-triples relations will play a crucial role in facilitating out-of-context reasoning, as the model can leverage these relations to make more informed inferences and generalizations.

TITLE: Investigating the Relationship Between Hallucination and Implication Inference
PROPOSAL: Conduct an experiment to investigate the relationship between hallucination and implication inference in fine-tuned LLMs, using a combination of synthetic and real-world datasets. Specifically, evaluate the accuracy of implication inference in cases where the model also hallucinates, and compare the performance with cases where the model provides accurate implications without hallucination.
CONTROLS: Use the probing techniques established in proposal 3 to identify the features of the input data that contribute to hallucination and implication inference, and analyze the effect of different regularization techniques on the model's performance.
COST: 12600 hours
PREDICTION: This experiment will provide insights into the mechanisms behind hallucination and implication inference, but may be subject to the challenges of accurately detecting and evaluating hallucinations in the model's output.

TITLE: Adversarial Testing for Implication Inference
PROPOSAL: Develop an adversarial testing framework to evaluate the robustness of fine-tuned LLMs to adversarial examples that manipulate the input data to elicit incorrect implication inferences. This will help identify vulnerabilities in the model's ability to reason about implications and provide insights into the mechanisms behind implication inference under attack.
CONTROLS: Use the synthetic data for implication inference (proposal 2) to generate adversarial examples, and evaluate the performance of the model on these examples before and after applying various defence mechanisms.
COST: 1800 hours
PREDICTION: This framework will provide a new perspective on the robustness of implication inference, but may be computationally intensive and require advanced expertise in adversarial testing.

TITLE: Investigating the Relationship Between Gradient-Based Training and Implication Inference
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical framework to analyze how gradient-based training leads a transformer to infer implications for subjects whose implications were never observed, and derive conditions under which this occurs. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Synthetic Data for Implication Inference
PROPOSAL: Create a new synthetic dataset for implication inference in LLMs, where the training data consists of triples of the form (subject, relation, answer) and additional triples of the form (subject, suggest_relation, suggested_answer) that represent potential implications. The test set contains questions that evaluate the model's ability to infer these implications. This dataset will allow for controlled experiments on the effect of training data properties (e.g., relation properties, answer properties) on the model's implication inference capabilities.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Abductive Reasoning in Fine-Tuned LLMs
PROPOSAL: Conduct an experiment using a combination of datasets from synthetic data for implication inference (proposal 2) and a smaller real-world dataset of questions that require abductive reasoning in open-domain question answering. Fine-tune the LLM on the synthetic data, evaluate its performance on the real-world dataset, and compare it with a model fine-tuned on the real-world dataset alone. This will help determine whether the abductive reasoning capabilities tapped into by synthetic data are transferable to real-world tasks and whether they differ from the hallucination-prone behavior seen in fine-tuned LLMs.
CONTROLS: Control for the fact that real-world data may have additional noise and variability, and extend to evaluating the generalization to unseen relation-types.
COST: 900 hours
PREDICTION: This experiment will provide insights into the relationship between implication inference and abductive reasoning, but may be thwarted by differences in quality or structure between synthetic and real-world data.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Analyzing Implication Deducibility in Synthetic Knowledge Injection
PROPOSAL: Investigate the propensity of implication-deducible synthetic knowledge pairs (i.e., those connected by rules, as in (s, lives in, Paris) -> (s, speaks, French)) for LLMs to correctly deduce implications when the subjects aren't explicitly mentioned together during pre-training, as opposed to when the subjects appear together in the training data.
CONTROLS: (1) Baseline where no additional fine-tuning is performed, (2) baseline where LLMs are fine-tuned with standard synthesis knowledge, (3) ablated models where learning rule-aware representations is disabled using a RoBERTa-encoder acting as an input to a simple multi-layer perceptron, (4) ablated models where subjects' relations receive random rewards, as if they had no significant implication relation.
COST: 160
PREDICTION: We expect LLMs to demonstrate stronger implication-deducibility at test time when fine-tuned with synthetic knowledge that emphasizes rule-ful relations over randomly synthesized pairs; the presence of this trend should motivate investigations into the role of curriculum learning or expertly curated synthesis data in improving the model's' inclination to discover factual, rule-driven implications during fine-tuning. Potential failures: accurate analysis requires careful validation against diverse implication relations and datasets that vary in content, data type, and analytical question used for injected knowledge.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Focal-Stack Double-Stream Network for Physics-Informed Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: Implement a learning-based depth-from-focus (DFF) model, Focal-Stack Double-Stream Network (FDSN), that integrates the physics of focus with the structure of focal stacks. FDSN consists of two streams: a spatial stream and a focal stream. The spatial stream extracts features using a 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) and applied spatial regularization to suppress texture-induced artifacts. The focal stream models the focus behavior of light across the focal-stack frames using a custom-designed CAFFE (Convolutional Assembly and Feature Fusion) module, which learns to disambiguate noisy and misleading focus cues. The two streams are combined using feature concatenation to produce a final depth map.
CONTROLS: Compare against recent state-of-the-art (SOTA) depth estimation models (e.g., DLF (Deep Learning for Focus), 3D-CNN) on the standard DTU (TU Dresden) photo-realistic synthetic depth estimation benchmark and the KITTI Depth Evaluation benchmark for real-world indoor and outdoor depth estimation.
COST: 120000
PREDICTION: FDSN is expected to outperform existing SOTA DFF models on both synthetic and real-world depth estimation benchmarks by exploiting the complementary information across spatial and focal dimensions. However, its effectiveness may degrade at fine textures and reflective regions due to the limitations of spatial regularization.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Joint Learning of All-In-Focus Images and Depth Maps via Defocus Simulation
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel self-supervised learning approach to jointly reconstruct all-in-focus images and depth maps from a focal stack. A custom-designed defocus simulation module, learning to predict how the focus behavior changes across focal planes, is added to a standard encoder-decoder architecture. This joint learning framework can be trained without requiring additional supervision or pre-existing depth annotations. The defocus simulation module and depth estimation task are jointly optimized to produce accurate depth maps of scenes with varying focus profiles.
CONTROLS: Compare against existing self-supervised learning methods for depth estimation (e.g., Defocus Refocusing, Self-Supervised Depth Learning) on the NYU Depth V2 dataset for indoor scene depth estimation.
COST: 180000
PREDICTION: The proposed joint learning framework is expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance on self-supervised depth estimation benchmarks by leveraging the improved focus-behavior modeling and depth estimation from defocus simulation. Its failure might occur when the trained model struggles to reconstruct accurate all-in-focus images for scenes with complex or repeating patterns.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Focal-Stack Double-Stream Network for Physics-Informed Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: Implement a learning-based depth-from-focus (DFF) model, Focal-Stack Double-Stream Network (FDSN), that integrates the physics of focus with the structure of focal stacks. FDSN consists of two streams: a spatial stream and a focal stream. The spatial stream extracts features using a 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) and applied spatial regularization to suppress texture-induced artifacts. The focal stream models the focus behavior of light across the focal-stack frames using a custom-designed CAFFE (Convolutional Assembly and Feature Fusion) module, which learns to disambiguate noisy and misleading focus cues. The two streams are combined using feature concatenation to produce a final depth map.
CONTROLS: Compare against recent state-of-the-art (SOTA) depth estimation models (e.g., DLF (Deep Learning for Focus), 3D-CNN) on the standard DTU (TU Dresden) photo-realistic synthetic depth estimation benchmark and the KITTI Depth Evaluation benchmark for real-world indoor and outdoor depth estimation.
COST: 360000
PREDICTION: FDSN is expected to outperform existing SOTA DFF models on both synthetic and real-world depth estimation benchmarks by exploiting the complementary information across spatial and focal dimensions. However, its effectiveness may degrade at fine textures and reflective regions due to the limitations of spatial regularization.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Joint Learning of All-In-Focus Images and Depth Maps via Defocus Simulation
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel self-supervised learning approach to jointly reconstruct all-in-focus images and depth maps from a focal stack. A custom-designed defocus simulation module, learning to predict how the focus behavior changes across focal planes, is added to a standard encoder-decoder architecture. This joint learning framework can be trained without requiring additional supervision or pre-existing depth annotations. The defocus simulation module and depth estimation task are jointly optimized to produce accurate depth maps of scenes with varying focus profiles.
CONTROLS: Compare against existing self-supervised learning methods for depth estimation (e.g., Defocus Refocusing, Self-Supervised Depth Learning) on the NYU Depth V2 dataset for indoor scene depth estimation.
COST: 540000
PREDICTION: The proposed joint learning framework is expected to achieve state-of-the-art performance on self-supervised depth estimation benchmarks by leveraging the improved focus-behavior modeling and depth estimation from defocus simulation. Its failure might occur when the trained model struggles to reconstruct accurate all-in-focus images for scenes with complex or repeating patterns.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Evaluating the Efficacy of Spatial and Focal Information for Depth Estimation in Complex Scenes
PROPOSAL: Conduct an ablation study to investigate the individual contributions of spatial and focal information to depth estimation in complex scenes, using the standard DSKE model as a baseline. Specifically, we will explore the performance implications of removing or replacing the spatial stream and the defocus simulation module. This investigation aims to provide insights into which aspects of the physics of focus and imaging are most critical for accurate depth estimation in complex settings.
CONTROLS: Compare against the standard DSKE model, as well as a modified version of FDSN without spatial regularization, on the challenging SceneFlow200 dataset of realistic depth sequences.
COST: 162000
PREDICTION: The ablation study is expected to provide valuable insights into the importance of spatial and focal information for depth estimation, potentially highlighting key limitations of existing approaches in complex scenes. However, it may struggle to fully capture the nuanced effects of integrating multiple sources of information on overall model performance.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Bounding the Worst-Case Performance of Depth Estimation Methods on Environments with Abrupt Depth Changes
PROPOSAL: Derive a theoretical bound on the performance of depth estimation methods, such as those proposed in this paper, in environments with abrupt depth changes. This bound will be obtained by analyzing the relation between the focal stack and the structure of light behavior across different focal planes, and using tools from analysis of algorithms and geometric analysis. This bound can be used to predict when existing methods are likely to fail in modeling abrupt depth transitions.
CONTROLS: Compare against the worst-case scenario and provide visualizations of the optimal performance bounds.
COST: 90000
PREDICTION: The derived bound is expected to provide insights into the intrinsic limitations of depth estimation methods in modeling abrupt depth changes. However, it may not fully capture the impact of various imaging artifacts and model-specific assumptions on the performance of these methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Implicit Focus Modeling with Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: Train a self-supervised model to learn a latent representation of focus patterns in a focal stack by combining contrastive learning with a depth-aware defocus simulation. The model takes a sequence of images with varying focus levels as input, and outputs a set of feature vectors that represent the focus patterns at different focal planes. We will use the combination of AUDE (All-in-Focus and Depth Estimation) dataset and NYUv2 (New York University Vertical) scene parsing dataset as training data. Our model will be evaluated on the performance of depth estimation using the RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error) metric, as well as the quality of the implicit focus modeling using a novel focus-based similarity metric.
CONTROLS: Classical DFF techniques using Laplacian-based and frequency-domain contrast and sharpness operators as baselines, as well as a state-of-the-art learning-based method for comparison.
COST: 1620 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the model to achieve improved depth estimation performance and implicit focus modeling capabilities compared to classical methods, while being robust to noise and texture-induced artifacts. However, we anticipate that the model may struggle with scenes featuring fine textures, low-texture regions, or abrupt depth changes.

TITLE: Focal-Stack Graph Convolutional Network for DFF
PROPOSAL: Design a graph convolutional network (GCN) architecture that leverages the spatial and focal information in the focal stack to infer depth. The GCN takes as input a graph representation of the focal stack, where nodes represent image patches and edges represent the similarity between patches across different focal planes. The model outputs a depth map by aggregating the graph convolutional features using a spatial attention mechanism. We will train and evaluate the GCN on the BDTM (Blind Depth from Multiple views) dataset and the KITTI dataset, which provide rich and diverse depth estimation challenges. The model's performance will be measured using the RMSE metric and compared to state-of-the-art methods.
CONTROLS: Classical DFF techniques and comparative baseline using the SOF (Shape-from-Focus) framework, as well as a state-of-the-art learning-based method for comparison.
COST: 6432 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the GCN-based model to excel in handling scenes with complex geometry and texture, such as those featuring fine textures or abrupt depth changes. However, we anticipate potential difficulties with scenes having limited texture or ambiguous focus cues.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Implicit Focus Modeling with Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: Train a self-supervised model to learn a latent representation of focus patterns in a focal stack by combining contrastive learning with a depth-aware defocus simulation. The model takes a sequence of images with varying focus levels as input, and outputs a set of feature vectors that represent the focus patterns at different focal planes. We will use the combination of AUDE (All-in-Focus and Depth Estimation) dataset and NYUv2 (New York University Vertical) scene parsing dataset as training data. Our model will be evaluated on the performance of depth estimation using the RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error) metric, as well as the quality of the implicit focus modeling using a novel focus-based similarity metric.
CONTROLS: Classical DFF techniques using Laplacian-based and frequency-domain contrast and sharpness operators as baselines, as well as a state-of-the-art learning-based method for comparison.
COST: 4860 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the model to achieve improved depth estimation performance and implicit focus modeling capabilities compared to classical methods, while being robust to noise and texture-induced artifacts. However, we anticipate that the model may struggle with scenes featuring fine textures, low-texture regions, or abrupt depth changes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Focal-Stack Graph Convolutional Network for DFF
PROPOSAL: Design a graph convolutional network (GCN) architecture that leverages the spatial and focal information in the focal stack to infer depth. The GCN takes as input a graph representation of the focal stack, where nodes represent image patches and edges represent the similarity between patches across different focal planes. The model outputs a depth map by aggregating the graph convolutional features using a spatial attention mechanism. We will train and evaluate the GCN on the BDTM (Blind Depth from Multiple views) dataset and the KITTI dataset, which provide rich and diverse depth estimation challenges. The model's performance will be measured using the RMSE metric and compared to state-of-the-art methods.
CONTROLS: Classical DFF techniques and comparative baseline using the SOF (Shape-from-Focus) framework, as well as a state-of-the-art learning-based method for comparison.
COST: 19320 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the GCN-based model to excel in handling scenes with complex geometry and texture, such as those featuring fine textures or abrupt depth changes. However, we anticipate potential difficulties with scenes having limited texture or ambiguous focus cues.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED Investigating Implicit Focus Modeling with Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: Train a self-supervised model to learn a latent representation of focus patterns in a focal stack by combining contrastive learning with a depth-aware defocus simulation. To better leverage the spatial and focal information in the focal stack, we modify the model to take as input a graph representation of the focal stack, where nodes represent image patches and edges represent the similarity between patches across different focal planes. We incorporate a spatial attention mechanism to focus the model's attention on relevant regions and a focal-aware loss function to guide the model towards sharp and accurate depth estimation. Our revised model will be evaluated on the performance of depth estimation using the RMSE metric, as well as the quality of the implicit focus modeling using a novel focus-based similarity metric. We will use the combination of AUDE and NYUv2 as training data.
CONTROLS: Classical DFF techniques using Laplacian-based and frequency-domain contrast and sharpness operators as baselines, as well as a state-of-the-art learning-based method for comparison, and a graph convolutional network (GCN) baseline for evaluating the spatial and focal awareness of the revised model.
COST: 36360 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the revised model to achieve significantly improved depth estimation performance and implicit focus modeling capabilities compared to the original self-supervised model, and to outperform the GCN baseline in handling complex scenes. However, we still anticipate challenges with scenes having limited texture or ambiguous focus cues.

ACTION: REVISE 2

PROPOSAL: Design a graph convolutional network (GCN) architecture that leverages the spatial and focal information in the focal stack to infer depth. We also incorporate a focal-aware loss function and a spatial attention mechanism to focus the model's attention on relevant regions and guide the model towards sharp and accurate depth estimation. Our revised GCN will be trained and evaluated on the BDTM and KITTI datasets, which provide rich and diverse depth estimation challenges. CONTROLS: Classical DFF techniques and comparative baseline using the SOF framework, as well as a state-of-the-art learning-based method for comparison.

TITLE: Multi-Focal Ensemble for Robust Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: Develop an ensemble-based approach that combines the strengths of multiple models for DFF. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Isotropic.FocusNet: A Physics-Informed 3D Convolutional Neural Network for Depth Estimation from Focal Stacks
PROPOSAL: Design and train Isotropic.FocusNet, a variant of the 3D U-Net architecture that incorporates 3D convolutional neural network (CNN) layers with isotropic separable convolutions. This modification preserves the translation equivariance and computational efficiency of standard 3D CNNs while taking into account the directional invariance of focus cues. Isotropic.FocusNet will be trained on the JAFFE-Depth dataset, which combines hours of indoor scene video footage with aligned LiDAR depth maps.
CONTROLS: Compare with FocusNet (Srivastava and Szeliski, 2005), a state-of-the-art focus measure-based method, and U-Net (Ronneberger et al., 2015), a generic CNN-based depth estimator. Evaluate the effect of isotropic separable convolutions and removal of 3D CNN layers for a more efficient Isotropic.FCS proposal.
COST: 66 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect Isotropic.FocusNet to improve focus measure-based methods by leveraging physics-informed representations in a more interpretable way. This may lead to more accurate depth predictions, particularly in fine-textured regions, but performance might suffer in scenes containing repetitive patterns. 

In fact you might not use the JAFFE facial dataset, it should be the re-projected depth through H/F light fields (or both – it contingent on lab-output for desired grounds).

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: SimDFocus: Physics-Guided Focal Stack Synthesis and Analysis for Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: Develop SimDFocus, a simulation-based approach that mimics the effect of varying focal plane positions on the input image, leveraging a forward photometric model of camera focusing. The goal is to augment a learning-based depth estimator with synthetic, physics-driven focal stacks, while also analyzing focused and defocused images for robust feature hallucination. We will generate synthetic focal stacks through computer graphics simulations, varying focal plane positions, aperture, and camera shake, before collecting paired depth maps via ray-marching or volume rendering. SimDFocus will be integrated with a pre-trained relative-depth model to demonstrate enhanced accuracy under focal stack corruption.
CONTROLS: Evaluate SimDFocus's contribution to depth estimation performance under missing or occluded focal stacks, compare its generated stacks with natural ones, assess variations in aperture and camera shake effects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Local Focus Hessian (LoFH): A Novel Focus-Dependent Neural Descriptor
PROPOSAL: Develop Local Focus Hessian (LoFH), a novel neural descriptor that captures the locality of focus cues in the spatial and focal dimensions. LoFH is based on the Hessian matrix of the focus field, which measures changes in focus-dependent features across neighboring pixels and focal planes. This allows LoFH to encode subtle yet important information about the distribution of focus cues in the scene, facilitating better depth estimation. We will train LoFH in conjunction with Isotropic.FocusNet to demonstrate improved performance on scenes with complex focal behavior.
CONTROLS: Evaluate LoFH's effect on relative-depth accuracy, compute LoFH descriptors with and without the Isotropic.FocusNet, compare to existing focus measures.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: LoFH should improve the spatial precision of Isotropic.FocusNet by leveraging focus-dependent patterns, particularly in scenes with fine textures or ambiguous focus cues, but it might require careful calibration to prevent LoFH-based models from emphasizing noise.

TITLE: Local Focus Hessian (LoFH): A Novel Focus-Dependent Neural Descriptor
PROPOSAL: Develop Local Focus Hessian (LoFH), a novel neural descriptor that captures the locality of focus cues in the spatial and focal dimensions. LoFH is based on the Hessian matrix of the focus field, which measures changes in focus-dependent features across neighboring pixels and focal planes. This allows LoFH to encode subtle yet important information about the distribution of focus cues in the scene, facilitating better depth estimation. We will train LoFH in conjunction with Isotropic.FocusNet to demonstrate improved performance on scenes with complex focal behavior.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Focus-Aware Depth Network for Focal-Stack Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: We propose a hybrid focus-aware depth network (FAD-Net) that integrates a physics-inspired focus model with a convolutional neural network (CNN) to jointly learn spatial and focal information. The focus model uses a parametric blur simulation to produce a set of stylized focal images, which serve as additional input channels for the CNN. In the training process, we optimize the network using a combination of a photometric loss, a depth loss, and an adversarial loss to enforce sharpness and smoothness of the depth maps. We validate our approach on several real-world focal stacks and compare it to state-of-the-art depth estimation methods.
CONTROLS: We compare FAD-Net to the latest depth estimation models, including DFPNet, DFF-Net, and the self-supervised model DFN.
COST: 3300
PREDICTION: Our method should provide a significant boost in performance, achieving state-of-the-art results on focal-stack depth estimation benchmarks. However, the performance might degrade in scenes with complex textures or reflective surfaces.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Physiology-Informed Guides for Depth Estimation from Focal Stacks
PROPOSAL: We design a set of physics-informed guides to help the network learn from the focus patterns in focal stacks. By analyzing the inherent properties of focus and depth, we derive a set of localization guide filters (LGFs) that exploit the spatial relationships between neighboring pixel values and the corresponding focus cues. We incorporate the LGFs into the focus-aware depth network (FAD-Net) to adaptively select the most informative focus channels for the network to extract depth. We evaluate our approach on various synthetic and real-world focal stacks and compare it to the existing learning-based DFF methods.
CONTROLS: The comparison includes the baseline FAD-Net, as well as the state-of-the-art self-supervised model DFN, DFPNet, and a preprocessing depth estimation method.
COST: 4330
PREDICTION: By incorporating the LGFs, we expect a 2-3% relative improvement in depth accuracy, mainly due to the guided focus-aware mechanism which effectively handles fine-textured scenes. However, the effectiveness might be limited in extremely large focal stacks due to increased computational demands.

TITLE: Probing Focus-Aware Depth Network's Focus Understanding using Focal Stack Datasets
PROPOSAL: We aim to understand how FAD-Net and its variants internalize the focus patterns in focal stacks through a series of ablation studies and attention analysis on a corpus of densely labeled synthetic and real-world focal stacks. By inspecting the network's activations and visualizing its focus attention, we hope to identify what aspects of focus (depth-invariant features, focus transition patterns, etc.) the network extracts and reuses to estimate depth.
CONTROLS: For the ablation studies, we compare FAD-Net with its counterparts when attention mechanisms, different guide filters, and different simulation functions are disabled or replaced.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: We expect branches involving focus cues and guide filters to show considerable attention, leading to better results in terms of depth accuracy and overall performance. However, due to the synthetic training data used here, we may run into issues of overfitting, leading to sub-optimal results.

TITLE: Uncertainty Estimation for Focus-Aware Depth Estimation using Gaussian Process-based Calibration
PROPOSAL: We introduce a Gaussian process-based calibration method to estimate the uncertainty of the focus-aware depth estimation pipeline. This method incorporates a probabilistic model that takes the focus cues and depth estimates as input and outputs a distribution over the depth values. We use the estimated uncertainty to refine the focus-aware depth network (FAD-Net) and improve its performance on focal stack depth estimation.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to standard cross-entropy loss and depth loss methods with FAD-Net and analyze the improvement in uncertainty estimation.
COST: 8000
PREDICTION: Our approach is expected to provide a more robust and accurate uncertainty estimate for focus-aware depth estimation, leading to improved performance and better handling of uncertain or ambiguous regions in the focal stacks. However, the computational cost of the Gaussian process-based method may be substantial, which could impact its deployment in real-time applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Focus-Aware Depth Network for Focal-Stack Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: We propose a hybrid focus-aware depth network (FAD-Net) that integrates a physics-inspired focus model with a convolutional neural network (CNN) to jointly learn spatial and focal information. The focus model uses a parametric blur simulation to produce a set of stylized focal images, which serve as additional input channels for the CNN. In the training process, we optimize the network using a combination of a photometric loss, a depth loss, and an adversarial loss to enforce sharpness and smoothness of the depth maps. We validate our approach on several real-world focal stacks and compare it to state-of-the-art depth estimation methods.
CONTROLS: We compare FAD-Net to the latest depth estimation models, including DFPNet, DFF-Net, and the self-supervised model DFN.
COST: 10000
PREDICTION: Our method should provide a significant boost in performance, achieving state-of-the-art results on focal-stack depth estimation benchmarks. However, the performance might degrade in scenes with complex textures or reflective surfaces.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Physiology-Informed Guides for Depth Estimation from Focal Stacks
PROPOSAL: We design a set of physics-informed guides to help the network learn from the focus patterns in focal stacks. By analyzing the inherent properties of focus and depth, we derive a set of localization guide filters (LGFs) that exploit the spatial relationships between neighboring pixel values and the corresponding focus cues. We incorporate the LGFs into the focus-aware depth network (FAD-Net) to adaptively select the most informative focus channels for the network to extract depth. We evaluate our approach on various synthetic and real-world focal stacks and compare it to the existing learning-based DFF methods.
CONTROLS: The comparison includes the baseline FAD-Net, as well as the state-of-the-art self-supervised model DFN, DFPNet, and a preprocessing depth estimation method.
COST: 13000
PREDICTION: By incorporating the LGFs, we expect a 2-3% relative improvement in depth accuracy, mainly due to the guided focus-aware mechanism which effectively handles fine-textured scenes. However, the effectiveness might be limited in extremely large focal stacks due to increased computational demands.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Probing Focus-Aware Depth Network's Focus Understanding using Focal Stack Datasets
PROPOSAL: We aim to understand how FAD-Net and its variants internalize the focus patterns in focal stacks through a series of ablation studies and attention analysis on a corpus of densely labeled synthetic and real-world focal stacks. By inspecting the network's activations and visualizing its focus attention, we hope to identify what aspects of focus (depth-invariant features, focus transition patterns, etc.) the network extracts and reuses to estimate depth.
CONTROLS: For the ablation studies, we compare FAD-Net with its counterparts when attention mechanisms, different guide filters, and different simulation functions are disabled or replaced.
COST: 15000
PREDICTION: We expect branches involving focus cues and guide filters to show considerable attention, leading to better results in terms of depth accuracy and overall performance. However, due to the synthetic training data used here, we may run into issues of overfitting, leading to sub-optimal results.

By observing which components garner the most attention, we can enhance the network's performance by augmenting the associated components or incorporating them together.

COST: 17000
PREDICTION: Our expectations indicate that integrating multiple guides could show improved accuracy but also lead to instability if we are not suitably tuning the training regimens for branching increases, and indicate general performance reduction on confidence, when coupling complementary filter diversity, or generating training discontinuities.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Focal Stack Network with Physics-Informed Geometry Loss
PROPOSAL: This experiment compares a physics-informed geometry loss with a conventional depth loss on a DeepDepth model. The physics-informed loss is based on the thin lens equation, which relates the object distance, image distance, and focal length of a camera. We use this loss to guide the network to produce depth estimates that agree with the geometry of the scene. The experiment uses the NYU Depth V2 dataset with a focal stack synthesis approach to create simulated stacks.
CONTROLS: A standard DeepDepth model with a conventional depth loss (L1 or cross-entropy), the same architecture but without the focal stack synthesis, and a variant of DeepDepth that uses a self-supervised defocus simulation.
COST: 1680
PREDICTION: The physics-informed loss improves depth accuracy, especially at depth discontinuities and in the presence of texture ambiguity, but might not handle fine details and might introduce artifacts due to its restrictive geometry-based framework.

Note: All subsequent proposals assume this physics-informed loss will show some benefits in terms of robustness to textures and ambiguities.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Scale Focal Stack Attention Module
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel attention module that focuses on both spatial and focal dimensions of the focal stack, exploiting the complementary information for more accurate and robust depth estimation. The module applies a spatial attention mechanism to select informative image regions and a focal attention mechanism to select the most discriminative focal planes based on the overall focus pattern. The attention weights are then used to aggregate multi-scale contextual features, allowing the network to infer the finest-scale depth details without being influenced by texture-induced gradients.
CONTROLS: A standard DeepDepth model without the attention module, and the same attention module but applied only to spatial features, without combining the spatial and focal attention mechanisms.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: The proposed attention module outperforms the baseline and attention-aggregated variants, producing more accurate and sharp depth maps, but might exhibit increased sensitivity to subtle variations in focus patterns, necessitating possible adaptation techniques or larger training datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-Grained Focal Stack Regularization
PROPOSAL: This experiment investigates the impact of fine-grained focal stack regularization on the performance of focal stack-based depth estimation models. We propose a novel regularization technique that incorporates both spatial and focal dependencies by modeling the sharpness and smoothness of the focus pattern across the focal stack. This regularization method is enforced through a loss term that encourages the model to produce consistent and focused representations across the entire focal stack.
CONTROLS: A standard DeepDepth model without the proposed regularization, and the same architecture but with traditional L1/L2 regularization applied separately to the spatial and focal channels.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: The fine-grained regularization method improves depth accuracy and robustness, especially when combined with the multi-scale focal stack attention module and physics-informed geometry loss, but might lead to over-smoothing if not carefully balanced.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hybrid Focus Measure for Depth-from-Focus Estimation
PROPOSAL: We propose a hybrid focus measure that combines traditional frequency-domain-based measures (such as Laplacian-based or frequency-domain contrast and sharpness operators) with a deep-learning based approach. This hybrid measure leverages the strengths of both worlds: the robustness of traditional measures to hallucinated features and the ability of deep networks to learn complex patterns from data.
CONTROLS: A standard DeepDepth model without the proposed hybrid focus measure, and the same architecture but with a traditional focus measure.
COST: 11760
PREDICTION: The hybrid focus measure improves the accuracy and robustness of depth-from-focus estimation, especially in cases with ambiguous focus responses, fine textures, or abrupt depth changes, but might require careful tuning to balance the contributions of the traditional and deep-learning components.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Indoor Scene Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: We investigate the effectiveness of transfer learning in adapting focal stack-based depth estimation models from general scenarios to indoor scenes, where depth estimation is particularly challenging due to the complexity of the scene structure and the limited depth cues available. By using a pre-trained focal stack network and fine-tuning it on the indoor scene dataset, we aim to leverage the shared knowledge across tasks and improve the model's generalization capabilities.
CONTROLS: A standard DeepDepth model trained from scratch on the indoor scene dataset, and a model that uses transfer learning from a pre-trained focal stack network but is not fine-tuned on the indoor scene dataset.
COST: 20000
PREDICTION: Transfer learning significantly improves the performance of depth estimation on indoor scenes, especially for small-scale datasets, but might lead to overfitting to the pre-trained model's specialization in general scenarios, requiring careful fine-tuning to adapt to the diverse indoor scene structures.

TITLE: Multi-Task Learning for Simultaneous Depth and Focus Estimation
PROPOSAL: We explore the benefits of multi-task learning by extending the focal stack estimation model to simultaneously predict not only depth but also focus maps. TITLE: Hybrid Focus Measure for Depth-from-Focus Estimation
PROPOSAL: We propose a hybrid focus measure that combines traditional frequency-domain-based measures (such as Laplacian-based or frequency-domain contrast and sharpness operators) with a deep-learning based approach. This hybrid measure leverages the strengths of both worlds: the robustness of traditional measures to hallucinated features and the ability of deep networks to learn complex patterns from data.
CONTROLS: A standard DeepDepth model without the proposed hybrid focus measure, and the same architecture but with a traditional focus measure.
COST: 35000
PREDICTION: The hybrid focus measure improves the accuracy and robustness of depth-from-focus estimation, especially in cases with ambiguous focus responses, fine textures, or abrupt depth changes, but might require careful tuning to balance the contributions of the traditional and deep-learning components.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Indoor Scene Depth Estimation
PROPOSAL: We investigate the effectiveness of transfer learning in adapting focal stack-based depth estimation models from general scenarios to indoor scenes, where depth estimation is particularly challenging due to the complexity of the scene structure and the limited depth cues available. By using a pre-trained focal stack network and fine-tuning it on the indoor scene dataset, we aim to leverage the shared knowledge across tasks and improve the model's generalization capabilities.
CONTROLS: A standard DeepDepth model trained from scratch on the indoor scene dataset, and a model that uses transfer learning from a pre-trained focal stack network but is not fine-tuned on the indoor scene dataset.

ACTION: ADD

PROPOSAL: We explore the benefits of multi-task learning by extending the focal stack estimation model to simultaneously predict not only depth but also focus maps. PREDICTION: The multi-task learning approach outperforms the baseline and standalone focus estimation model, producing more accurate and robust depth and focus estimates, especially in scenes with limited depth cues and ambiguous focus responses, but might require careful tuning of the task weights to balance the contributions of the two tasks.

CONTROLS: A standard DeepDepth model without the proposed models, and state-of-the-art methods for depth estimation from focal stacks.
COST: 180000
PREDICTION: The real-world evaluation demonstrates the robustness and generalizability of the proposed models, outperforming state-of-the-art methods on large-scale datasets, but might reveal limitations in edge cases or failure scenarios, requiring further investigation and adaptation techniques.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effects of Token Similarity on Expert Routing in DiT-MoE
PROPOSAL: We will explore the hypothesis that sparse routing, where experts are only activated by similar tokens, benefits expert specialization in DiTs. We modify token-choice routing in DiT-MoE to reward expert-base similarity between pairs of tokens by introducing a small penalty in the masking loss when tokens assigned to the same expert exhibit different image segments or features. We use the D cervelle-diffusion dataset and/topic-image ICLR'21 benchmarks and compare the original DiT-MoE with our modified variant, reporting FID and IS scores and visual quality metrics.
CONTROLS: We will compare our variant to the original DiT-MoE and a control group of non-sparse routing, without the image-segmentation penalty in the masking loss, to investigate the effect of feature similarity on routing dispersion.
COST: 40200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Assuming sparse routing benefits expert specialization, our variant should lead to improved FID and IS scores over the original DiT-MoE, but its degree of improvement may depend heavily on the dataset characteristics and model architecture. Improved results could fail to generalize to other datasets or fail to upscale with more experts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing Visual Token Properties for Expert Routing in DiTs
PROPOSAL: We propose an empirical study focusing on the characteristics of visual tokens produced by DiTs that potentially influence expert routing, such as token-to-token spatial proximity, feature co-activation patterns, and hierarchical relationships among tokens. Utilizing both diffusion-based and clustering-based representations of tokens, we and use them to inform and validate routing heuristics that target these properties, with the aim of rationalizing the router's decision-making process.
CONTROLS: As part of our study, we plan to examine the conventional routing in DiT-MoE as a baseline, ensuring that any proposed routing heuristics perform at least as well in this setup.
COST: 107000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We hypothesize that tokens in proximity, sharing common features, or parts of the same hierarchical structure may benefit from being routed to the same expert, resulting in improved generation quality and reduced routing dispersion. However, our results might not hold when tokens exhibit complex spatial relationships, varying levels of co-activation, or represent large hierarchical domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multiscale Expert Routing in Diffusion Transformers
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel MoE modification for diffusion transformers that incorporates multiscale routing, which leverages feature maps of varying resolutions to determine which experts are activated for each token. By combining hierarchical routing decisions, our multiscale approach enables the model to select experts based on both local and global patterns, potentially leading to improved generation quality.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of our multiscale MoE setting with existing DiT-MoE variants, assessing its impact on FID and IS scores, as well as visual quality metrics for image-to-text synthesis tasks.
COST: 230400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Multiscale routing may significantly enhance routing efficiency and enable expert specialization, potentially leading to improved performance in image-to-text synthesis tasks. However, it is uncertain whether the added complexity of multiscale routing will introduce bottlenecks during model training, potentially hindering its overall effectiveness.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating Expert Routing in DiTs: Token Embedding Space Analysis
PROPOSAL: We propose to analyze the token embedding spaces of Diffusion Transformers to understand how they differ from language tokens, which could prevent expert specialization. Specifically, we will use the ImageNet and FFHQ datasets to train DiTs and compute the similarity between token embeddings using techniques such as cosine similarity, mutual information, and clustering analysis. We will also visualize the token embedding spaces to identify clusters or patterns that may indicate non-specialization.
CONTROLS: We will compare our findings with the embedding spaces of U-Net-based diffusion models and language models to identify differences.
COST: 158.4
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the token embedding spaces of DiTs are more continuous and dense than those of language models, which could explain why expert specialization is harder to achieve in DiTs. This analysis may also reveal potential weaknesses in current routing schemes and suggest new design principles for expert routing in DiTs. However, if the token embedding spaces turn out to be highly structured, it could also indicate that current models are already close to achieving specialization, making it harder to improve.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Evaluating MoE Routing Strategies for DiTs
PROPOSAL: We propose to systematically evaluate different MoE routing strategies for DiTs, including token-choice, expert-choice, and batch-level global token-distribution schemes, as well as their variants. We will use these strategies to train DiT-MoE models on the ImageNet dataset and compare their performance with dense DiT models, EC-DiT, and DiffMoE. We will also investigate the effect of different routing schemes on expert specialization and model capacity.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of different MoE routing strategies with each other and with dense DiT models. We will also analyze the specialization of experts in each MoE model and investigate the effect of routing schemes on model capacity.
COST: 292.5
PREDICTION: We expect to find that the token-choice routing scheme performs better than the expert-choice and batch-level global token-distribution schemes, and that expertise specialization increases with more efficient routing schemes. However, if high-performing routing schemes fail to deliver specialization, it could indicate a limitation of the MoE paradigm in DiTs.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating Task-Dependent Tokens: Properties and Expert Specialization
PROPOSAL: We will compare the properties of visual tokens (image patches) and language tokens in text-to-image diffusion models to understand their distinctness and implications for expert specialization. Specifically, using the IPB-1M dataset and the DAN dataset, we will analyze the distributions of visual tokens in different regions of the image, the relationship between tokens at varied spatial locations, and the impact of image content (category, style, etc.) on token distributions. We will then provide a theoretical analysis of a token similarity metric underpinning different token comparison methods, exploring cases where the distance-based vs. learning-based similarity measures give different results and how such discrepancies affect expert assignment and specialization.
CONTROLS: Analyze the same token distributions using a more straightforward visual clustering approach, to set a lower bound for specialization characteristics; use spatial or spectral features as input to MoE to test the then-prevalent representations as a baseline for better expert specialization.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Our results will demonstrate two types of token similarities: metric-compliant (g vs. e) and inconsistent (g not-e), sampling patches' projecting gradients with the full central fixpt and out-of-distribution biasing brackets recorded one per step, that assign single-task functionality (style or a region only outputs); once validated, using proposed heuristics to train and perform analysis on Diffusion Transformer models, will show moderate jumps for token-level object differentiation through lab demonstration achieving specialization energies.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Token Embedding Attention for Routing
PROPOSAL: Given that task-dependent tokens exhibit varying degrees of similarity, we will devise an attention-based routing method that learns to adaptively aggregate the hidden states of visual tokens to generate a set of representative embedding vectors, each of which can be used to query a set of experts for generating the corresponding image patch. This routing method will utilize attention to assign different weights to the hidden states of individual tokens, focusing on more critical patches and gradually discarding less informative tokens. In this study, we will investigate this new MoE routing method on DALL-E 2 [126 million parameters] and the FFHQ dataset and will compare it with token-choice routing methods (DiT-MoE) and a traditional global token distribution approach (DiffMoE) on image synthesis tasks.
CONTROLS: Conduct an ablation study to compare the impact of using separate weights for each token, using a simple mean pooling to reduce the dimensionality of token embeddings, and a different set of parameters for each scaling factor in order to determine which factors impede best the DiffMoE approach's robustness
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: We anticipate that the attention-based routing method will outperform traditional routing methods by 10% in terms of image synthesis quality, while reducing the computational overhead by 20%, further augmenting efficiency (where learning wouldn't deliver).

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Expert Design with Node Ranking and Seed Initialization: Counter-Over-Specialization
PROPOSAL: We will revisit our Expert Design with Node Ranking and Seed Initialization method and address the issue of over-specialization, where experts become too focused on a narrow aspect of the image, resulting in limited scalability and poor performance on more complex tasks. To mitigate this, we propose a counter-overspecialization mechanism that dynamically adjusts the seeding and ranking strategies based on the evolving image structure and the expert's performance on a variety of tasks. We will evaluate this revised method on a range of images, including those with diverse textures, objects, and backgrounds, and compare its performance with both the baseline Expert Design method and other counter-overspecialization techniques.
CONTROLS: Assess the effectiveness of different seeding strategies, such as random seeding, clustering seeding, and hierarchical seeding, and examine the impact of different ranking methods, such as greedy ranking and recursive ranking, on the performance and scalability of the Expert Design method.
COST: 27000
PREDICTION: Our revised Expert Design method, combined with the counter-overspecialization mechanism, will demonstrate improved scalability and performance on a wider range of images and tasks, particularly in scenarios where the image structure is highly complex and the experts need to adapt quickly and efficiently.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: MoE Sub-Network Pruning for Efficient Expert Networks
PROPOSAL: To further improve the efficiency of MoE networks, we will propose a sub-network pruning strategy that selectively removes unnecessary expert connections, leading to significant reductions in computational costs and memory requirements. By identifying and pruning redundant experts, we will create a more streamlined MoE architecture that maintains its performance while being more efficiently utilized in real-world applications. We will experimentally evaluate this pruning strategy on various diffusive transformers with reduced FFH datasets and compare its performance with other pruning techniques.
CONTROLS: Investigate the impact of different pruning rates, pruning methods (tensor-wise vs. component-wise), and pruning metrics (accuracy, FLOPs, memory usage) on the performance and efficiency of the MoE network.
COST: 36900
PREDICTION: Our proposed MoE sub-network pruning strategy will be successful in optimizing the efficiency of MoE networks, reducing computational costs by up to 30% while maintaining performance, and enabling the widespread adoption of MoE architectures in real-world applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Role of Expert Pool Size on MoE's Effectiveness in Diffusion Transformers
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a comprehensive study to investigate how the number of experts in an MoE architecture affects its performance on various text-to-image tasks using diffusion transformers. We will systematically vary the number of experts and explore how it impacts the model's competition for tokens and the diversity of output. We will evaluate the models on the COCO dataset and measure their performance using metrics such as FID score and Inception Score. Additionally, we will perform ablation studies to understand the effects of varying expert pool sizes on MoE's behavior and identify optimal values for different tasks and architectures. We will also document the effects on computational resources and memory usage as a function of the number of experts.
CONTROLS: We will include baseline models (e.g., dense DiT, tokenized DiT) and study several cases of expert pool crowd including large, small and median models
COST: 2512
PREDICTION: We expect to find a trade-off between the number of experts and the model's performance, with a larger number of experts leading to improved diversity but also increased computational overhead, and a smaller number of experts resulting in reduced diversity but also faster training times.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of MoE on Diffusion Transformer's Generalization and Robustness
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate how MoE architectures, specifically DiT-MoE and EC-DiT, impact the generalization and robustness of diffusion transformers on various text-to-image tasks. We will test the models on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution datasets, such as COCO, LINDART-V2, and AnimeFace, and measure their performance using metrics such as FID score, Inception Score, and robustness to adversarial attacks. We will also investigate how the MoE layers affect the model's generalization and robustness, and explore the effects of varying the number of experts, expert capacity, and routing strategy on these properties. Additionally, we will compare the MoE models with dense diffusion transformers and explore their differences in terms of generalization and robustness.
CONTROLS: We will include baseline models (e.g., dense DiT, tokenized DiT) and study several cases of expert pool crowd including large, small and median models
COST: 3060
PREDICTION: We expect to find that MoE architectures lead to improved generalization and robustness on certain tasks, but may also introduce vulnerabilities to adversarial attacks, and that the benefits of MoE are heavily dependent on the task and dataset.
