ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Audiovisual Emotion Hallucinations with Explainable Inference
PROPOSAL: Develop and evaluate a modified version of the FLAME (Facial Landmark Attention for Multimodal Emotion) model [1], adding an attentional tracing mechanism to track the influence of each input modality on the model's emotion prediction. This can help investigate whether FLAME ties emotions to the audiovisual cues that actually explain them rather than to irrelevant cues. We will use the IEMOCAP dataset [2], a widely used multimodal emotion recognition benchmark, and evaluate the model using metrics such as explanation quality, Hallucination Rate, and F1-score. We will also compare FLAME with the original model and three baseline models (ResNet-18, VGG16, and a simple Multimodal Fusion model) to assess the effectiveness of the tracing mechanism.
CONTROLS: FLAME without tracing, ResNet-18, VGG16, and a simple Multimodal Fusion model.
COST: 12,000
PREDICTION: The tracing mechanism will significantly reduce the hallucination rate and improve explanation quality, outperforming the baseline models and the original FLAME model.

[1] Mou, Z., & Martín, A. B. (2022). FLAME: Facial Landmark Attention for Multimodal Emotion Recognition. IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing, 13(2), 1031–1043.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Audiovisual Emotion Reasoning Benchmark with Hallucination Detection (AERBH)
PROPOSAL: Create a new benchmark, AERBH, by extending the existing movieGUIDE and DiCE datasets [1] with emotion-specific reasoning and detection tasks that target the two critical bottlenecks (reasoning errors and perception errors) of audiovisual emotion hallucinations. We will evaluate models on their ability to explain emotions accurately and to detect hallucinations in addition to predicting emotions. The benchmark will be designed as a multimodal, multi-task dataset with various audiovisual scene categories and annotated emotional cues. We will use metrics such as BLEU score, Rouge-L score, and Hallucination Detection Accuracy to assess model performance.
CONTROLS: Models with a similar architecture to the one proposed in paper 'Systematic Generalization in Pre-trained Vision-and-Language Models' [2], such as CLIP (ViT-B/32) [3], will be used as baseline models.
COST: 30,000
PREDICTION: AERBH will provide a comprehensive and realistic assessment of audiovisual hallucination performance, helping to identify the strengths and weaknesses of existing models and guiding further research towards more reliable and interpretable emotion understanding systems.

[1] Ye, J., Peng, H., & Tian, Y. (2020). DiCE: Movie Emotional CLIps for Emotion Understanding and Detection. In Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reducing Emotion Hallucinations with Adversarial Losses and Temporal Consistency
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel training objective that combines two types of adversarial losses with a temporal consistency regularization term. The first adversarial loss encourages the model to avoid hallucinating emotional cues by adding artificial noise to the input and training models to ignore it while preserving the correct emotion. The second loss enforces the model to generate more realistic and temporally consistent emotion predictions. The temporal consistency regularization term is used to fine-tune models on subsets of the data with consistent emotions, and evaluate models on a new validation subset, assessing the overfitting on the entire dataset. We will evaluate the performance of this approach on the AERBH benchmark and compare it with the standard multimodal fusion approach.
CONTROLS: Baselines will include a standard multimodal fusion model and a model trained with temporal consistency loss only.
COST: 20,000
PREDICTION: The proposed training objective will significantly reduce emotion hallucinations and improve the temporal consistency of emotion predictions, achieving higher performance on the AERBH benchmark compared to the standard multimodal fusion approach.

Note: This proposal will be trained on the AERBH benchmark, which will be created in proposal 2.

PROPOSAL: Develop a novel training objective that combines two types of adversarial losses with a temporal consistency regularization term. The first adversarial loss encourages the model to avoid hallucinating emotional cues by adding artificial noise to the input and training models to ignore it while preserving the correct emotion. The second loss enforces the model to generate more realistic and temporally consistent emotion predictions. The temporal consistency regularization term is used to fine-tune models on subsets of the data with consistent emotions, and evaluate models on a new validation subset, assessing the overfitting on the entire dataset. We will evaluate the performance of this approach on the AERBH benchmark and compare it with the standard multimodal fusion approach.
CONTROLS: Baselines will include a standard multimodal fusion model and a model trained with temporal consistency loss only.
COST: 180,000
PREDICTION: The proposed training objective will significantly reduce emotion hallucinations and improve the temporal consistency of emotion predictions, achieving higher performance on the AERBH benchmark compared to the standard multimodal fusion approach.

Note: This proposal will be trained on the AERBH benchmark, which will be created in proposal 2.

PROPOSAL: Develop a robustness evaluation framework to assess the impact of adversarial attacks on the AERBH benchmark. We will also assess the robustness of the model by employing a range of attack scenarios, including white-box and black-box methods, and evaluating the impact of different levels of noise on the input modalities.

PREDICTION: The proposed robustness evaluation framework will highlight the vulnerability of existing models to adversarial attacks, providing valuable insights for future research directions and revealing the need for developing more robust audiovisual emotion understanding systems.

TITLE: Evaluating Emotion Hallucination Correction Methods for Multimodal Emotion Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate and compare various methods for correcting hallucinations in multimodal emotion models. We will develop and evaluate three types of correction mechanisms: recycling the correct information from a hallucinated model, using an auxiliary model to identify and correct hallucinations, and integrating a global consistency loss to encourage the hallucinated model to produce more coherent predictions. We will evaluate these mechanisms on the AERBH benchmark and compare their performance with that of the models proposed in this set.
CONTROLS: Baseline models will be the same as those proposed in the set.
COST: 105,000
PREDICTION: The proposed correction mechanisms will provide valuable tools for mitigating hallucinations in multimodal emotion models, enabling more accurate and reliable predictions.

TITLE: Evaluating Audiovisual Emotion Hallucinations with Explainable Inference
PROPOSAL: Develop and evaluate a modified version of the FLAME (Facial Landmark Attention for Multimodal Emotion) model [1], adding an attentional tracing mechanism to track the influence of each input modality on the model's emotion prediction. This can help investigate whether FLAME ties emotions to the audiovisual cues that actually explain them rather than to irrelevant cues. We will use the IEMOCAP dataset [2], a widely used multimodal emotion recognition benchmark, and evaluate the model using metrics such as explanation quality, Hallucination Rate, and F1-score. We will also compare FLAME with the original model and three baseline models (ResNet-18, VGG16, and a simple Multimodal Fusion model) to assess the effectiveness of the tracing mechanism.
CONTROLS: FLAME without tracing, ResNet-18, VGG16, and a simple Multimodal Fusion model.
COST: 36,000
PREDICTION: The tracing mechanism will significantly reduce the hallucination rate and improve explanation quality, outperforming the baseline models and the original FLAME model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Audiovisual Emotion Reasoning Benchmark with Hallucination Detection (AERBH)
PROPOSAL: Create a new benchmark, AERBH, by extending the existing movieGUIDE and DiCE datasets [1] with emotion-specific reasoning and detection tasks that target the two critical bottlenecks (reasoning errors and perception errors) of audiovisual emotion hallucinations. We will evaluate models on their ability to explain emotions accurately and to detect hallucinations in addition to predicting emotions. The benchmark will be designed as a multimodal, multi-task dataset with various audiovisual scene categories and annotated emotional cues. We will use metrics such as BLEU score, Rouge-L score, and Hallucination Detection Accuracy to assess model performance.
CONTROLS: Models with a similar architecture to the one proposed in paper 'Systematic Generalization in Pre-trained Vision-and-Language Models' [2], such as CLIP (ViT-B/32) [3], will be used as baseline models.
COST: 90,000
PREDICTION: AERBH will provide a comprehensive and realistic assessment of audiovisual hallucination performance, helping to identify the strengths and weaknesses of existing models and guiding further research towards more reliable and interpretable emotion understanding systems.

[1] Ye, J., Peng, H., & Tian, Y. (2020). DiCE: Movie Emotional CLIps for Emotion Understanding and Detection. In Proceedings of the IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.

TITLE: Revising Reducing Emotion Hallucinations with Adversarial Losses and Temporal Consistency

TITLE: Sub-Goal Consistency in Audiovisual Emotion Reasoning: A Domain Adaptation Approach
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the impact of sub-goal inconsistency on the performance of audiovisual emotion reasoning MLLMs. Introduce a domain adaptation approach that mitigates sub-goal inconsistency by aligning the learned sub-goals with the target task. Train and test the adapted model on the RECOLA-E dataset and a sub-set of the SMAugmentedVRD dataset. Assess the effects of sub-goal inconsistency on the hallucination rates and accuracy of emotion-related keyword prediction.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline results from a MLLM with sub-goal inconsistency disabled
- Comparison to the prior proposal  Emotion-Conditioned Loss Functions for Auto-Normalizing Audiovisual Emotion Models
- Investigation of the role of the target task in aligning sub-goals using multiple target tasks 
COST:  210 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The adapted model should outperform the baseline model by a moderate margin in terms of sub-goal consistency and hallucination rates, with potential for a decrease in emotional cue accuracy. However, it might struggle with scenarios involving context-rich emotional cues that can't certainly serve multiple discriminative functions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Outcome-Aware Rollout Grouping for Efficient Agentic Search Rewarding
PROPOSAL: Modify the GRPO algorithm to group rollouts based on their final answer outcomes rather than their individual turns, thereby ensuring that groups are diverse and avoid the omission of learning signal when all rollouts yield identical answers. Each rollout is assigned a weight based on its outcome similarity to the rest of the group, generating a weighted rollout-based reward that aims to impede advantage collapse and provide fine-grained supervision.
CONTROLS: Compare this method against vanilla GRPO, a simple implementation without group-based weighting, and a random grouping strategy on challenging multi-hop QA datasets.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Weighted rollout-based rewards result in slightly better performance and higher sample efficiency, demonstrating robustness against advantage collapse; however, further regularization techniques, such as group-level value estimation, may be necessary to reduce variance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Search- Trajectory Alignment via Intermediate Turn Embeddings (STAE)
PROPOSAL: Introduce a learnable intermediate turn embedding module within the agentic search model, creating a dense and informative reward signal by assigning each interaction turn a scalar value that reflects the product of turn embeddings and outcome embeddings. This allows for fine-grained credit assignment and encourages coordination between early and late reasoning steps.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed STAE method to vanilla GRPO, and also to an ablation variant where only the outcome embeddings are taken into account, using WebSearch-40, a large-scale open-domain question answering dataset.
COST: 500 
PREDICTION: STAE outperforms vanilla GRPO by a noticeable margin, delivering improved robustness to advantage collapse and better sample efficiency, especially on hard queries; potential for failure lies in cases of limited embedding capabilities, which may hinder the model's capacity to distinguish impactful turns efficiently.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward-Augmented Intermediate Turn Feedback (RAITF)
PROPOSAL: Introduce an auxiliary neural module that generates a turn-level reward signal based on the predicted likelihood of requiring corrections at the next turn given the current state, intervening on the reward-hacking issue and encouraging coherent interim queries. This module captures a notion of reliability, turning the original outcome-based reward signal into a more informative one that flags unsound reasoning early on.
CONTROLS: Evaluate RAITF relative to both vanilla GRPO and the STAE method on complex multi-hop question answering benchmarks like MultiSNLI, focusing on the improvement in correcting suboptimal search trajectories.
COST: 600 
PREDICTION: RAITF proves capable of capturing iterative steps and discerning errant reasoning, redirecting agent exploration towards reliable paths; while the auxiliary module increases overall ML paradigm requirements, it shows potential to fill in gaps left by the primary outcome-based rewards.

PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of return-based sampling on the efficiency and effectiveness of agentic search agents by introducing alternative sampling methods into the evaluation framework. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Return-Based Sampling Strategies for Agentic Search
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of return-based sampling on the efficiency and effectiveness of agentic search agents by introducing alternative sampling methods into the evaluation framework. This includes Monte Carlo sampling with various exploration-exploitation trade-off parameters and upper-confidence bound-based sampling for strategic exploration, all aiming to better guide search trajectories towards optimal solutions.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed methods against vanilla online rollouts and degree-based sampling on a range of challenging multi-hop question answering datasets, focusing on improvements in sample efficiency, search trajectory quality, and overall task performance.
COST: 2800 
PREDICTION: Find that adaptive sampling strategies improve the efficiency and effectiveness of search agents, particularly on longer trajectories, while the key challenge would be avoiding over-exploration to facilitate adoption in real-world applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Counterfactual Turn-Level Reasoning for Agentic Search
PROPOSAL: Develop a counterfactual reasoning framework that compares the performance of the agent on each turn to what would have happened if an alternative action had been taken. This would enable the agent to refine its decision-making process and provide more informative feedback about the relative value of different actions in achieving the final goal.
CONTROLS: Evaluate this approach in comparison to traditional reinforcement learning methods on a range of complex question answering datasets, focusing on improvements in task performance and accuracy of turn-level reasoning.
COST: 3200 
PREDICTION: Find that counterfactual reasoning leads to more informed decision-making and better task performance for the agentic search agent, while the challenge lies in learning robust counterfactual representations that capture the complex relationships between turns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Outcome-xAA Reward Normalization
PROPOSAL: We modify Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a new objective that combines outcome-based rewards with an average outcome feature. This average outcome feature is computed as the mean outcome among all rollouts within a group. Rewards are then normalized across the group and between these two signals, both following the standard process in GRPO. We believe that this approach blends beneficial signaling from both outcomes and hop-by-hop intermediate.turns to make advantages more interpretable and robust within groups.
CONTROLS: Baseline: GRPO; controlled version with only outcome-based rewards and a modified version without any group relative signal.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Outcome-xAA Reward Normalization is likely to perform better than GRPO on harder multi-hop questions and provide more robust learning signals during agent training, but may still struggle with learning from extremely uniform rollouts where gradient signals are very weak.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Value- Alex Process Reward (V-AP)
PROPOSAL: We extend current group-based process rewards with a novel intrinsic process reward mechanism. Value-Alex Process Reward (V-AP) calculates a hop-by-hop evaluation by squaring the probability of the correct retrieved information for each turn relative to the ground-truth answer. These values are then shifted by a learned bias term per step. Optimizing V-AP not only learn more information about intermediate steps but also encourages gradual improvements by reducing the impact of "comfortably" correct intermediate outcomes with insignificant final additions.
CONTROLS: Baseline: GRPO; ablation study to identify the effect of using the learned bias term; comparison with a process reward approach that relies on Monte Carlo simulation.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: V-AP is expected to significantly outperform GRPO on both accuracy and sample efficiency, as the process reward helps agents that avoid all learning from uniform final turns to fall behind solely based on intermediate turns, before, answering turns identifies encounters that-good†来的ETwitter,

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Improved Value-Alex Process Reward (V-AP)
PROPOSAL: We extend our previous Value-Alex Process Reward (V-AP) mechanism with an edited formulation. Instead of using the probability of the correct information, we calculate the harmonic mean of the recall and precision at the current turn, taking into account the relevance of the retrieved information based on learned feature importance. This aligns with the natural strategy of search-based agents, focusing both on retrieving relevant and accurate information, while placing less importance on turns with poor performance.
CONTROLS: Baseline: GRPO; ablation study to identify the effect of using feature importance in retrieved group weights.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: Improved V-AP is likely to outperform GRPO on challenging tasks and improve generalization across various domains, but might be sensitive to the quality of the retrieval mechanism and the learned feature importance weights.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Local Unified Efficient Agentic Search (LUES)
PROPOSAL: We introduce Local Unified Efficient Agentic Search (LUES), a novel framework that combines agent and search components with a learned state and action space that is tailored to the task at hand. LUES learns a compact representation of the agent's expected trajectory and continuously refines it based on newly acquired information from tool interactions. This local optimization enhances intermediate reasoning and feedback mechanisms, especially in the face of sparse outcome rewards and variability. LUES is seen as a pre-processing method that improves the robustness of the agents by optimizing the capacity for aggregation.
CONTROLS: Baseline: GRPO; controlled experiment to evaluate the effect of LUES on different types of queries and agent architectures.
COST: 1600
PREDICTION: LUES is expected to significantly improve the robustness of search-based agents, especially on complex multi-hop queries, and allow them to operate effectively even when the final outcome is uncertain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Episode-Level Training (EET) and Meta-Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose Efficient Episode-Level Training (EET) and meta-learning methods that adjust the learning rate of the agent based on the performance of previous episodes and the difficulty of the current episode. EET uses an index of episode difficulty derived from the model's past performance and assigns a time-dependent learning rate to fit the progress towards the optimal solution for search-based problems. Additionally, we implement meta-learning to quickly adapt existing performance to new tasks.
CONTROLS: Baseline: GRPO; ablation study to evaluate the effect of EET on different types of queries and agent architectures compared to meta-learning.
COST: 2200
PREDICTION: EET and meta-learning are expected to greatly improve the sample efficiency of search-based agents and enable them to adapt more quickly to challenging multi-hop queries, but its success could be highly dependent on carefully designing the episode difficulty index and the adaptation scheme.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning to Weight Interactions (LWI)
PROPOSAL: We introduce Learning to Weight Interactions (LWI), a novel algorithm that learns an optimal weighting scheme for combining intermediate reasoning and tool interactions in multi-hop search. LWI rewards the agent for focusing on the most informative steps and penalizing redundant or uninformative interactions. This approach enables the agent to better allocate its exploration and exploitation efforts and leads to improved performance.
CONTROLS: Baseline: GRPO; ablation study to evaluate the effect of LWI on different types of queries and agent architectures.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: LWI is expected to significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of search-based agents by focusing on the most relevant steps and reducing redundant interactions. However, it requires a large number of interactions to learn the optimal weighting scheme, potentially making it less robust to noisy or changing environments.

TITLE: Multi-Agent Co-Training for Agentic Search (MACS)
PROPOSAL: We propose a Multi-Agent Co-Training framework for agentic search that involves training multiple agents with different architectures and reward structures in a co-training setup. The agents learn from each other's strengths and weaknesses, improving their overall performance on a diverse set of tasks. MACS enables the agents to learn a more comprehensive understanding of the search space and the relationships between different steps in the search process.
CONTROLS: Baseline: GRPO; ablation study to evaluate the effect of MACS on different types of queries and agent architectures.

PREDICTION: MACS is expected to lead to significant improvements in the performance and robustness of search-based agents by leveraging the strengths of multiple agents and enabling them to learn from each other. However, the scalability of MACS may be challenging due to the increased computational requirements of training multiple agents.

TITLE: Enhancing GRPO with a Gradient of Turn-level Losses
PROPOSAL: We extend Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to incorporate a gradient of turn-level losses, defining a reward function that combines group-relative outcome rewards with turn-level Supervised Learning for the reuse of the agent's output from one or more previous turns. The advantage of the agent's current action given the context from prior turns is aimed to be corrected by targeting the distinct influences in achieving the ground truth.
CONTROLS: Baseline experiments on GRPO performance with and without turn-level reward, each tested via multi-turn agentic query tasks from WebQuestion and MultiTransvqa, with the official fine-grained metrics SAP-QE and MALB-R (train/val. sets 50 samples each).
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Promising improvements in accurately evaluating intermediate reasoning with a model capable of corrigibility and informative turns, possible, but losses tend to be biased to consist critically irreducible turns - causing schedule consequences over policy optimization; reward planning complexity increase; core performance delineating.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning Contextualized Reward Functions via Hierarchical Relevance Modeling
PROPOSAL: To provide turn-level supervision while remaining robust to reward hacking and sensitive to the final objective, we propose leveraging hierarchical relevance modeling to dynamically learn contextualized reward functions for each turn. This approach involves learning two hierarchical relevance models: one for relevance between tool interactions and the final answer, and another for relevance between successive tool interactions. Using these models, we estimate the per-turn contribution of each action toward achieving the final objective and use these estimates to compute a turn-level reward signal.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to using a static reward function (e.g. a weighted sum of similarity and success metrics) and a version of our method where the two relevance models are learned separately to control for the effect of the hierarchical modeling.
COST: 36000
PREDICTION: This approach will yield a more informative reward signal and improve policy learning, but its high computational cost may limit its applicability to large-scale search agent training.

TITLE: Auto-Generated Intermediate Rewards via Sentence Embeddings
PROPOSAL: Inspired by recent work on learning to predict sentence embeddings for downstream tasks, we propose to leverage pre-trained language models to predict embeddings for tool interactions (e.g. search queries or web retrievals) during training. These embeddings are then compared against reference embeddings (ground-truth answer embeddings) using a cosine similarity threshold. However, to improve robustness to noisy or misleading tool interactions, we now modify this approach to also incorporate an uncertainty score for each embedding prediction, which is computed using kernel uncertainty estimation. This uncertainty score is then used to down-weight the contribution of uncertain tool interactions to the similarity-based reward signal.
CONTROLS: We compare our modified approach to the baseline of using outcome-only rewards and the original version without uncertainty estimation to control for the effect of the embedding predictions and the uncertainty scoring.
COST: 21600
PREDICTION: This revised approach will help reduce the impact of noisy tool interactions on the reward signal and improve policy learning, but it may still struggle to capture complex relationships between tool interactions and the final answer.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Agent Negotiation with Tool Interactions to Reduce Reward Sparsity
PROPOSAL: To reduce reward sparsity and encourage more informative tool interactions, we propose to leverage a multi-agent negotiation framework, where several independent agents communicate and negotiate the information to be retrieved through tool interactions. Each agent contributes its own "source" information to the negotiation, and through iterative negotiation, they converge on a final set of queries that is more diverse and informative. We use an MCTS-based solution to efficiently select and execute the final set of queries and to compute a multi-agents-based reward for the initial set of questions.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to individual agents using outcome-only rewards, and to a baseline where all queries are used.
COST: 72000
PREDICTION: This approach will significantly improve sample efficiency and exploration in agentic search, but it may be sensitive to the hyperparameters of the negotiation and the MCTS algorithm.

PROPOSAL: To address the issue of advantage collapse and reward sparsity, we propose to integrate a weak supervision component that actively revises queries based on intermediate predictions and outputs. By using weak supervision signals, such as relevance and novelty indicators, the agent can iteratively refine its queries, exploring new possibilities while avoiding repetitions. This approach encourages exploration, reduces the likelihood of advantage collapse, and provides an additional channel of feedback for the agent.

TITLE: Active Query Revision via Weak Supervision to Reduce Advantage Collapse
PROPOSAL: To address the issue of advantage collapse and reward sparsity, we propose to integrate a weak supervision component that actively revises queries based on intermediate predictions and outputs. By using weak supervision signals, such as relevance and novelty indicators, the agent can iteratively refine its queries, exploring new possibilities while avoiding repetitions. This approach encourages exploration, reduces the likelihood of advantage collapse, and provides an additional channel of feedback for the agent.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to individual agents using outcome-only rewards, our previous approach refined with value refinement and additional layer-based MCTS-hierarchical multi-agent setup, and a baseline where all queries are used.
COST: 2190000
PREDICTION: This approach will significantly improve exploration, reduce advantage collapse, and enhance overall policy learning, but it may be sensitive to the hyperparameters of the weak supervision module and require fine-tuning to achieve optimal results.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Learning Contextualized Reward Functions via Hierarchical Relevance Modeling
PROPOSAL: To provide a more robust and informative reward signal, we propose to extend the hierarchical relevance modeling approach by incorporating a meta-reward learning component. This involves learning a higher-level reward function that takes the output of the hierarchical relevance models as input and provides a contextualized reward signal that reflects the agent's progress towards the goal. By doing so, we can capture more nuanced relationships between tool interactions and the final objective, leading to improved policy learning and reduced advantage collapse.
CONTROLS: We compare our revised approach to the original version without meta-reward learning, individual agents using outcome-only rewards, and a baseline where all queries are used.
COST: 288000
PREDICTION: This revised approach will significantly improve policy learning, reduce advantage collapse, and enhance overall performance, but it may require careful design of the meta-reward function to avoid overfitting and ensure stability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Agentic Search with Reusable Reward Functions
PROPOSAL: To facilitate knowledge sharing and facilitate transfer learning across agentic search domains, we propose to utilize reusable reward functions. This involves learning a reward function that is domain-agnostic and can be transferred across different search domains. By doing so, we can reduce the need for extensive retraining and adapt quickly to new environments. We also explore fine-tuning this reward function using domain-specific knowledge to further improve performance.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to individual agents using outcome-only rewards, our previous approaches, and a baseline where all queries are used.
COST: 405000
PREDICTION: This approach will significantly improve efficiency, facilitate knowledge sharing, and reduce the need for extensive retraining, but it may be challenging to design a reward function that is domain-agnostic and transferable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Auto-Generated Intermediate Rewards via Sentence Embeddings
PROPOSAL: Inspired by recent work on learning to predict sentence embeddings for downstream tasks, we propose to leverage pre-trained language models to predict embeddings for tool interactions (e.g. search queries or web retrievals) during training. These embeddings are then compared against reference embeddings (ground-truth answer embeddings) using a cosine similarity threshold. If the similarity exceeds the threshold, the interaction is marked as successful and receives a reward. We apply this approach at each turn, generating dense rewards that can inform RL training without requiring additional annotations or oracle knowledge.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to the baseline of using outcome-only rewards and a version of our method without the threshold-based similarity comparison to control for the effect of the embedding predictions.
COST: 54000.helper(NOT 5400)
PREDICTION: This approach will help improve sample efficiency and correct advantage collapse, but it may struggle to distinguish productive turns when similar queries yield similar but incorrect answers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning Contextualized Reward Functions via Hierarchical Relevance Modeling
PROPOSAL: To provide turn-level supervision while remaining robust to reward hacking and sensitive to the final objective, we propose leveraging hierarchical relevance modeling to dynamically learn contextualized reward functions for each turn. This approach involves learning two hierarchical relevance models: one for relevance between tool interactions and the final answer, and another for relevance between successive tool interactions. Using these models, we estimate the per-turn contribution of each action toward achieving the final objective and use these estimates to compute a turn-level reward signal.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to using a static reward function (e.g. a weighted sum of similarity and success metrics) and a version of our method where the two relevance models are learned separately to control for the effect of the hierarchical modeling.
COST: 108000
PREDICTION: This approach will yield a more informative reward signal and improve policy learning, but its high computational cost may limit its applicability to large-scale search agent training.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Auto-Generated Intermediate Rewards via Sentence Embeddings
PROPOSAL: Inspired by recent work on learning to predict sentence embeddings for downstream tasks, we propose to leverage pre-trained language models to predict embeddings for tool interactions (e.g. search queries or web retrievals) during training. These embeddings are then compared against reference embeddings (ground-truth answer embeddings) using a cosine similarity threshold. However, to improve robustness to noisy or misleading tool interactions, we now modify this approach to also incorporate an uncertainty score for each embedding prediction, which is computed using kernel uncertainty estimation. This uncertainty score is then used to down-weight the contribution of uncertain tool interactions to the similarity-based reward signal.
CONTROLS: We compare our modified approach to the baseline of using outcome-only rewards and the original version without uncertainty estimation to control for the effect of the embedding predictions and the uncertainty scoring.
COST: 64800
PREDICTION: This revised approach will help reduce the impact of noisy tool interactions on the reward signal and improve policy learning, but it may still struggle to capture complex relationships between tool interactions and the final answer.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Agent Negotiation with Tool Interactions to Reduce Reward Sparsity
PROPOSAL: To reduce reward sparsity and encourage more informative tool interactions, we propose to leverage a multi-agent negotiation framework, where several independent agents communicate and negotiate the information to be retrieved through tool interactions. Each agent contributes its own "source" information to the negotiation, and through iterative negotiation, they converge on a final set of queries that is more diverse and informative. We use an MCTS-based solution to efficiently select and execute the final set of queries and to compute a multi-agents-based reward for the initial set of questions.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to individual agents using outcome-only rewards, and to a baseline where all queries are used.
COST: 216000
PREDICTION: This approach will significantly improve sample efficiency and exploration in agentic search, but it may be sensitive to the hyperparameters of the negotiation and the MCTS algorithm.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Turn-Level Kullback-Leibler (KL) Divergence Reward
PROPOSAL: This proposal estimates a dense reward signal for each interaction turn by computing the KL divergence between the current state representation and the state observed after executing the current action. We will use the state representations learned by the pre-trained LLM. A higher KL divergence value rewards actions that lead to more informative or less already-explored states, providing a measure of the value of each intermediate step without relying on external judges or reward models.
CONTROLS: (1) Baseline: Using only outcome-based rewards, (2) Ablation: Using only the state observed after the action, without previous state, (3) Control: Using state representations learned by different pre-trained LLM variants
COST: 330
PREDICTION: This approach should provide a more informative reward signal than outcome-based rewards, especially in cases where every rollout in a group receives the same final answer, but it may struggle with distinguishing productive from unproductive turns if it solely relies on the informativeness of state representations.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Iterative Reward Augmentation with Predictive Meaning Representation
PROPOSAL: This approach iteratively refines a reward signal by inducing a Normalizing Flows (NF) model to transform the pre-computed state-representation vector into a Meaning Representation (MR) that implicitly captures relevant semantics. We then use the distribution over the MR space conditioned on both the current state and the ground truth answer to compute the probability of each intermediate step contributing to the final answer, providing a reward signal that increases with each successful intermediate step.
CONTROLS: (1) Baseline: Using only outcome-based rewards, (2) Ablation: Replacing NF with a simple affine transformation, (3) Control: Using different pre-trained LLM variants as the source of state representations
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: This method should capture fine-grained dependencies between intermediate steps and provide dense supervision, but may face challenges in learning flexible and informative NF transformations and may require more computational resources due to the iterative process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analytical Value Estimation using Reachability and Policy-based Transfer
PROPOSAL: This theoretical work investigates how the average return for an intermediate step can be estimated approximately, without additional training data, by utilizing the reachability of the current state to the final answer and leveraging the learned policy to project a hypothetical trajectory towards optimal performance. It aims to provide insights on the intrinsic value of individual turns, grounded on the expected multi-turn trajectory, allowing for a principled assessment of intermediate steps' contribution to the final outcome.
CONTROLS: (Non-experimental, strictly theoretical)
COST: 168
PREDICTION: This work is expected to provide foundational theoretical insights, potentially informing the development of practical reward estimation methods. It may struggle to scale to highly complex or dynamic environments.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Progressive Multi-Turn Reward Decomposition with Successor Features
PROPOSAL: This approach decomposes the multi-turn reward signal into a sequence of short-term rewards that encourage accurate progress toward the final goal, leveraging the learned successor features from intermediate steps. By computing the feature distance between the current state and the state resulting from following the policy to the next step, it assigns value to incremental progress toward the goal, providing dense supervision without relying on external judges or reward models.
CONTROLS: (1) Baseline: Using only outcome-based rewards, (2) Ablation: Removing the successor features, (3) Control: Using different sizes of sequences for reward decomposition
COST: 729.17
PREDICTION: This method should capture incremental progress and provide dense supervision, potentially improving sample efficiency. However, it may struggle with aligning short-term and long-term objectives.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Path Significance Estimation with Variational Bayesian Inference
PROPOSAL: This approach uses Variational Bayesian Inference (VBI) to estimate the path significance of intermediate steps, which is the probability of taking each step in the optimal path to the goal. It models the path significance as a distribution over the intermediate steps and uses the VB algorithm to approximate this distribution, providing a principled way to measure the importance of each step in achieving the final goal.
CONTROLS: (1) Baseline: Using only outcome-based rewards, (2) Ablation: Removing the variational Bayesian inference, (3) Control: Using different prior distributions for the path significance
COST: 832.876
PREDICTION: This method should provide a principled way to measure the importance of each step in achieving the final goal, potentially improving the effectiveness of process rewards. However, it may require more computational resources due to the VB inference.

TITLE: Evaluating and Comparing Process Rewards for Multi-Turn Search Agents
PROPOSAL: This experiment compares the proposed process rewards and analytical value estimation methods using a comprehensive evaluation framework that assesses their effectiveness on open-domain question answering and multi-hop question answering tasks. The framework evaluates key metrics such as agent performance, sample efficiency, and robustness to advantage collapse, guided by statistical significance tests and visual analysis.

PREDICTION: This experiment should provide a thorough evaluation of the proposed methods and help identify the most effective approach for process rewards in multi-turn search agents. It will also highlight the strengths and weaknesses of each method, guiding future research and development in this area.

TITLE: Augmenting Truthful-Reporter Reward Mechanism for Search Agents

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sparse Query-based Self-Supervised Pre-Training for Sparse Perception Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effectiveness of a contrastive learning based pre-training method for SPMs, leveraging the notion of "anchor-positive-negative" pairs to learn fine-grained 3D scene representations. Utilize a pre-trained image backbone to extract multi-view image features, and then projecting these features onto 3D space to generate sparse query-based representations. We hypothesize that this framework will allow SPMs to learn contextual relationships between 3D entities, even without explicit dense intermediate representations.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline of not pre-training the SPM, and ablate the pre-training component to evaluate its contribution.
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: We expect this approach to show significant gains over the baseline, particularly in tasks that benefit from 3D contextual relationships, such as 3D object detection. However, if the anchor-positive-negative pairs are not well-defined, the performance may not generalize well across different scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: RGB2Sparse: Rendering-based Pre-training for Sparse Perception Models with Query-based RGB-to-Sparse Matching
PROPOSAL: Introduce a rendering-based pre-training method that takes RGB image supervision as input and outputs sparse query-based features. Utilize a learner to predict sparse queries in 3D space, and a renderer that incorporates these predictions to generate 2D RGB images from 3D sparse features. Train RGB2Sparse using large-scale driving datasets and fine-tune the pre-trained models on sparse semantic occupancy prediction and 3D object detection tasks.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the generalized performance of pre-trained SPMs on different downstream tasks and compare with a baseline trained from scratch.
COST: 45000
PREDICTION: We anticipate that this approach will demonstrate better performance than the baseline, especially when RGB-to-sparse correspondences are challenging to establish. However, over-reliance on pre-training might lead to overfitting when applied to specific real-world driving scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Complementary Learning: Integrating Explicit and Implicit Queries for Enhanced 3D Understanding in SPMs
PROPOSAL: Investigate the feasibility of training both explicit (e.g., pixel-based or bev-based) and implicit (e.g., query-based) representations within a single SPM, under the guidance of a modulated multi-task loss function. This complementary learning framework allows the network to explore both explicit and implicit representations, potentially mitigating the limitations of any single approach.
CONTROLS: Quantitatively compare the performance of Complementary Learning against its constituent sub-architectures, as well as popular dense and sparse baselines, across a set of driving tasks.
COST: 75000
PREDICTION: We believe that Complementary Learning will lead to more robust and versatile SPMs that combine strengths from both explicit and implicit representations. However, high-dimensional and complex interactions between loss terms might increase training instability and convergence difficulties.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: 3D Scene Graph Pre-training for SPMs
PROPOSAL: We propose to pre-train Sparse Perception Models on unlabeled multi-view driving data by introducing a 3D scene graph pre-training scheme. This approach learns to extract a global graph structure representing the spatiotemporal relationships between objects and scenes. The graph is constructed by predicting bounded 3D boxes around salient objects and pairwise relationships among these bounding boxes. The model learns to predict the adjacency matrix, edge attributes, and node attributes (including object classes and locations) in an end-to-end fashion.
CONTROLS: We compare our 3D scene graph pre-training with state-of-the-art SPMs (e.g., DETR3D, PETR series) and dense BEV-centric models (e.g., BEVFormer, Lift-Splat-Shoot) pre-trained with other methods (e.g., contrastive learning, NeRF-based approaches).
COST: 10000
PREDICTION: Our 3D scene graph pre-training significantly improves the performance of SPMs on downstream tasks, and it outperforms other pre-training methods. However, the method may struggle with complex scenes and large numbers of objects, where the graph becomes too dense and difficult to learn.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Few-Shot Adaptation of Sparse Queries via Invariant Esimation
PROPOSAL: We investigate the problem of few-shot adaptation of sparse queries from a pre-trained generator network to a new task and environment, where the query space varies significantly. Inspired by recent advances in symmetry and invariance, we propose an invariant estimation approach to learn query-invariant representations that can generalize across different tasks and environments. The key idea is to learn a set of invariant query descriptors that can capture the underlying structures and patterns in the sparse queries, and to apply these descriptors to adapt the pre-trained generator network to new tasks with minimal supervision.
CONTROLS: We compare our few-shot adaptation method with state-of-the-art SPMs (e.g., DETR3D, PETR series) and dense BEV-centric models (e.g., BEVFormer, Lift-Splat-Shoot) with various few-shot adaptation strategies (e.g., nearest-neighbours interpolation, fine-tuning pre-trained models).
COST: 24000
PREDICTION: Our few-shot adaptation method effectively adapts the pre-trained generator network to new tasks and environments with minimal supervision, and outperforms current state-of-the-art few-shot adaptation methods. However, the method may require a large number of examples to learn the invariant query descriptors accurately, especially for complex query spaces.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Attention-based Query Refinement for SPMs
PROPOSAL: We propose an attention-based query refinement technique for SPMs, which refines the sparse queries based on the attention map between the input features and the pre-post-updated features. The attention map is used to reweight the importance of each query in the query set, and then update the sparse queries accordingly. Our approach leverages the advantages of SPMs while addressing their limitation of relying on a fixed set of queries.
CONTROLS: We compare our attention-based query refinement with state-of-the-art SPMs (e.g., DETR3D, PETR series) and compare the performance with queries generated by other pre-training and fine-tuning methods.
COST: 14400
PREDICTION: Our attention-based query refinement improves the performance of SPMs on downstream tasks and outperforms existing query refinement methods. However, the refinement process may be computationally expensive and not always necessary, depending on the query distribution and the specific task.

REVISE 2: 
PREDICTION (Few-Shot Adaptation of Sparse Queries via Invariant Esimation): While our few-shot adaptation method effectively adapts the pre-trained generator network to new tasks and environments with minimal supervision, and outperforms current state-of-the-art few-shot adaptation methods, it requires a large number of examples to learn the invariant query descriptors accurately, especially for complex query spaces, which might lead to overfitting if not managed properly, and could use a separate neural regularizer to adapt more class heads.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Visual-Semantic Context Augmentation for SPMs
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel method to augment the visual and semantic context of sparse queries in SPMs, which leverages knowledge from a large-scale ontology to generate relevant context for each query. Our method involves a hierarchical structure to descend through the ontology and generate context vectors based on modularizing auxiliary concepts and dynamics of coherent geometries as viewed from an observer. These augmented context vectors are used as input features to enhance the sparse query representations.
CONTROLS: We compare our visual-semantic context augmentation with state-of-the-art SPMs (e.g., DETR3D, PETR series) and dense BEV-centric models (e.g., BEVFormer, Lift-Splat-Shoot) that use contextual information in pre-training (e.g., Masked Autoencoders, NeRF-based approaches).
COST: 36000
PREDICTION: Our visual-semantic context augmentation improves the performance of SPMs on downstream tasks by introducing crucial background and contextual information that was not available in the original sparse queries. However, the method requires a large-scale ontology and may be computationally expensive to process, which could affect its practical deployment in real-world applications.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Topological Regularization for SPMs
PROPOSAL: We propose a topological regularization method for SPMs, which introduces a new regularization term to the loss function that encourages the sparse queries to form a topological structure that preserves the relationships between objects in the scene. Our method leverages the idea that objects often lie on manifolds or surfaces, and uses geometric and topological notions to define a manifold structure for the object data. We show that this regularization term helps to improve the robustness and generalizability of SPMs.
CONTROLS: We compare our topological regularization with state-of-the-art SPMs (e.g., DETR3D, PETR series) and dense BEV-centric models (e.g., BEVFormer, Lift-Splat-Shoot) without any regularization, as well as with other regularization methods (e.g., L1, L2).
COST: 54000
PREDICTION: Our topological regularization significantly improves the robustness and generalizability of SPMs on downstream tasks, particularly in scenes with complex object relationships and occlusions. However, the method may require careful tuning of hyperparameters to achieve optimal results, as the regularization term can sometimes lead to over-smoothing of the query representations.

REVISE 4: 
PREDICTION (Visual-Semantic Context Augmentation for SPMs): While our visual-semantic context augmentation improves the performance of SPMs on downstream tasks, the method requires a large-scale ontology and may be computationally expensive to process, which could affect its practical deployment in real-world applications. A more feasible approach would be to use hierarchical feature selection, and leveraging large image datasets to creatively train on them such they can share similar topological properties and class preservation between datapoints in it.

TITLE: 3D Scene Graph Pre-training for SPMs
PROPOSAL: We propose to pre-train Sparse Perception Models on unlabeled multi-view driving data by introducing a 3D scene graph pre-training scheme. This approach learns to extract a global graph structure representing the spatiotemporal relationships between objects and scenes. The graph is constructed by predicting bounded 3D boxes around salient objects and pairwise relationships among these bounding boxes. The model learns to predict the adjacency matrix, edge attributes, and node attributes (including object classes and locations) in an end-to-end fashion.
CONTROLS: We compare our 3D scene graph pre-training with state-of-the-art SPMs (e.g., DETR3D, PETR series) and dense BEV-centric models (e.g., BEVFormer, Lift-Splat-Shoot) pre-trained with other methods (e.g., contrastive learning, NeRF-based approaches).
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: Our 3D scene graph pre-training significantly improves the performance of SPMs on downstream tasks, and it outperforms other pre-training methods. However, the method may struggle with complex scenes and large numbers of objects, where the graph becomes too dense and difficult to learn.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Few-Shot Adaptation of Sparse Queries via Invariant Esimation
PROPOSAL: We investigate the problem of few-shot adaptation of sparse queries from a pre-trained generator network to a new task and environment, where the query space varies significantly. Inspired by recent advances in symmetry and invariance, we propose an invariant estimation approach to learn query-invariant representations that can generalize across different tasks and environments. The key idea is to learn a set of invariant query descriptors that can capture the underlying structures and patterns in the sparse queries, and to apply these descriptors to adapt the pre-trained generator network to new tasks with minimal supervision.
CONTROLS: We compare our few-shot adaptation method with state-of-the-art SPMs (e.g., DETR3D, PETR series) and dense BEV-centric models (e.g., BEVFormer, Lift-Splat-Shoot) with various few-shot adaptation strategies (e.g., nearest-neighbours interpolation, fine-tuning pre-trained models).

However, the method may require a large number of examples to learn the invariant query descriptors accurately, especially for complex query spaces.

PROPOSAL: We propose an attention-based query refinement technique for SPMs, which refines the sparse queries based on the attention map between the input features and the pre-post-updated features. The attention map is used to reweight the importance of each query in the query set, and then update the sparse queries accordingly. Our approach leverages the advantages of SPMs while addressing their limitation of relying on a fixed set of queries.
CONTROLS: We compare our attention-based query refinement with state-of-the-art SPMs (e.g., DETR3D, PETR series) and compare the performance with queries generated by other pre-training and fine-tuning methods.

TITLE: Hierarchical Self-Supervised Learning for Sparse Perception Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a hierarchical self-supervised learning framework for pre-training Sparse Perception Models. Our method consists of two stages: a coarse-stage that uses sparse 3D queries with pixel-wise semantic segmentation as the loss function, and a fine-stage that uses a texture completion objective to learn detailed geometric features. We jointly optimize the two stages with a curriculum learning strategy, starting from a fully-supervised regime and gradually introducing self-supervision at the fine stage.
CONTROLS: BEVFormer and Lift-Splat-Shoot
COST: 80

Our method consists of two stages: a coarse-stage that uses sparse 3D queries with pixel-wise semantic segmentation as the loss function, and a fine-stage that uses a texture completion objective to learn detailed geometric features. We jointly optimize the two stages with a curriculum learning strategy, starting from a fully-supervised regime and gradually introducing self-supervision at the fine stage.
CONTROLS: BEVFormer and Lift-Splat-Shoot
COST: 720
PREDICTION: We expect our method to outperform existing pre-training approaches for SPMs on 3D object detection and semantic segmentation tasks, with a 5-10% increase in mAP and SEO score respectively. However, it may fail on complex scenes with numerous occlusions due to the limited capacity of our hierarchical framework.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unsupervised Pre-training for Sparse Perception Models via Geometric Reparametrization
PROPOSAL: We pre-train a SPM with a novel combination of 3DGS modules and an unsupervised training objective, designed to optimize consistency between the predicted sparse queries and a geometrically reparameterized latent space, induced by the 3DGS representation. The SPM learns to compactly represent the underlying 3D scene structure in an unsupervised manner, without relying on dense intermediate representations.
CONTROLS: We compare against baselines which pre-train using a coarse 3D reconstruction task, and ablate our method by removing the geometric reparameterization component.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our method should significantly improve the unsupervised pre-training of SPMs, while still being efficient enough to finish within the specified timeframe. It may fail if the geometric reparameterization component is not sufficiently reliable or generalizable.

TITLE: Efficient Query-Based Self-Supervised Learning for Sparse Perception Models
PROPOSAL: We propose an efficient self-supervised learning framework for SPMs, which leverages the power of sparse points sampling and achieves improved generalization capabilities. We design a custom self-supervised loss function that encourages the model to learn distinguished features from the vicinity of each sampled point, exploiting the inherent properties of sparse point clouds.
CONTROLS: We compare against the state-of-the-art self-supervised learning baseline for SPMs, as well as ours without the efficient sampling and query components.
COST: 225 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method should be efficient, adaptable to diverse point cloud geometries, and yields good quality sparse point clouds. However, the robustness of the method may degrade if the sampling density is too low.

TITLE: Unsupervised Pre-training for Sparse Perception Models via Geometric Reparametrization
PROPOSAL: We pre-train a SPM with a novel combination of 3DGS modules and an unsupervised training objective, designed to optimize consistency between the predicted sparse queries and a geometrically reparameterized latent space, induced by the 3DGS representation. The SPM learns to compactly represent the underlying 3D scene structure in an unsupervised manner, without relying on dense intermediate representations.
CONTROLS: We compare against baselines which pre-train using a coarse 3D reconstruction task, and ablate our method by removing the geometric reparameterization component.
COST: 450 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our method should significantly improve the unsupervised pre-training of SPMs, while still being efficient enough to finish within the specified timeframe. It may fail if the geometric reparameterization component is not sufficiently reliable or generalizable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Query-Based Self-Supervised Learning for Sparse Perception Models
PROPOSAL: We propose an efficient self-supervised learning framework for SPMs, which leverages the power of sparse points sampling and achieves improved generalization capabilities. We design a custom self-supervised loss function that encourages the model to learn distinguished features from the vicinity of each sampled point, exploiting the inherent properties of sparse point clouds.
CONTROLS: We compare against the state-of-the-art self-supervised learning baseline for SPMs, as well as ours without the efficient sampling and query components.
COST: 680 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method should be efficient, adaptable to diverse point cloud geometries, and yields good quality sparse point clouds. However, the robustness of the method may degrade if the sampling density is too low.

ACTION: REVISE
NUMBER: 1
TITLE: Unsupervised Pre-training for Sparse Perception Models via Geometric Reparametrization
PROPOSAL: We extend the unsupervised pre-training for SPMs by introducing an attention-based geometric matching mechanism to promote the alignment between predicted sparse points and the actual 3D scene structure. This attention-based mechanism helps to focus on the most informative points for matching.
CONTROLS: The base case for the revisited model is the same as before, with our previous addition. We also ablate the importance of the attention-based mechanism to geometric matching.
COST: 790 GPU-hours (increased to account for added complexity)
PREDICTION: The addition of the geometric matching mechanism should significantly improve the unsupervised pre-training of SPMs, particularly in scenes with complex geometry. However, the added complexity might cause the model to fail if the attention mechanism is too rigid or inflexible.

ACTION: REVISE
NUMBER: 2
TITLE: Efficient Query-Based Self-Supervised Learning for Sparse Perception Models
PROPOSAL: We refine the self-supervised loss function by incorporating a semantic-aware term that encourages the model to learn more attentive and context-aware features around each sampled point. This term is designed to promote the prediction of points that are semantically meaningful and relevant.
CONTROLS: We compare against our previous self-supervised baseline, and ablate the impact of the semantic-aware term on the overall performance of the model.
COST: 920 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The introduction of the semantic-aware term should improve the generalization and robustness of the model to diverse point cloud geometries, but might fail if the semantic labels are not correctly assigned or if the addition of the term leads to overfitting.

ACTION: REVISE
NUMBER: 2
TITLE: Efficient Query-Based Self-Supervised Learning for Sparse Perception Models
PROPOSAL: We modify the self-supervised loss function to include a triplet-based point matching mechanism, designed to learn more robust and discriminative features between the sparse point clouds.
CONTROLS: We compare against our previous self-supervised baseline, and ablate the impact of the triplet-based mechanism on the overall performance of the model.
COST: 920 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The introduction of the triplet-based point matching mechanism should improve the model's ability to distinguish between points with different semantic meanings, but might fail if the sampling density is too low or if the mechanism leads to increased training instability.

ACTION: REVISE
NUMBER: 1
TITLE: Unsupervised Pre-training for Sparse Perception Models via Geometric Reparametrization
PROPOSAL: We revise the geometric matching mechanism to utilize a learnable projector that adapts to the point cloud geometry, enabling more effective alignment between the predicted sparse points and the actual 3D scene structure. The projector is trained jointly with the SPM, allowing for optimal adaptation to the specific task.
CONTROLS: The base case for the revisited model is the same as before, with our previous extension. We also ablate the importance of the learnable projector in the geometric matching mechanism.
COST: 1050 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The introduction of the learnable projector should significantly improve the unsupervised pre-training of SPMs, particularly in scenes with complex geometry and varying densities. However, the model may fail if the projector is not able to generalize across different types of point cloud geometries.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer of Pre-trained Sparse Perception Models to Heterogeneous Downstream Tasks
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel adaptation mechanism for pre-trained SPMs to be transferred to downstream tasks with different query structures and decoders. Our approach utilizes a multi-task learning framework that adapts the pre-trained SPM to learn task-specific query embeddings and decoder parameters.
CONTROLS: We compare against direct transfer of the pre-trained SPM to the downstream task, and ablate the impact of the adaptation mechanism on the overall performance of the model.
COST: 1300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The adaptation mechanism should enable effective transfer of pre-trained SPMs to diverse downstream tasks, but may fail if the adaptation process is not able to handle significant changes in query structure and decoder architectures.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Resolution Sparse Point Cloud Completion for 3D Object Detection
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel multi-resolution sparse point cloud completion approach for 3D object detection. Our method utilizes a hierarchical structure to progressively refine the point cloud representation, enabling the detection of objects at varying scales and orientations.
CONTROLS: We compare against a baseline that uses a single-resolution point cloud completion approach, and ablate the impact of each resolution level on the overall performance of the method.
COST: 1550 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The multi-resolution approach should significantly improve the accuracy of 3D object detection, particularly for objects with complex shapes and varied sizes. However, the method may fail if not able to handle objects with ambiguous or inconsistent point cloud representations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving Transferability of Sparse Perception Models with Viewpoint-Agnostic Training
PROPOSAL: We propose a viewpoint-agnostic training approach for sparse perception models, which learns to generalize across different viewpoints and directional lighting conditions. Our method utilizes a contrastive learning framework that encourages the model to learn viewpoint-agnostic embeddings for the sparse point cloud.
CONTROLS: We compare against a baseline that trains the model on a single viewpoint, and ablate the impact of each component of the viewpoint-agnostic training approach.
COST: 1750 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The viewpoint-agnostic training approach should significantly improve the transferability of sparse perception models across different viewpoints and directional lighting conditions. However, the method may fail if the viewpoint variation is too large or if the contrastive learning framework does not effectively capture the viewpoint-agnostic semantics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comprehensive Evaluation of Sparse Perception Models on a Variety of Autonomous Driving Tasks
PROPOSAL: We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the proposed sparse perception models on a variety of autonomous driving tasks, including 3D object detection, scene understanding, and motion forecasting. Our evaluation protocol aims to assess the robustness, generalization, and transferability of the models across different tasks and scenarios.
CONTROLS: We compare the proposed models against state-of-the-art dense perception models and ablate the impact of each component of the models on the evaluation results.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The comprehensive evaluation should provide a thorough understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of the proposed sparse perception models and their applicability to real-world autonomous driving scenarios. However, the evaluation process may be challenging and time-consuming, and may require significant expertise in autonomous driving and perception tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pseudo-Label Filtering with Progressive Confidence Score
PROPOSAL: 
We propose a self-training based online adaptation framework, where instead of relying on a fixed confidence threshold to filter pseudo-labels, we use a progressive confidence score that adaptively updates at every test step. This is achieved by maintaining a buffer of pseudo-labels generated at each test step, which we use to train a classifier to predict whether the pseudo-labels at current step are reliable or not. We then use this classifier to progressively update the filter threshold, allowing samples with increasingly lower confidence to contribute after each power iteration. The use of progressive confidence score helps alleviate the scarcity and noise issue of pseudo-labels and improves overall adaptation stability. We deploy this methodology on the pre-trained vision-language detector GLIP.
CONTROLS: 
- compare with baseline GLIP model on pseudo-label filtering with a fixed confidence threshold
- ablate the progressive confidence score with a static Confidence Threshold
- compare the proposed method with an oracle that uses the ground truths as pseudo-labels
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: 
We expect the proposed method to show significant improvement over baselines by being more robust to pseudo-label noise and scarcity, and achieving better adaptation performance on real-world datasets. It may fail to converge if the pseudo-label buffer size is too small or if the pseudo-label generator is too noisy, resulting in biased classifier decisions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Vision-Language Adapter Distillation
PROPOSAL: 
We propose a distillation-based test-time adaptation method that leverages the pre-trained knowledge of vision-language detectors. By attaching an adapter module on top of the pre-trained detector, we transfer the target domain knowledge while preserving the pre-trained generalization capability. The adapter module is inspired by typical vision-language tasks and is designed to extract domain-invariant features from pseudo-labels. To effectively transfer knowledge, we employ a self-distillation scheme where the student detector (with the adapter) distills the knowledge of the teacher detector (without the adapter). This process iteratively refines the adapter weights and pseudolabels, allowing for effective knowledge transfer.
CONTROLS: 
- compare the performance of the proposed method with the baseline pre-trained GLIP model on real-world datasets
- ablate the adapter module to investigate its contribution
- compare with the same self-training method that uses a static detector without distillation
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: 
We expect the distillation-based method to exhibit superior adaptation performance by efficiently transferring target domain knowledge while preserving pre-trained generalization. It may fail to converge or experience information loss if the adapter module is too complex or if the distillation process gets stuck in a suboptimal solution due to the pseudo-label noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation via Alignment of Invariant Features
PROPOSAL: 
We propose a novel test-time adaptation method that leverages the pre-trained vision-language detector to extract domain-invariant features from both the source and target domains. By aligning these invariant features using adversarial training, we adapt the detector to new target domains without requiring any labeled source data or identical category spaces between source and target domains. This approach allows for effective test-time adaptation in both closed-set and open-set scenarios. To further improve adaptation performance, we use a combination of feature alignment and pseudo-labeling to iteratively refine the adaptation process.
CONTROLS: 
- compare the proposed method with the baseline pre-trained GLIP model on real-world datasets in both closed-set and open-set scenarios
- ablate the adversarial training component to investigate its contribution
- compare with the same self-training method that uses pseudo-labels but without domain invariant feature alignment
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: 
We expect the proposed method to demonstrate superior adaptation performance by effectively leveraging domain-invariant features and adversarial training. It may fail to improve or exhibit mode collapse if the adversarial training process is unstable or gets stuck in a suboptimal solution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Agent Test-Time Adaptation for Domain Adaptation
PROPOSAL: 
We propose a novel multi-agent architecture for test-time domain adaptation, where multiple agents work together to achieve adaptation. Each agent is designed to specialize in a specific domain or a subset of domains, and they interact with each other to share knowledge and adapt to the target domain. By leveraging the power of multi-agent learning, our approach enables effective adaptation even in the presence of scarce or noisy pseudo-labels. Specifically, we design a shared pseudo-label generation module that enables agents to generate high-quality pseudo-labels for each other's support.
CONTROLS: 
- compare the proposed multi-agent approach with the baseline pre-trained GLIP model on real-world datasets
- ablate the number of agents and their specialized roles to investigate their contribution
- compare with the single-agent version of the proposed method
COST: 10000
PREDICTION: 
We expect the proposed multi-agent approach to demonstrate superior adaptation performance by leveraging the knowledge sharing and pseudo-label generation capabilities of the agents. It may fail to improve or exhibit instability if the number of agents or their specialized roles is not effectively designed, leading to suboptimal adaptation effects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Test-Time Adaptation with Bayesian Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: 
We propose a novel test-time adaptation framework that leverages Bayesian Neural Networks (BNNs) to quantify epistemic uncertainty during adaptation. By modeling the uncertainty in the adaptation process, our approach enables the model to adapt more robustly to new domains and reduce overfitting. Specifically, we use a BNN to predict the uncertainty of pseudo-labels and weights, and use these uncertainty estimates to adapt the model in a data-driven manner. This allows our approach to adapt to the target domain while maintaining a robustness to the uncertainty of the adaptation process.
CONTROLS: 
- compare the proposed uncertainty-aware adaptation approach with traditional test-time adaptation methods on real-world datasets
- ablate the use of BNNs to investigate their contribution
- compare with an oracle adaptation approach that has access to ground truth uncertainty estimates
COST: 10700
PREDICTION: 
We expect the proposed uncertainty-aware adaptation approach to demonstrate superior robustness and performance in test-time adaptation, thanks to the use of Bayesian Neural Networks to quantify epistemic uncertainty. It may fail to improve or under-perform if the BNNs are not effectively trained or if the uncertainty estimates are not accurately captured, leading to suboptimal adaptation effects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hybrid Test-Time Adaptation Framework
PROPOSAL: 
We propose a hybrid test-time adaptation framework thatcombines the strengths of multiple adaptation approaches. Specifically, our framework integrates the improved pseudo-label generation using contextualized image embeddings (Revisit Proposal 1) with the adaptive learning of domain-invariant features via adversarial training (Proposal 3) and the uncertainty-aware adaptation using Bayesian Neural Networks (Proposal 5). By leveraging the synergy between these approaches, our hybrid framework is designed to improve the robustness, efficiency, and performance of test-time adaptation in real-world scenarios.
CONTROLS: 
- compare the proposed hybrid framework with individual adaptation approaches on real-world datasets
- ablate each component of the hybrid framework to investigate their contribution
- compare with a meta-adaptation approach that adapts the adaptation process itself
COST: 15000
PREDICTION: 
We expect the proposed hybrid framework to demonstrate superior performance and robustness in test-time adaptation, thanks to the integration of multiple adaptation approaches. It may fail to improve or under-perform if the individual components are not effectively integrated or if the adaptation process becomes too complex, leading to suboptimal adaptation effects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation via Model Pruning and Knowledge Distillation
PROPOSAL: 
We propose an efficient test-time adaptation approach that leverages model pruning and knowledge distillation to reduce the computational overhead of adaptation. Specifically, we use a gradient-based pruning method to remove redundant weights and connections in the detector, and then use knowledge distillation to transfer the knowledge from the pruned detector to a smaller, more efficient model. By pruning the detector and distilling the knowledge, our approach enables efficient adaptation in real-time scenarios while maintaining a comparable level of performance.
CONTROLS: 
- compare the proposed efficient adaptation approach with traditional test-time adaptation methods on real-world datasets
- ablate the pruning method and knowledge distillation to investigate their contribution
- compare with a parallel adaptation approach that uses multiple GPUs to speed up adaptation
COST: 20000
PREDICTION: 
We expect the proposed efficient adaptation approach to demonstrate significant improvements in adaptation speed and efficiency while maintaining a comparable level of performance. It may fail to improve or under-perform if the pruning method is not effective or if the knowledge distillation process is not well-matched, leading to suboptimal adaptation effects.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Quality-Controlled Test-Time Adaptation
REVISION: 2. Vision-Language Adapter Distillation
PROPOSAL: 
We enhance Vision-Language Adapter Distillation (VLAD) by incorporating a quality control mechanism to handle pseudo-label scarcity, noise, and missing pseudo-labels. Specifically, we propose a threshold-based filtering mechanism that assigns different weights to pseudo-labels based on their quality scores. This allows for a more nuanced handling of pseudo-labels, where high-quality ones contribute more significantly to the distillation process, while low-quality ones are downweighted or even ignored. By controlling the quality of pseudo-labels fed into the distillation process, we improve the robustness and efficiency of VLAD.
CONTROLS: 
- compare the quality-controlled VLAD with original VLAD on real-world datasets
- ablate the quality threshold to investigate its contribution
- compare with the proposed pseudo-label filtering methodology (Revisit Proposal 1)
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: 
We expect the quality-controlled VLAD to achieve better adaptation performance by alleviating the issues caused by pseudo-label noise and scarcity. It may fail to improve or under-perform if the quality threshold is too stringent or too lenient, leading to either too many or too few pseudo-labels being considered, respectively.
