ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Alternative Regularization Scheme for Vision-Language Adapter Distillation
REVISION: 2. Vision-Language Adapter Distillation
PROPOSAL: 
We revisit Vision-Language Adapter Distillation (VLAD) by proposing an alternative regularization scheme to address the issue of adapter weights growing too large during the distillation process. Specifically, we leverage a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) structure to learn a regularizer that maps the domain-specific knowledge to a low-dimensional space while maintaining the compatibility with the pre-trained detector. This helps in reducing the size of the adapter weights while maintaining the model's ability to adapt to new domains. Our regularizer serves as an implicit knowledge distillation mechanism that complements the explicit one in VLAD, allowing for more efficient knowledge transfer.
CONTROLS: 
- compare the proposed regularizer with traditional dropout and L1/L2 regularization in VLAD
- ablate the GAN structure to investigate its contribution
- compare with the original VLAD without any regularization
COST: 20000
PREDICTION: 
We expect the proposed regularization scheme to improve the stability and efficiency of VLAD by preventing overfitting and adapter weights growing too large. It may fail to improve or under-perform if the GAN structure is not effectively optimized or gets stuck in a suboptimal solution, leading to poor regularization effects.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Improved Pseudo-Label Generation using Contextualized Image Embeddings
REVISION: 1. Pseudo-Label Filtering with Progressive Confidence Score
PROPOSAL: 
We build upon Pseudo-Label Filtering with Progressive Confidence Score (PLF-PCS) by introducing contextualized image embeddings to improve pseudo-label generation. Specifically, we use a Visual BERT model to contextualize the image embeddings and capture the meaningful semantics and relationships between objects in the scene. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Labeled-Turning Shortcut for Enriched Pseudo-Labeling
PROPOSAL: We propose a method that injects labeled data into the target domain as pseudo-labels using source-trained detectors at every k-th test image, thereby continuously enriching the pseudo-label set with higher-quality labels while ensuring that target test samples are not overwhelmed by redundant pseudo-labels for consecutive inference. This strategy can bridge the gap between self-training and expectation-maximization pseudo-labeling, allowing the vision-language detector to explore more effectively the initially challenging target domains without suffering from the degradation of early pseudo-labels.
CONTROLS: Baselines include standard self-training, use of adapters (e.g., Open Categories and RTOracle), and pseudo-label filtering without additional mid-batch augmentation. Our ablation study will also explore the impact of label injection frequency and pseudo-label set size on the detector's performance.
COST: 1345.6
PREDICTION: Our labeled-turning shortcut is expected to bring a 2-3% mAP improvement over standard self-training with batch pseudo-label filtering due to the injection of higher-quality pseudo-labels and thereby a more efficient adaptation process, but may perform poorly when pseudo-labeling with both the source-trained detector and label injector (k=1) provides excessive noise for adaptation, heightening the risk of overfitting to poor pseudo-labels early in adaptation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Task-Specific Knowledge Distillation for Vision-Language Detection
PROPOSAL: We introduce an adaptive task-specific knowledge distillation (TSKD) method, where a meta-learner is trained to distill task-specific knowledge from the pre-trained detector and a test-time adaptator (TTA), and use the distillation objective as an additional loss function during the online adaptation process, thereby transferring task-specific knowledge of the pre-trained detector to the adaptator and promoting effective adaptation to unseen target domains without overwriting valuable pre-trained knowledge.
CONTROLS: Our comparisons will include the vanilla TTAOD method, pseudo-labeling with, and without the use of an TTA, and state-of-the-art real-time adaptation methods like FastAdapt and iCARL.
COST: 1680
PREDICTION: The proposed adaptive TSKD method is expected to bring a 5% mAP improvement in real-time, unseen domain adaptation tasks by leveraging the benefits of task-specific knowledge transfer, endowing the detector with improved adaptability, and quick capture of valuable pre-trained knowledge patterns, but requires careful hyperparameter selection due to its adaptive nature.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Domain-Agnostic Meta-Objective for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
PROPOSAL: We propose a domain-agnostic meta-objective, which combines the original task objective and a new meta-objective that adapts to the target domain, promoting better learning of domain-agnostic features and adaptation abilities. This meta-objective will enable the detector to more efficiently adapt to unseen target domains by regularly updating its adaptation strategy based on a meta-learning process that backpropagates through the target adaptation process.
CONTROLS: Baseline controls will include self-training with a meta- learner, meta-learning for domain adaptation, and adaptation strategies that utilize uncertainty-based sampling.
COST: 1400
PREDICTION: The proposed domain-agnostic meta-objective is expected to improve the detector's adaptation by 4% mAP on unseen domains due to the detector's optimized adaptation strategy that learns to adapt to new domains during the training process, but may encounter overupdating issues if the meta-objective adaptation process becomes overly focused on adapting to noise-rich data or failed source-domain samples.

TITLE: Self-Supervised Vision-Language Mass Prototype Adapter for Online Object Detection
PROPOSAL: Adapt a mass prototype-based architecture that combines the powerful inference capabilities of prototypical networks with the vision-language pre-training capabilities of recent foundation models, yielding a generic, initialization-free, and highly adaptable object detector. As such, it doesn't need any source data, pre-trained detectors, or category labels. Instead, it does the following: at test time, the detector partitions the current target test batch into a fixed-size set of mini-batches, where each mini-batch is processed once through a learnable, instance-wise fully connected adaptation module; it adds irrelevant prototypes for absent categories and progressively reduces them as confidence arises, avoiding scarce pseudo-label issues; and, it regularly pools and spreads the adaptation across all mini-batches, enhancing data efficiency and generalization. We focus on three versions with respective capacities of 20k, 50k, and 100k parameters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Vision-Language Based Test-Time Adaption for Cross-Domain, Cross-Class Object Detection
PROPOSAL: Implement the PreTrained VL-TTAOD algorithm, a test-time adaptation method using the pre-trained vision-language detector ViLT, exploiting its zero-shot generalization capabilities, to translate unlabeled target domain data into a latent space compatible with the pre-trained detector's weights. The algorithm consists of two stages: target-aware projection and regularization of the weights during inference. Control experiments include:
- Baselines: No adaptation, ViLT fine-tuning on target data, vanilla pseudo-labeling.
- Ablations: (1) removal of target-aware projection; (2) removal of weight regularization; (3) using different vision-language detectors.
- Controls: assessing the algorithm's robustness under target data scarcity and varying quality of pseudo-labels.
COST: 8000
PREDICTION: The algorithm significantly improves on ViLT's zero-shot performance on the target domain and demonstrates robustness under the conditions tested, with potential for overfitting if the target data distribution shifts drastically.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Target Data Refining with Entropic K-Means for Enhanced Pseudo-Labeling in VL-TTAOD
PROPOSAL: Develop an iterative pseudo-labeling procedure within the PreTrained VL-TTAOD pipeline, leveraging Entropic K-Means clustering to refine the target domain distribution and generate more accurate pseudo-labels. Specifically, the algorithm clusters the target domain data into coherent segments that are then projected onto the pre-trained detector's latent space. These refined pseudo-labels improve the detector's adaptation performance while maintaining ViLT's zero-shot generalization ability.
Control experiments include: comparing clustering algorithms, experimenting with different cluster sizes and iterations.
- Baselines: PreTrained VL-TTAOD without refining, pseudo-labeling with simpler clustering algorithms (K-Means, Hierarchical Clustering).
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: The iterative Entropic K-Means clustering leads to a substantial boost in the detector's adaptation performance and demonstrates improved robustness under noise in the target data, especially when combined with the target-aware projection in PreTrained VL-TTAOD.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Investigating Scalable Neural Network Performance with Combinatorial Optimization
PROPOSAL: 
Design a neural network to solve the Euclidean Traveling Salesman Problem (ETSP) for small instance sizes, using a fixed capacity of 1.2M parameters and an unconstrained compute budget. Train the model using an evolutionary algorithm, with grid search for optimal hyperparameters. This setup should push the model close to its capacity limit, allowing for complexity trends to emerge. Simulate multiple instances of ETSP with varying numbers of cities (10-50), keeping other problem complexity measures (e.g., problem dimensionality) constant. Measure performance as solution quality (rms Euclidean distance between optimal and found tours) under fixed compute time constraints. Investigate if performance degrades predictably with increasing solution space size (more cities), and if dimensionality growth affects the scaling behavior.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Neural network trained with backpropagation instead of evolutionary algorithm (to compare optimization method)
- Baseline 2: Small instance size (5 cities, to isolate the effect of growing solution space)

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling Solution Space Size in the Euclidean Traveling Salesman Problem
PROPOSAL: We investigate the regime where the solution space size is scaled while keeping the representation space size fixed. We create a variant of the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) where the number of cities and the maximum allowed route length are increased in tandem, resulting in a combinatorially exploding solution space size. We train a fixed-size neural network using reinforcement learning to solve the TSP with decreasing maximum allowed route lengths, effectively scaling down the solution space size, and record its performance. We compare this to a variant where the representation space size is also scaled by increasing the dimensionality of the city locations.
CONTROLS: Ablation of the exploration noise in the reinforcement learning algorithm, comparison to the landscape optimization algorithm, use of larger/trained-from-scratch baseline models.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: We expect that performance improves 'smoothly' when the maximum allowed route length is reduced (solution space size scaling) but degrades at first when the representation space size is scaled, before eventually recovering. It might fail if the baseline performance of the TSP without route limitations is unpredictable or scales too unpredictably with the incremental TSP variant we were looking at.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaled-Down Route Optimization Trade-off
PROPOSAL: As an extension to the first experiment, we investigate whether scaling down the representation space size using input dimensionality reduction techniques affects the trade-off between model performance and training compute. We apply singular value decomposition (SVD) and random feature mapping (RMF) to reduce the dimensionality of the city locations, analyzing how the magnitude of dimensionality reduction affects TSP performance. We compare this to a baseline where the dimensionality of the city locations remains fixed.
CONTROLS: Comparison to the experiment where only the solution space size is scaled, ablation of the dimensionality reduction techniques, and a transfer learning baseline where we train the model on TSP instances of smaller scale and then apply it to the larger instance with reduced input dimensionality.
COST: 2164.5808
PREDICTION: We expect that model performance improves modestly when the dimensionality is reduced, and we'll discover a particular training compute input that manages an optimal balance between performance improvement and training cost reduction. It might fail if the model completely fails to adapt to the dimensionality reduction or if the baseline performance is too high, making any loss due to dimensionality reduction obscure.

PROPOSAL: Train a fixed-size neural network (e.g., a convolutional neural network (CNN)) using simulated data for the Euclidean Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP). textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating a Hierarchical Selection Approach for Multilingual Data
PROPOSAL: We will create a hierarchical model-based approach to select high-quality data for LLM pretraining in multiple languages. The model will consist of a language-agnostic quality estimator, which uses a transformer-based classifier to predict the quality of input documents, and a language-specific estimator, which refines the predictions for each language using a multilayer perceptron (MLP) with language-specific weights. We will pretrain the language-agnostic estimator on a large-scale multilingual dataset, such as ParaCrawl, and fine-tune the language-specific estimator on each language's particular characteristics, leveraging resources such as Wikipedia, Multilingual WMT News Commentary, and web data from the web archive. The hierarchical model will output a combined quality score for each document, which will be used to select the top-quality documents for LLM pretraining.
CONTROLS: We will compare our hierarchical approach to existing model-based selection methods, such as DCLM, AskLLM, and FineWeb2-HQ, as well as traditional heuristic selection methods using deduplication and rule-based filtering. We will also conduct an ablation study to evaluate the importance of the language-specific estimator.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Our hierarchical approach will outperform existing model-based selection methods, particularly in terms of consistency across languages and adaptability to different linguistic contexts, and achieve better downstream performance of LLMs in both English and other languages, compared to traditional heuristic selection methods. However, it may require more compute resources and potentially introduce new biases if not properly calibrated.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Evaluation Criteria for Multilingual Quality Assessment
PROPOSAL: To address the lack of a unified evaluation framework for multilingual quality assessment, we propose to design a comprehensive multilingual evaluation suite, including benchmarks and metrics for both monolingual and multilingual setups. We will first identify a set of quality-related evaluation metrics, such as BLEU, METEOR, and F1-score, and then develop a suite of human evaluation protocols for each language, incorporating diverse domains and corpuses. Our evaluation suite will serve as a common ground for comparing and fine-tuning our multi-lingual quality estimator, as well as for evaluating other model-based selection approaches. As a secondary objective, we will also explore the applicability and inter-interpretability of various quality-related evaluation metrics across languages and datasets.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate our evaluation suite on a variety of multilingual benchmarks, including ParaCrawl, TED, and WMT, as well as a selection of web-based corpora for diverse languages, including Fr, Es, and cn.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The novel evaluation suite will be widely adopted and facilitate comparative evaluations of various quality estimation and data selection approaches across languages, leading to improved accuracy in selecting high-quality pretraining data and reducing the reliance on domain-dependent metrics; also, the comparison of multiple metrics across languages is likely to reveal discrepancies in how quality is assessed across linguistic contexts. However, a unifying framework might favor approaches that perform best under the particular metrics included, potentially penalizing other high-performing solutions.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Weakly-Supervised Cross-Lingual Pretraining of Quality Estimators
PROPOSAL: To address the challenge of acquiring labeled data in multiple languages, we propose a weakly-supervised cross-lingual pretraining approach for quality estimators. Leveraging the idea of (self-)distillation, our method involves training a teacher model in each language with pseudo-labels generated using a multilingual quality estimator. The teacher model's predictions are then used to distill knowledge into the student model, which can be pre-trained in a multilingual setting without explicit supervision in any language. To further improve the robustness of our proposed approach, we will incorporate a transfer-learning module, allowing the student model to leverage its existing knowledge in one language to adapt to another. We aim to show that our approach can efficiently learn high-quality data selection criteria for multiple languages.
CONTROLS: We will compare our weakly-supervised cross-lingual pretraining approach with both fully supervised and unsupervised training methods, as well as with self-supervised pretraining methods, such as pseudo-Supervised Transformers.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The proposed weakly-supervised cross-lingual pretraining approach will significantly improve the efficiency of acquiring high-quality data selection criteria for multiple languages, reducing the need for labeled data in each language, and show comparable or even better performance compared to fully supervised methods. However, it may not fully leverage the diversity of available language-specific data and might require fine-tuning the model for each language, which may increase the risk of overfitting.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Unified Evaluation Criteria for Multilingual Quality Assessment
PROPOSAL: We will refine the proposal for the unified evaluation suite to include an additional component: a quality-aware data augmentation module. This module will generate high-quality synthetic data for evaluation, leveraging a model-based quality estimator to control the augmentation process. Our goal is to create a more comprehensive and realistic evaluation environment for testing the performance of quality estimators and data selection approaches. The augmented data will be used in conjunction with real-world data to simulate a real-world quality estimation setting, allowing us to evaluate the robustness and adaptability of quality estimators to different types of input data.
CONTROLS: We will compare the effectiveness of our quality-aware augmentation module with standard data augmentation techniques and with simulated data augmentation using a randomly initialized quality estimator.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The inclusion of the quality-aware augmentation module will significantly enhance the realism and simulation of a real-world evaluation setting, enabling more accurate assessments of quality estimators' performance and guidance for their improvement; however, it might introduce new challenges and discrepancies with how real-world data selection is typically performed, which could affect some approaches' evaluation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating a Pretraining Paradigm for Minimal Informativeness Domains
PROPOSAL: To identify scenarios where quality-based pretraining data selection might not be beneficial, we propose to investigate how models pretrain on minimal informativeness domains (MIDs), such as datasets consisting mainly of extreme instances of a particular attribute or bias-laden data. We will pretrain models on MID datasets with a quality estimator that distinguishes between high-quality and low-quality examples and compare their performance to those pretraining on conventionally selected datasets. We hypothesize that pretraining on MID datasets with a quality-aware model might exacerbate any pre-existing biases in the data and result in poorer downstream performance.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to pretraining on MID datasets without quality awareness, as well as pretraining on conventional datasets with and without quality estimation. Additionally, we will investigate whether augmenting the MID datasets with noise or paired examples can help mitigate the negative effects of pretraining on these data.
COST: 2100
PREDICTION: Pretraining on MID datasets with a quality estimator will significantly exacerbate any pre-existing biases in the data, resulting in poorer downstream performance compared to pretraining on conventionally selected or conventional MID datasets; however, the specific behaviors and outcomes will likely depend both on the specific MID data employed and on the chosen pretraining paradigm.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating a Hierarchical Selection Approach for Multilingual Data
PROPOSAL: We will enhance the initial hierarchical model-based approach for quality estimation by incorporating a transfer learning module that enables the adaptation of the language-agnostic quality estimator to new languages using few-shot learning. This transfer learning component will consist of a multi-task learning framework, where the model learns to predict quality scores across multiple languages simultaneously, leveraging its existing knowledge to adapt to new languages with minimal additional training data. Additionally, we will evaluate the hierarchical approach in a contrastive learning framework to augment the data selection process with robustness to variations in text.
CONTROLS: We will compare our enhanced hierarchical approach with the initial version, as well as with state-of-the-art few-shot learning methods and traditional quality estimation approaches without transfer learning or contrastive learning.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The enhanced hierarchical approach with transfer learning and contrastive learning components will further improve its adaptability across languages, effectiveness in selecting high-quality pretraining data, and robustness to variations in text, potentially leading to better downstream performance of LLMs in multiple languages. However, the success of few-shot learning depends significantly on the applicability and quality of the initial training data, and over-reliance on transfer learning might limit the capacity of the model to learn unique linguistic patterns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Data Quality-Aware Attention Mechanism for Language Model Training
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a novel attention mechanism, QualityAwareAttention, which integrates quality estimation directly into the self-attention mechanism of a transformer-based language model, thereby aiding in better data utilization and avoiding noise and repetitive content during pretraining. This method will help weight the input tokens and contextualize them based on their quality scores, allowing the model to better distinguish between informative and shallow data, enabling improved generalization and effectiveness in downstream NLP tasks.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate QualityAwareAttention using a set of quality-aware quality estimators and compare its results to transformer-based models pre-trained with standard attention mechanisms, as well as other self-supervised learning techniques.

PREDICTION: The data quality-aware transformer model will leverage the ability of quality estimators to filter irrelevant or redundant data during the pretraining process, leading to models better suited for real applications by optimizing its generalization across tasks; however, integration may induce introduction of parameters or power up a pre-existing bias on quality estimators results towards select ' quality instances'.

TITLE: Formulating a General Framework for Transferable Quality Estimation Across Domains
PROPOSAL: Building on the current understanding and proposals, we will aim to develop a broad and general framework for transferable quality estimation that generalizes across different domain settings. Our framework, named Multi-QE, will predict quality scores as an interpretable combination of domain-specific, cross-linguistic, and language-neutral factors.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating a Hierarchical Selection Approach for Multilingual Data
PROPOSAL: We will create a hierarchical model-based approach to select high-quality data for LLM pretraining in multiple languages. The model will consist of a language-agnostic quality estimator, which uses a transformer-based classifier to predict the quality of input documents, and a language-specific estimator, which refines the predictions for each language using a multilayer perceptron (MLP) with language-specific weights. We will pretrain the language-agnostic estimator on a large-scale multilingual dataset, such as ParaCrawl, and fine-tune the language-specific estimator on each language's particular characteristics, leveraging resources such as Wikipedia, Multilingual WMT News Commentary, and web data from the web archive. The hierarchical model will output a combined quality score for each document, which will be used to select the top-quality documents for LLM pretraining.
CONTROLS: We will compare our hierarchical approach to existing model-based selection methods, such as DCLM, AskLLM, and FineWeb2-HQ, as well as traditional heuristic selection methods using deduplication and rule-based filtering. We will also conduct an ablation study to evaluate the importance of the language-specific estimator.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: Our hierarchical approach will outperform existing model-based selection methods, particularly in terms of consistency across languages and adaptability to different linguistic contexts, and achieve better downstream performance of LLMs in both English and other languages, compared to traditional heuristic selection methods. However, it may require more compute resources and potentially introduce new biases if not properly calibrated.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Evaluation Criteria for Multilingual Quality Assessment
PROPOSAL: To address the lack of a unified evaluation framework for multilingual quality assessment, we propose to design a comprehensive multilingual evaluation suite, including benchmarks and metrics for both monolingual and multilingual setups. We will first identify a set of quality-related evaluation metrics, such as BLEU, METEOR, and F1-score, and then develop a suite of human evaluation protocols for each language, incorporating diverse domains and corpuses. Our evaluation suite will serve as a common ground for comparing and fine-tuning our multi-lingual quality estimator, as well as for evaluating other model-based selection approaches. As a secondary objective, we will also explore the applicability and inter-interpretability of various quality-related evaluation metrics across languages and datasets.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate our evaluation suite on a variety of multilingual benchmarks, including ParaCrawl, TED, and WMT, as well as a selection of web-based corpora for diverse languages, including Fr, Es, and cn.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: The novel evaluation suite will be widely adopted and facilitate comparative evaluations of various quality estimation and data selection approaches across languages, leading to improved accuracy in selecting high-quality pretraining data and reducing the reliance on domain-dependent metrics; also, the comparison of multiple metrics across languages is likely to reveal discrepancies in how quality is assessed across linguistic contexts. However, a unifying framework might favor approaches that perform best under the particular metrics included, potentially penalizing other high-performing solutions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Weakly-Supervised Cross-Lingual Pretraining of Quality Estimators
PROPOSAL: To address the challenge of acquiring labeled data in multiple languages, we propose a weakly-supervised cross-lingual pretraining approach for quality estimators. Leveraging the idea of (self-)distillation, our method involves training a teacher model in each language with pseudo-labels generated using a multilingual quality estimator. The teacher model's predictions are then used to distill knowledge into the student model, which can be pre-trained in a multilingual setting without explicit supervision in any language. To further improve the robustness of our proposed approach, we will incorporate a transfer-learning module, allowing the student model to leverage its existing knowledge in one language to adapt to another. We aim to show that our approach can efficiently learn high-quality data selection criteria for multiple languages.
CONTROLS: We will compare our weakly-supervised cross-lingual pretraining approach with both fully supervised and unsupervised training methods, as well as with self-supervised pretraining methods, such as pseudo-Supervised Transformers.
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: The proposed weakly-supervised cross-lingual pretraining approach will significantly improve the efficiency of acquiring high-quality data selection criteria for multiple languages, reducing the need for labeled data in each language, and show comparable or even better performance compared to fully supervised methods. However, it may not fully leverage the diversity of available language-specific data and might require fine-tuning the model for each language, which may increase the risk of overfitting.

TITLE: Unified Evaluation Criteria for Multilingual Quality Assessment
PROPOSAL: We will refine the proposal for the unified evaluation suite to include an additional component: a quality-aware data augmentation module. This module will generate high-quality synthetic data for evaluation, leveraging a model-based quality estimator to control the augmentation process. Our goal is to create a more comprehensive and realistic evaluation environment for testing the performance of quality estimators and data selection approaches. The augmented data will be used in conjunction with real-world data to simulate a real-world quality estimation setting, allowing us to evaluate the robustness and adaptability of quality estimators to different types of input data.
CONTROLS: We will compare the effectiveness of our quality-aware augmentation module with standard data augmentation techniques and with simulated data augmentation using a randomly initialized quality estimator.
COST: 4500
PREDICTION: The inclusion of the quality-aware augmentation module will significantly enhance the realism and simulation of a real-world evaluation setting, enabling more accurate assessments of quality estimators' performance and guidance for their improvement; however, it might introduce new challenges and discrepancies with how real-world data selection is typically performed, which could affect some approaches' evaluation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating a Pretraining Paradigm for Minimal Informativeness Domains
PROPOSAL: To identify scenarios where quality-based pretraining data selection might not be beneficial, we propose to investigate how models pretrain on minimal informativeness domains (MIDs), such as datasets consisting mainly of extreme instances of a particular attribute or bias-laden data. We will pretrain models on MID datasets with a quality estimator that distinguishes between high-quality and low-quality examples and compare their performance to those pretraining on conventionally selected datasets. We hypothesize that pretraining on MID datasets with a quality-aware model might exacerbate any pre-existing biases in the data and result in poorer downstream performance.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to pretraining on MID datasets without quality awareness, as well as pretraining on conventional datasets with and without quality estimation. Additionally, we will investigate whether augmenting the MID datasets with noise or paired examples can help mitigate the negative effects of pretraining on these data.
COST: 6300
PREDICTION: Pretraining on MID datasets with a quality estimator will significantly exacerbate any pre-existing biases in the data, resulting in poorer downstream performance compared to pretraining on conventionally selected or conventional MID datasets; however, the specific behaviors and outcomes will likely depend both on the specific MID data employed and on the chosen pretraining paradigm.

TITLE: Investigating a Hierarchical Selection Approach for Multilingual Data
PROPOSAL: We will enhance the initial hierarchical model-based approach for quality estimation by incorporating a transfer learning module that enables the adaptation of the language-agnostic quality estimator to new languages using few-shot learning. This transfer learning component will consist of a multi-task learning framework, where the model learns to predict quality scores across multiple languages simultaneously, leveraging its existing knowledge to adapt to new languages with minimal additional training data. Additionally, we will evaluate the hierarchical approach in a contrastive learning framework to augment the data selection process with robustness to variations in text.
CONTROLS: We will compare our enhanced hierarchical approach with the initial version, as well as with state-of-the-art few-shot learning methods and traditional quality estimation approaches without transfer learning or contrastive learning.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: The enhanced hierarchical approach with transfer learning and contrastive learning components will further improve its adaptability across languages, effectiveness in selecting high-quality pretraining data, and robustness to variations in text, potentially leading to better downstream performance of LLMs in multiple languages. However, the success of few-shot learning depends significantly on the applicability and quality of the initial training data, and over-reliance on transfer learning might limit the capacity of the model to learn unique linguistic patterns.

PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a novel attention mechanism, QualityAwareAttention, which integrates quality estimation directly into the self-attention mechanism of a transformer-based language model, thereby aiding in better data utilization and avoiding noise and repetitive content during pretraining. This method will help weight the input tokens and contextualize them based on their quality scores, allowing the model to better distinguish between informative and shallow data, enabling improved generalization and effectiveness in downstream NLP tasks.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate QualityAwareAttention using a set of quality-aware quality estimators and compare its results to transformer-based models pre-trained with standard attention mechanisms, as well as other self-supervised learning techniques.

By integrating MID-aware quality estimators into the pretraining loop, our model will gain the capability to automatically adapt to situations where the training data exhibits subtle patterns indicative of MID-bias, leading to improved downstream performance and enhanced interpretability. PROPOSAL: Building on the current understanding and proposals, we will aim to develop a broad and general framework for transferable quality estimation that generalizes across different domain settings. ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Evaluation Metric Divergence in Multilingual Data Selection 
PROPOSAL: 
We investigate how evaluation metrics, commonly used in selecting high-quality pretraining data, may diverge across languages, affecting the ability of model-based data selection strategies to effectively remove low-quality data. We examine the similarity of BLEU and METEOR scores, as well as the implications for spans-based phrase extractors, across dense and sparsely represented languages (e.g., English, Yoruba, Nepali, Japanese). We design and implement a theoretical analysis of metric correlation, specifically deriving bounds for BLEU and METEOR similarity using language model interpretability techniques. We apply this theoretical framework to empirical evaluation, where we collect linguistic annotations in test sets for non-English languages.
CONTROLS: 
We compare our results to a baseline that uses simple heuristics (e.g., word length, token frequency) to estimate quality divergence, and we evaluate the robustness of our approach to changes in pretraining data distributions and evaluation tasks.
COST: 10700

PREDICTION: This revised experiment will provide a more nuanced understanding of evaluation metric divergence, highlighting potential biases in existing methods and suggesting directions for improvement. However, it may face challenges in generalizing to diverse linguistic contexts and tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multilingual Adversarial Training for Data Selection
PROPOSAL: 
We develop a novel approach to training data selectors by incorporating multilingual adversarial training, where the goal is to learn a discriminator that can distinguish between high-quality and low-quality data in multiple languages simultaneously. We use a variational autoencoder (VAE) framework to represent the data and its quality, allowing for sensitive and fine-grained quality scores. We generate adversarial examples using the gradients of the discriminator's output, and update the selector's parameters to minimize the difference between the predicted quality and the true quality. We evaluate our approach on a multilingual web crawl dataset, including languages such as Chinese, Arabic, and Hindi.
CONTROLS: 
We compare our results to a baseline that uses a simple binary classifier, and we examine the effect of varying the number of languages and the complexity of the training data on the selector's performance.
COST: 18000

PREDICTION: This method will demonstrate strong performance in learning a shared quality representation across multiple languages, improving the selector's ability to adapt to new languages and reduce bias. However, it may be computationally expensive to train and may require careful hyperparameter tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multitask Learning for Multilingual Data Quality Estimation
PROPOSAL: 
We explore the use of multitask learning to improve multilingual data quality estimation by jointly training models to predict multiple related tasks, including sentence-level quality scores, document-level quality scores, and task-specific performance metrics. We design a shared encoder-decoder architecture that learns to extract relevant features from the input text and uses task-specific heads to predict the corresponding output. We evaluate our approach on a multilingual dataset, including tasks such as sentiment analysis, question-answering, and language modeling. We also investigate the effect of varying the number of tasks and the importance of each task on the model's performance.
CONTROLS: 
We compare our results to a baseline that trains a separate model for each task, and we examine the effect of using different types of multitask learning, such as hard parameter sharing and soft parameter sharing.
COST: 21000

PREDICTION: This approach will demonstrate strong performance in predicting multiple tasks simultaneously, improving the model's ability to capture nuanced quality relationships and reducing the need for task-specific fine-tuning. However, it may require careful hyperparameter tuning to balance the importance of each task, and may be computationally expensive to train.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Few-Shot Learning for Zero-Shot Data Selection in Multilingual Settings
PROPOSAL: 
We investigate the use of few-shot learning techniques to enable zero-shot data selection in multilingual settings, where the task is to evaluate the quality of unseen languages or domains without any explicit supervision. We propose a meta-learning framework that learns to adapt a pre-trained data selector to new languages or domains with only a few examples. We use a prototypical networks-based approach to learn a knowledge graph that captures the relationships between languages and domains, and use this graph to guide the adaptation process. We evaluate our approach on a range of multilingual datasets, including languages with limited resources and domains with varying levels of quality.
CONTROLS: 
We compare our results to a baseline that uses a traditional supervised learning approach, and we examine the effect of varying the number of shots and the complexity of the adaptation task on the model's performance.
COST: 27000

PREDICTION: This approach will demonstrate strong performance in zero-shot data selection, enabling efficient adaptation to new languages and domains with limited resources. However, it may require careful tuning of the meta-learning schedule and the prototypical networks architecture to achieve optimal performance.

TITLE: Axiomatic Framework for Multilingual Data Quality Evaluation
PROPOSAL: 
We develop an axiomatic framework for evaluating the quality of multilingual data, providing a theoretical foundation for data quality assessment across languages and domains. We define a set of axioms that capture fundamental properties of data quality, such as coherency, consistency, and relevance, and demonstrate that these axioms are sufficient to guarantee the existence of a unique data quality evaluation function. We also show that this function can be learned as a multilingual metric, allowing for efficient evaluation of data quality in diverse language settings.
CONTROLS: 
We compare our results to a baseline that uses existing metrics for data quality evaluation, and we examine the effect of varying the number of axioms and the complexity of the evaluation task on the model's performance.
COST: 30000

PREDICTION: This approach will provide a rigorous theoretical foundation for multilingual data quality evaluation, enabling accurate and fair assessment of data quality across languages and domains. However, it may require careful tuning of the axiomatic framework and the evaluation metric to capture the nuances of data quality in diverse language settings.

TITLE: Evaluation Metric Divergence in Multilingual Data Selection 
PROPOSAL: 
We investigate how evaluation metrics, commonly used in selecting high-quality pretraining data, may diverge across languages, affecting the ability of model-based data selection strategies to effectively remove low-quality data. We examine the similarity of BLEU and METEOR scores, as well as the implications for spans-based phrase extractors, across dense and sparsely represented languages (e.g., English, Yoruba, Nepali, Japanese). We design and implement a theoretical analysis of metric correlation, specifically deriving bounds for BLEU and METEOR similarity using language model interpretability techniques. We apply this theoretical framework to empirical evaluation, where we collect linguistic annotations in test sets for non-English languages.
CONTROLS: 
We compare our results to a baseline that uses simple heuristics (e.g., word length, token frequency) to estimate quality divergence, and we evaluate the robustness of our approach to changes in pretraining data distributions and evaluation tasks.
COST: 32000

PREDICTION: This revised experiment will provide a more nuanced understanding of evaluation metric divergence, highlighting potential biases in existing methods and suggesting directions for improvement. However, it may face challenges in generalizing to diverse linguistic contexts and tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multilingual Adversarial Training for Data Selection
PROPOSAL: 
We develop a novel approach to training data selectors by incorporating multilingual adversarial training, where the goal is to learn a discriminator that can distinguish between high-quality and low-quality data in multiple languages simultaneously. We use a variational autoencoder (VAE) framework to represent the data and its quality, allowing for sensitive and fine-grained quality scores. We generate adversarial examples using the gradients of the discriminator's output, and update the selector's parameters to minimize the difference between the predicted quality and the true quality. We evaluate our approach on a multilingual web crawl dataset, including languages such as Chinese, Arabic, and Hindi.
CONTROLS: 
We compare our results to a baseline that uses a simple binary classifier, and we examine the effect of varying the number of languages and the complexity of the training data on the selector's performance.
COST: 54000

PREDICTION: This method will demonstrate strong performance in learning a shared quality representation across multiple languages, improving the selector's ability to adapt to new languages and reduce bias. However, it may be computationally expensive to train and may require careful hyperparameter tuning.

TITLE: Multitask Learning for Multilingual Data Quality Estimation
PROPOSAL: 
We explore the use of multitask learning to improve multilingual data quality estimation by jointly training models to predict multiple related tasks, including sentence-level quality scores, document-level quality scores, and task-specific performance metrics. We design a shared encoder-decoder architecture that learns to extract relevant features from the input text and uses task-specific heads to predict the corresponding output. We evaluate our approach on a multilingual dataset, including tasks such as sentiment analysis, question-answering, and language modeling. We also investigate the effect of varying the number of tasks and the importance of each task on the model's performance.
CONTROLS: 
We compare our results to a baseline that trains a separate model for each task, and we examine the effect of using different types of multitask learning, such as hard parameter sharing and soft parameter sharing.

PREDICTION: This approach will demonstrate strong performance in predicting multiple tasks simultaneously, improving the model's ability to capture nuanced quality relationships and reducing the need for task-specific fine-tuning. However, it may require careful hyperparameter tuning to balance the importance of each task, and may be computationally expensive to train.

We propose a meta-learning framework that learns to adapt a pre-trained data selector to new languages or domains with only a few examples. TITLE: Experimental Framework for Geometry-Appearance Latents
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel 3D representation framework, combining a grid-based latent with a learned appearance module. The latent will be trained using the PartNet dataset for 3D object reconstruction. The appearance module will leverage the StyleGAN2 architecture and be conditioned on the latent's spatial coordinates and view direction. The framework will be trained end-to-end on the PartNet training set, evaluating performance on the PartNet validation set.
CONTROLS: We will run ablations comparing our proposed framework against a baseline using only the grid-based latent without the appearance module. Additionally, we will compare our results against state-of-the-art geometry-only reconstruction methods.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Our framework should outperform the baseline and geometry-only reconstruction methods on PartNet validation set benchmarks, demonstrating improved accuracy in capturing view-dependent appearance. However, it may struggle with objects exhibiting complex reflections or subtle material property changes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Experimental Framework for Geometry-Appearance Latents
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel 3D representation framework, combining a grid-based latent with a learned appearance module. The latent will be trained using the PartNet dataset for 3D object reconstruction. The appearance module will leverage the StyleGAN2 architecture and be conditioned on the latent's spatial coordinates and view direction. The framework will be trained end-to-end on the PartNet training set, evaluating performance on the PartNet validation set.
CONTROLS: We will run ablations comparing our proposed framework against a baseline using only the grid-based latent without the appearance module. Additionally, we will compare our results against state-of-the-art geometry-only reconstruction methods.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: Our framework should outperform the baseline and geometry-only reconstruction methods on PartNet validation set benchmarks, demonstrating improved accuracy in capturing view-dependent appearance. However, it may struggle with objects exhibiting complex reflections or subtle material property changes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Impact of View Dependence on Geometry-Only Representations
PROPOSAL: We propose an experiment to evaluate how state-of-the-art geometry-only 3D representations, such as Occupancy Networks (ONet) and DeepSDF, handle view-dependent geometry and appearance variations using the ShapeNetCore dataset. We will train these models on a diverse set of view-dependent scenes and assess their performance on novel view prediction and view-dependent accuracy metrics.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of ONet and DeepSDF against our proposed framework in the 1st proposal and against other state-of-the-art geometry-only representations. We will also analyze the effects of varying the number of views in the training set and the complexity of view-dependent geometry on the performance of these geometry-only representations.
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: This experiment should reveal that while geometry-only representations can handle some view-dependent effects, they may struggle with more complex reflections and subtle material property changes, motivating the need for joint geometry-appearance representations. However, the outcome might be nuanced, and their performance could be surprisingly robust in certain regimes.

We will analyze the trade-off between spatial resolution, memory efficiency, and view-dependent accuracy.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the framework with varying grid resolutions against state-of-the-art geometry-only representations and against our proposed framework without the appearance module.

PREDICTION: This experiment should reveal that a higher grid resolution can improve view-dependent accuracy but comes at the cost of increased memory consumption. This trade-off may limit the applicability of our proposed framework to certain scenarios with strict memory constraints. However, it might also expose a fundamental bottleneck in current 3D representations, driving research towards more efficient data structures.

PROPOSAL: We revise our proposed framework to incorporate knowledge distillation, where we train a smaller, more efficient appearance module as a student network to mimic the output of a pre-trained, larger teacher network. This should help improve the generalization of the framework to unseen data and reduce the computational cost. We will evaluate its performance on the PartNet validation set, comparing it against the original framework and state-of-the-art geometry-only representations.

However, it may also limit the framework's ability to capture very complex view-dependent effects, potentially requiring further research into more sophisticated knowledge distillation techniques.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unsupervised Joint 3D Geometry and View-Dependent Appearance Learning using Implicit VAEs
PROPOSAL: We propose to use a hierarchical architecture of Implicit Variational Autoencoders (IVAEs) to concurrently learn a compact 3D latent representation of object geometry and view-dependent appearance from real-world images of objects under diverse lighting conditions. IVAEs will be trained on a large real-world dataset (e.g. NYU Depth V2, ShapeNet, LINEMOD) to output both a probabilistic occupancy field representing the object's surface geometry and a multiview diffusion map encoding the object's view-dependent material properties. By jointly learning geometry and appearance in a probabilistic framework, we aim to capture nuanced view-dependent effects and achieve higher fidelity object reconstructions compared to current state-of-the-art models.
CONTROLS: We will consider ablation studies of our proposed IVAE architecture by (1) comparing to standard IVAEs that only learn a 3D latent representation of geometry, (2) evaluating our hierarchical IVAE against other recent works that jointly learn geometry and appearance but lack probabilistic outputs for material properties, and (3) examining the impact of adding a simple two-stage refinement process for sharpening geometry and material details from the IVAE's probabilistic outputs.
COST: 1680
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our IVAE model will generate high-quality 3D reconstructions that reflect view-dependent effects such as subtle material changes and nuanced lighting interactions, as we will leverage the power of probabilistic representations for material properties; however, accurately modeling intricate details and environmental effects (e.g. complex lighting conditions, real-world occlusions) could prove challenging.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving Image-to-3D Asset Generation with Physics-Informed Metrics
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a new set of physics-informed metrics to evaluate and improve image-to-3D asset generation models. By leveraging the simulation power of physics engines, we will define a suite of metrics that assess the accuracy of generated 3D assets in terms of physical properties such as conserving mass, respecting material properties, and accurately modeling light transport. These metrics will be used to guide model training and evaluation, driving generation towards more realistic and accurate 3D assets. As a feasibility study, we will integrate our metrics with a popular image-to-3D model (e.g. NeRF) and evaluate its improved performance on well-known benchmarks in 3D object reconstruction and asset generation.
CONTROLS: To ensure our physics-informed metrics are effective, we will compare their impact to traditional evaluation metrics (e.g. 3D IoU, depth accuracy) and regularized training with simple accuracy objectives only.
COST: 2340
PREDICTION: We expect our physics-informed metrics to improve the accuracy of generated 3D assets significantly, especially in terms of physical properties such as mass conservation and material interaction; however, accurately modeling complex light transport and mirroring might still require rigorous physics-based optimization procedures.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: ViewPOINT: View-Dependent Perception for 3D Object Reconstruction and Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop ViewPOINT, a novel 3D reconstruction and generation framework that incorporates view-dependent perception. By incorporating multiple views of an object under varying lighting conditions, ViewPOINT learns a comprehensive representation of an object's geometry and view-dependent appearance. Specifically, ViewPOINT will utilize a dynamic neural architecture that adapts to the input image, incorporating view-dependent information to selectively focus on specific aspects of an object's appearance. This ability to perceive an object from multiple viewpoints will allow ViewPOINT to generate highly realistic and accurate 3D reconstructions and objects.
CONTROLS: To examine the impact of view-dependent perception on 3D reconstruction and generation, we will compare ViewPOINT against several recent works that only consider a single viewpoint or lack view-dependent perception, and we will also explore ViewPOINT's applicability to different scenarios such as object manipulation and tracking.
COST: 4681.83
PREDICTION: We anticipate that ViewPOINT's view-dependent perception mechanism will significantly improve the accuracy of 3D reconstructions and generated objects, allowing it to capture nuanced details and lighting interactions that current models often fail to capture; however, the added complexity and computational cost of ViewPOINT may impede its real-time performance and applicability to more complex scenarios.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Unsupervised Joint 3D Geometry and View-Dependent Appearance Learning using Implicit VAEs
PROPOSAL: We refine our previous IVAE proposal by introducing a novel "appearance-conditioned" reconstruction loss function, which aligns the generated view-dependent appearance with the target view-dependent appearance in the input image. Specifically, the proposed loss function will compare the predicted material properties and view-dependent texture of the generated object to those extracted from the input image. This loss function, combined with the probabilistic nature of IVAEs, will allow our model to learn more accurate view-dependent appearance and reduce the domain gap between generated and real-world objects.
CONTROLS: To validate the effectiveness of our appearance-conditioned loss, we will compare our refined IVAE model against its original version and recent works that lack this loss function, on benchmark datasets like ShapeNet and NYU Depth V2.
COST: 1731.6
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our appearance-conditioned reconstruction loss will lead to more accurate view-dependent appearance and reduced domain gap, resulting in improved generated 3D objects that better reflect the target view-dependent effects; however, its sensitivity to noise and variability in material properties may require careful tuning and handling.

TITLE: Understanding the Role of Texture and Shape Silhouettes in View-Dependent 3D Object Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We propose an in-depth investigation into the importance of texture and shape silhouettes in view-dependent 3D object reconstruction. By systematically manipulating and analyzing these factors in a series of controlled experiments, we aim to quantify their respective contributions to the quality of generated 3D reconstructions and gain insights into the underlying mechanisms driving view-dependent appearance capture. Specifically, we will design an experimental protocol to evaluate the influence of texture, shape silhouettes, and their interactions on the reconstruction accuracy of state-of-the-art view-dependent 3D generation models (e.g. ViewPOINT).
CONTROLS: To isolate the effects of texture and shape silhouettes, we will conduct a series of ablation studies, voxel-level texture manipulations, andятиlation uncertainties related to the shape silhouette information.
COST: 2700
PREDICTION: We expect our analysis to reveal that texture and shape silhouettes play complex and interrelated roles in view-dependent 3D reconstruction, with texture primarily affecting subtle appearance details and shape silhouettes influencing the overall shape coherence; however, accurately modeling complex shape and texture interactions may require careful fusion of multiple cues and possibly specialized neural architectures.

TITLE: Improving Image-to-3D Asset Generation with Physics-Informed Metrics
PROPOSAL: We refine our previous proposal by incorporating a novel "phasor invariant" metric, which assesses the accuracy of generated 3D assets in terms of their ability to replicate the material interactions and light transport seen in the input image. By leveraging carefully designed phasor invariance principles, this metric will provide a more nuanced evaluation of the generated objects' ability to mimic real-world properties like light reflection, refraction, and diffusion. This improved metric will be used to fine-tune our image-to-3D generation model, enabling it to produce 3D assets that better capture the intricacies of real-world material interactions.
CONTROLS: To validate the effectiveness of our phasor invariant metric, we will compare the performance of our refined model to its original version and other recent works that use traditional physics-informed metrics, on benchmark datasets like ShapeNet and LINEMOD.
COST: 1620
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our phasor invariant metric will significantly enhance the accuracy of generated 3D objects, allowing them to better replicate real-world material interactions and light transport; however, accurately modeling complex optical effects may require specialized neural networks and computational resources.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unsupervised Joint 3D Geometry and View-Dependent Appearance Learning using Implicit VAEs
PROPOSAL: We propose to use a hierarchical architecture of Implicit Variational Autoencoders (IVAEs) to concurrently learn a compact 3D latent representation of object geometry and view-dependent appearance from real-world images of objects under diverse lighting conditions. IVAEs will be trained on a large real-world dataset (e.g. NYU Depth V2, ShapeNet, LINEMOD) to output both a probabilistic occupancy field representing the object's surface geometry and a multiview diffusion map encoding the object's view-dependent material properties. By jointly learning geometry and appearance in a probabilistic framework, we aim to capture nuanced view-dependent effects and achieve higher fidelity object reconstructions compared to current state-of-the-art models.
CONTROLS: We will consider ablation studies of our proposed IVAE architecture by (1) comparing to standard IVAEs that only learn a 3D latent representation of geometry, (2) evaluating our hierarchical IVAE against other recent works that jointly learn geometry and appearance but lack probabilistic outputs for material properties, and (3) examining the impact of adding a simple two-stage refinement process for sharpening geometry and material details from the IVAE's probabilistic outputs.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our IVAE model will generate high-quality 3D reconstructions that reflect view-dependent effects such as subtle material changes and nuanced lighting interactions, as we will leverage the power of probabilistic representations for material properties; however, accurately modeling intricate details and environmental effects (e.g. complex lighting conditions, real-world occlusions) could prove challenging.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving Image-to-3D Asset Generation with Physics-Informed Metrics
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop a new set of physics-informed metrics to evaluate and improve image-to-3D asset generation models. By leveraging the simulation power of physics engines, we will define a suite of metrics that assess the accuracy of generated 3D assets in terms of physical properties such as conserving mass, respecting material properties, and accurately modeling light transport. These metrics will be used to guide model training and evaluation, driving generation towards more realistic and accurate 3D assets. As a feasibility study, we will integrate our metrics with a popular image-to-3D model (e.g. NeRF) and evaluate its improved performance on well-known benchmarks in 3D object reconstruction and asset generation.
CONTROLS: To ensure our physics-informed metrics are effective, we will compare their impact to traditional evaluation metrics (e.g. 3D IoU, depth accuracy) and regularized training with simple accuracy objectives only.
COST: 7000
PREDICTION: We expect our physics-informed metrics to improve the accuracy of generated 3D assets significantly, especially in terms of physical properties such as mass conservation and material interaction; however, accurately modeling complex light transport and mirroring might still require rigorous physics-based optimization procedures.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: ViewPOINT: View-Dependent Perception for 3D Object Reconstruction and Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose to develop ViewPOINT, a novel 3D reconstruction and generation framework that incorporates view-dependent perception. By incorporating multiple views of an object under varying lighting conditions, ViewPOINT learns a comprehensive representation of an object's geometry and view-dependent appearance. Specifically, ViewPOINT will utilize a dynamic neural architecture that adapts to the input image, incorporating view-dependent information to selectively focus on specific aspects of an object's appearance. This ability to perceive an object from multiple viewpoints will allow ViewPOINT to generate highly realistic and accurate 3D reconstructions and objects.
CONTROLS: To examine the impact of view-dependent perception on 3D reconstruction and generation, we will compare ViewPOINT against several recent works that only consider a single viewpoint or lack view-dependent perception, and we will also explore ViewPOINT's applicability to different scenarios such as object manipulation and tracking.
COST: 14000
PREDICTION: We anticipate that ViewPOINT's view-dependent perception mechanism will significantly improve the accuracy of 3D reconstructions and generated objects, allowing it to capture nuanced details and lighting interactions that current models often fail to capture; however, the added complexity and computational cost of ViewPOINT may impede its real-time performance and applicability to more complex scenarios.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Unsupervised Joint 3D Geometry and View-Dependent Appearance Learning using Implicit VAEs
PROPOSAL: We refine our previous IVAE proposal by introducing a novel "appearance-conditioned" reconstruction loss function, which aligns the generated view-dependent appearance with the target view-dependent appearance in the input image. Specifically, the proposed loss function will compare the predicted material properties and view-dependent texture of the generated object to those extracted from the input image. This loss function, combined with the probabilistic nature of IVAEs, will allow our model to learn more accurate view-dependent appearance and reduce the domain gap between generated and real-world objects.
CONTROLS: To validate the effectiveness of our appearance-conditioned loss, we will compare our refined IVAE model against its original version and recent works that lack this loss function, on benchmark datasets like ShapeNet and NYU Depth V2.
COST: 5200
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our appearance-conditioned reconstruction loss will lead to more accurate view-dependent appearance and reduced domain gap, resulting in improved generated 3D objects that better reflect the target view-dependent effects; however, its sensitivity to noise and variability in material properties may require careful tuning and handling.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding the Role of Texture and Shape Silhouettes in View-Dependent 3D Object Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We propose an in-depth investigation into the importance of texture and shape silhouettes in view-dependent 3D object reconstruction. By systematically manipulating and analyzing these factors in a series of controlled experiments, we aim to quantify their respective contributions to the quality of generated 3D reconstructions and gain insights into the underlying mechanisms driving view-dependent appearance capture. Specifically, we will design an experimental protocol to evaluate the influence of texture, shape silhouettes, and their interactions on the reconstruction accuracy of state-of-the-art view-dependent 3D generation models (e.g. ViewPOINT).
CONTROLS: To isolate the effects of texture and shape silhouettes, we will conduct a series of ablation studies, voxel-level texture manipulations, andятиlation uncertainties related to the shape silhouette information.
COST: 8000
PREDICTION: We expect our analysis to reveal that texture and shape silhouettes play complex and interrelated roles in view-dependent 3D reconstruction, with texture primarily affecting subtle appearance details and shape silhouettes influencing the overall shape coherence; however, accurately modeling complex shape and texture interactions may require careful fusion of multiple cues and possibly specialized neural architectures.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Improving Image-to-3D Asset Generation with Physics-Informed Metrics
PROPOSAL: We refine our previous proposal by incorporating a novel "phasor invariant" metric, which assesses the accuracy of generated 3D assets in terms of their ability to replicate the material interactions and light transport seen in the input image. By leveraging carefully designed phasor invariance principles, this metric will provide a more nuanced evaluation of the generated objects' ability to mimic real-world properties like light reflection, refraction, and diffusion. This improved metric will be used to fine-tune our image-to-3D generation model, enabling it to produce 3D assets that better capture the intricacies of real-world material interactions.
CONTROLS: To validate the effectiveness of our phasor invariant metric, we will compare the performance of our refined model to its original version and other recent works that use traditional physics-informed metrics, on benchmark datasets like ShapeNet and LINEMOD.
COST: 4900
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our phasor invariant metric will significantly enhance the accuracy of generated 3D objects, allowing them to better replicate real-world material interactions and light transport; however, accurately modeling complex optical effects may require specialized neural networks and computational resources.

By using a learned-to-capture differentiable physics engine, eyegeneration will facilitate the efficient integration of view-dependent appearance and material properties, allowing it to generate high-quality 3D objects in real-time. This renderer will be used in conjunction with our previously proposed methods (e.g. IVAEs, ViewPOINT) to achieve improved performance and accuracy.

PREDICTION: We anticipate that eyegeneration will enable real-time 3D object generation with photorealistic appearance capture, while also facilitating the efficient integration of view-dependent material properties; however, accurately modeling complex material interactions and lighting effects may require specialized neural networks and significant computational resources.

PROPOSAL: Introduce a geometry-appearance alignment (GAA) loss function that encourages the geometry and appearance encoders to capture consistent information about object geometry. During training, compute the GAA loss between the output of the geometry decoder and the appearance renderer conditioned on the estimated 3D points. This should help improve the overall consistency of the learned representation.
CONTROLS: Evaluate GAA loss with and without geometry decoder + appearance encoder combination as in proposal 1, and examine the impact of GAA loss on geometry reconstruction accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: RefineMPI-NeRF: Improved Neural Radiance Fields for 3D Reconstruction with View-Dependent Appearance
PROPOSAL: We experiment with a combination of Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) and Multiresolution Pose Inference (MPI) to improve upon the baseline performance of late-time message passing on dense voxel grids for 3D reconstruction. NeRF is employed for capturing the view-dependent appearance of objects, while MPI enables efficient and compact spatial hierarchy inference for refining point clouds. We test this combination on a benchmark consisting of three datasets (ShapeNet, LSUN Chair, and IKEA) using metrics like location error, leaning error, and depth accuracy. For ablation study, we remove the NeRF component or disable MPI to observe individual contributions.
CONTROLS: Baselines are point clouds inferred by NeRF only, HRR-GEO net with primitive-based representations, and SING devolving to geometry-only rendering; ablated models have either NeRF or MPI disabled.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: Improving upon the baseline, our method RefineMPI-NeRF will achieve location errors below 1.5, leaning errors below 1, and depth accuracy around 95%, while also successfully capturing view-dependent effects like reflections and highlights in object appearance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Occupancy Aggregation for Multi-View 3D Scene Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We propose a new method to integrate occupancy information from multiple views to reconstruct 3D scenes with richer and more accurate geometry. Using a probabilistic occupancy aggregation network, we combine signed distance fields from different views while accounting for uncertainty in the signed distance estimates. This network is trained using a variant of the Chamfer distance as a loss function, and we compare its performance against state-of-the-art methods such as SC-FEGS and octPassive- Fusion on multiple real-world datasets (e.g. the Roy et al dataset and the real-world ScanNet freespaceChallenge).
CONTROLS: Baselines include SC-FEGS, octPassive-Fusion and geometry-occlusion inpainting from raw scans.
COST: 36000
PREDICTION: Our method will significantly outperform SC-FEGS and octPassive-Fusion on both Chamfer and iChamfer distance metrics, showcasing robust and accurate 3D scene reconstruction while providing a new approach to scale up to real-world variants and unruly real-world challenges.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stereopsis in Neural Radiance Fields: Learning Monocular 3D Reconstruction from Images and Depth Maps
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel framework for monocular 3D reconstruction using neural radiance fields, combining the strengths of NeRF and depth map learning. Our method, called SRNRF, predicts depth maps and neural radiance fields jointly from a single image, relying on a multi-task learning architecture that incorporates a depth prediction branch into the NeRF pipeline. We evaluate SRNRF on a new benchmark of real-world images with depth annotations and compare its performance to state-of-the-art monocular depth estimation and 3D reconstruction methods, including Deep3DV2, MiDAS, and NeRF-Vrising.
CONTROLS: Baselines include Deep3DV2 for depth estimation, NeRF-Vrising for monocular 3D reconstruction, and the geometry-only rendering of NeRF models.
COST: 240000
PREDICTION: Our proposed SRNRF will provide more accurate 3D reconstructions and depth maps than existing methods, achieving state-of-the-art results with an average depth accuracy of 95% and an average 3D reconstructions IoU of 85%, while improving over baselines in both metrics. However, it may struggle with scenes featuring complex geometry and slow motions.

TITLE: ContourNet: A Learning-based Approach for Extracting Accurate Contours from Single Images
PROPOSAL: We present a learning-based approach, ContourNet, that aims to recover accurate semantic contours from single images of real-world objects. ContourNet leverages a multi-scale architecture and a novel loss function that balances contour accuracy, smoothness, and completion to extract high-quality contours even from images with occlusions or poor lighting conditions. We train and evaluate ContourNet on edited contours datasets and compare its performance against state-of-the-art methods such as Perceptual Generator Contours (PGC) and fully-connected Conditional Random Fields (fCRF).
CONTROLS: Baselines include PGC for contour extraction, fCRF for contour completion, and geometry-only rendering of traditional algorithms (EdgeMap, JLinv, eNet).

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Generalizable 3D Reconstruction via Meta-Learned Neural Radiance Fields
PROPOSAL: We propose a meta-learning approach for generalizable 3D reconstruction using neural radiance fields. Our method, MetaNeRF, utilizes a meta-learning framework that trains a neural radiance field to recognize and adapt to unseen object classes, rendering scenes, and viewpoints. We evaluate MetaNeRF on a diverse set of datasets, including ShapeNet, ModelNet, and SUNCG, comparing its performance against state-of-the-art methods and assessing its generalizability across various object classes and scenes.
CONTROLS: Baselines include RefineMPI-NeRF, Stereopsis in Neural Radiance Fields, and traditional 3D mesh reconstruction methods.
COST: 400000
PREDICTION: MetaNeRF will demonstrate excellent generalizability and robustness across various object classes, scenes, and viewpoints, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in 3D reconstruction and viewpoint inference tasks, while requiring minimal fine-tuning for unseen scenes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Decomposing Latent 3D Representations with Unsupervised Texture Synthesis
PROPOSAL: We design a three-stage pipeline: (i) train a latent 3D representation that captures geometry only, using a LiDAR-scanned dataset like ScanNet; (ii) synthesize textures for reconstructed 3D objects using an unsupervised texture synthesis model, such as Bicycle GAN; (iii) train the original latent 3D model to predict RGB appearance jointly with its geometry, conditioned on the synthesized textures. In each stage, we focus on optimizing one objective: geometry only, texture only, and joint geometry-appearance, respectively.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach against existing geometry-only representations (e.g., PointNet) and appearance-conditioned generation (e.g., I2CAD), while ablating the unsupervised texture synthesis stage to validate its contribution.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: Our decomposition approach should improve joint geometry-appearance reconstruction over existing methods, given the dedicated stages for optimizing each objective. However, it may overfit to texture synthesis if not carefully regularized, causing the joint stage to focus too much on appearance at expense of geometry. We expect it to fail if the texture synthesis quality is subpar or if the geometry-only latent representation underfits the original task.

TITLE: Improving View-Dependent Effects in Latent 3D Representations with Neural Rendering
PROPOSAL: We introduce a second-stage neural rendering module that refines the rendered radiance fields (RFs) of objects reconstructed from our decomposed latent representation (proposal 1) by warping the images according to the target view and lighting conditions. This refinement uses a template-based rendering technique and is trained on a dataset with varied viewpoints and lighting conditions, similar to NeRF-W. We further incorporate a hints mechanism from a learned inverse graphics model (IG-FNN) to estimate ground truth reflective geometry and material properties.
CONTROLS: We compare our two-stage approach against standard latent 3D models with additional neural rendering (e.g., Occupancy Networks) and focus-ABL-NeRF with ablation on the hints mechanism.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Our approach should produce state-of-the-art results on capturing view-dependent effects, especially reflections and highlights. However, it may suffer due to the high dimensionality of learned representations and embossed hints that are required to account for intricate geometry, compromising sensitivity to the hints from ligraphics assuming conditions our learned model might underfit.
