ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Latent 3D Scene Understanding with a Rendering-to-Sketch Pipeline
PROPOSAL: We propose a refinement of our previous proposal, where we integrate a rendering-based inference mechanism with a graph-based 3D scene understanding network to jointly infer the 3D layout and geometry of real-world scenes. Our approach outputs a compact and differentiable representation that can be effectively optimized using gradient-based methods. We focus on leveraging our differentiable renderer (Focus) to regress the sketch-based generative model's outputs, to better capture view-dependent effects.
CONTROLS: We train and evaluate our pipeline using datasets like Pix3D and facade datasets with real-world view-dependent semantic labels, comparing against state-of-the-art 3D scene understanding models.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Our revised pipeline should achieve significant improvements in scene understanding and 3D geometry reconstruction, particularly under heavy occlusions and view-dependent effects. However, it may struggle with scenes containing highly textured or reflective surfaces, compromising the quality of the inferred 3D layout.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rig- Reformulation and Kinematic-Constrained Geometry Optimization
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to improve the quality and realism of 3D reconstructions by incorporating kinematic constraints and a learned rig representation. Our model, RK-Gen, learns to predict the underlying kinematic structure of the object (e.g., joints, bones) and optimizes the geometry using a dynamic rig system. This reformulates the traditional geometry-only optimization problem into a hybrid kinematic-geometry one, enabling more realistic deformations and occlusions.
CONTROLS: We compare RK-Gen against state-of-the-art methods for 3D reconstruction and kinematic modeling, evaluating on datasets like T-Home and KAIST Human-Object Interaction, while ablating the kinematic constraint to validate its contribution.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: Our approach should significantly improve the quality and realism of 3D reconstructions, particularly in scenes involving complex kinematics and occlusions. However, it may require large training datasets to accurately learn the kinematic structure and may struggle with scenes where the kinematic assumptions do not hold.

TITLE: Interactive 3D Generation with Physics-Aware Neural Rendering
PROPOSAL: We refine our previous proposal to better integrate physics-aware neural rendering with interactive 3D generation. Our revised model, PNR-Gen+, learns to predict the physics of the scene and generates realistic 3D reconstructions that respond to user interactions. PNR-Gen+ consists of a neural rendering module that takes into account the physics of the scene and a physics-aware optimization module that refines the generated 3D model. Additionally, we incorporate a learned rendering-to-synthesis pipeline to enhance the visual quality of the generated scenes.

We focus on leveraging our differentiable renderer (Focus) to regress the sketch-based generative model's outputs, to better capture view-dependent effects.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Direct One-Step Generator via Contraction Mapping
PROPOSAL: Investigate using contraction mapping to prove that a one-step generator exists such that its output distribution matches the teacher AR model's distribution. Specifically, we will define a point-to-set mapping in the space of token sequences and show that it is a contraction mapping. Using this, we will derive a unique fixed point that represents the one-step generator, thus obtaining a theoretical guarantee on the possibility of achieving one-step sampling without predefined noise-to-data mapping.
CONTROLS: This proposal will be compared against the performance of Direct One-Step Generator via Neural Network Optimization.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: This theoretical result will successfully prove the existence of a one-step generator, but its implementability in practice may be challenging to establish.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: One-Step Generators via Implicit Neural Layer Resolution
PROPOSAL: Explore using implicit neural layer resolution to learn a one-step generator by directly optimizing the output distribution of the teacher AR model. Specifically, we will parameterize the one-step generator using a neural network and derive an implicit objective that minimizes the distance between the generator's output distribution and the teacher AR model's output distribution. We will then optimize this objective using a custom loss function and a dataset of synthetic sequences.
CONTROLS: This proposal will be compared against the Direct One-Step Generator via Neural Network Optimization (proposed in proposal 1) and against the teacher AR model itself.
COST: 8328.76
PREDICTION: This approach is expected to outperform the Neural Network Optimization based method, but may require careful tuning of the implicit objective to avoid instabilities during training. It may also struggle with small datasets and may not achieve the same level of performance as DD1.

TITLE: Accelerated One-Step Sampling with Conditional Set Prediction
PROPOSAL: Investigate using conditional set prediction to accelerate the sampling process of the one-step generator. Specifically, we will use a smaller set of tokens to predict the entire set of tokens, and condition the prediction on the context variables. We will train a separate model to perform this prediction and use the predicted set of tokens to initialize the one-step generator.
CONTROLS: This proposal will be compared against the teacher AR model, set prediction without conditioning, and the one-step generator trained using implicit neural layer resolution (proposal 2).

PREDICTION: This approach is expected to accelerate the sampling process while maintaining high quality, but may require careful tuning of the conditional set prediction model to avoid loss of information. It may also rely heavily on the quality of the initialization provided by the set prediction model.

TITLE: Asymmetric Objective for Efficient One-Step Learning (AOE)
PROPOSAL: Investigate an asymmetric objective training framework for the one-step generator, by decoupling the match between the prior noise input and the teacher AR model's output distribution, which can be prioritized as a secondary objective, and focusing on a primary objective that maximizes the similarity between the one-step generator's output token sequence distribution and the teacher AR model's token sequences. The asymmetric objective may help alleviate the training difficulties of the DMT model and improve one-step generator performance.
CONTROLS: Compare performance under: (i) original symmetric objective, (ii) asymmetric objective with emphasis on output token sequence, and (iii) asymmetric objective with weight-penalizingwij lên penalizing deviations from the output distribution as a secondary objective (capturing DD1's strengths). Evaluate effect of sensitivity of the asymmetric objective's trade-off parameter to pre-defined hyperparameters and real data results.
COST: 8328.76
PREDICTION: This novel approach will enable faster and more efficient one-step generator training by focusing on the key characteristics of one-step generation, with AOE being competitive with or enhancing DMT in terms of quality – but potential failures are high if it tends to sacrifice sample quality for efficiency, especially when DD1 performance becomes a strong point of comparison.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Local Component Attention (LCA) Guided Mixture Learning
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel component in the one-step generator that uses local component attention to guide a mixture of probability distributions conditioned on each local context of the output token sequence. This is in turn guided by learned attention parameters that embrace relationships between spatial locations by the AR output vectors which guide the flow of information, potentially paralleling the output distribution guidance in AOE and adding a novel spatial component in the flow matching principle behind DD1.
CONTROLS: Original AR model without smoothing, LCA-Guided-Distribution distillation-style replacement of the mixture of AR-generated codebooks for direct generation. Retain training limits of both the former and AOE on too-sparse separable training contexts.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Filtered Region Re-Design (FRRD)
PROPOSAL: In LCA, replace the global mixture model with a filtered region-based approach, where the one-step generator only predicts tokens within predefined regions of the output image, such as boundaries, texture patches, or edges. Regions are filtered based on the AR teacher's output distribution, indicating areas where new token prediction is more effective. This change aims to adapt the capabilities of LCA under sparse and high-density regions with relatively small amounts of variation.
CONTROLS: vary threshold selector parameters, compare performance with different filtering techniques (e.g., graph-based, texture-based) and filtering thresholds, assess effect on model's ability to capture complex image structures.
COST: 14000
PREDICTION: FRRD will allow the LCA model to better adapt to regions of high non-uniformity, potentially improving its performance in settings where global mixture models are overwhelmed, likely leading to a level plateau in comparison to the original AR model and AOE.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latent Codebook Inversion Learning (LCIL)
PROPOSAL: Train a novel model, LCIL, that jointly learns to invert the codebook embedding of the teacher AR model and predict the discrete tokens from the inverted embedding. LCIL aims to capture the structure of the codebook and output a more coherent and continuous embedding space for one-step generation, potentially improving the performance of the teacher AR model.
CONTROLS: Original AR model, LCIL's performance under different inversion techniques (e.g., discrete or continuous), and ablation studies to assess the contribution of each component.
COST: 20000
PREDICTION: LCIL will enable the teacher AR model to better capture the underlying structure of the codebook, leading to improved one-step generation performance and potentially reducing the performance gap with AOE and FRRD, although its applicability may be limited by the quality of the codebook and the inversion technique used, and it may fail to generalize well to diverse datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Manifold-Spanning Multi-Step Inference (MSMI)
PROPOSAL: Instead of directly generating tokens from a single step, propose a manifold-spanning approach where the model predicts a set of intermediate codebook embeddings that represent a lower-dimensional manifold of the output space. These embeddings are then used to generate the final tokens in a multi-step inference process, potentially reducing the combinatorial complexity of direct token prediction and improving the model's ability to capture complex image structures.
CONTROLS: Compare performance with the original AR model, DMT, AOE, FRRD, and LCIL, and assess the impact of different manifold-spanning techniques (e.g., PCA, Autoencoders) and intermediate step counts on the model's performance.
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: MSMI will enable the one-step generator to accurately capture complex image structures by leveraging the underlying manifold of the output space, potentially achieving state-of-the-art performance in one-step image synthesis tasks, although its applicability may be limited by the quality of the manifold representation and the intermediate step count.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Direct Mapping Training (DMT) Proposal
PROPOSAL: Train an additional model, DMT, that directly maps the prior noise distribution to the output distribution of the teacher AR model, using the teacher AR model's probability vectors as a supervisory signal to match the output distribution, and the teacher AR model's token sequences as a target to match the output token sequence distribution. DMT model is trained to take the same prior noise input as the teacher AR model and output a sequence of tokens with the same distribution as the teacher's output, without any loss or sampling process in between.
CONTROLS: Compare with Distilled Decoding 1 (DD1) and the original teacher AR model, and also assess limitations of matching the output distribution versus the token sequence distribution.
COST: 10000
PREDICTION: The DMT model will achieve a stronger reduction in sampling steps than DD1, but potentially at the cost of increased model complexity, and its training may require significant amounts of computation, especially for large datasets, where it could fail to improve as much as expected due to overfitting or mode collapse.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Orthogonal Weighted Residual Flow Estimation
PROPOSAL: We estimate an invertible residual flow granularity to fit the fine-grained detail encoding in each position of the AR output conditional distribution without distilling from a learned mapping. Specifically, this is a two-stage process: the first stage inverts an autoregressive-residual (AR-Res) transformation to an intermediate representation of the previous token, drawing the available discriminative information from the embeddings and output of previous positions; the second stage fits a distribution-adaptive linear transformation from the representation into the target location in the original conditional distribution. A residual flow is used as the learnable transformation, enabling an analytical computation of its Jacobian determinant and its invertibility.
CONTROLS: We compare with a default 1x1 residual flow, a variant with increased flow granularity using more gated linear layers, and a simple and naively learned affine transformation.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: Our method reduces the performance drop in single-step sampling relative to the original AR model, and we observe that when it uses more gates in its residual flow, it approaches reliable performance compared to full distillation. However, the trained model might overfit when approaching some especially complex and unusual data, failing to capture certain edge cases and nuances of data.

TITLE: Orthogonal Weighted Residual Flow Estimation
PROPOSAL: We estimate an invertible residual flow granularity to fit the fine-grained detail encoding in each position of the AR output conditional distribution without distilling from a learned mapping. Specifically, this is a two-stage process: the first stage inverts an autoregressive-residual (AR-Res) transformation to an intermediate representation of the previous token, drawing the available discriminative information from the embeddings and output of previous positions; the second stage fits a distribution-adaptive linear transformation from the representation into the target location in the original conditional distribution. A residual flow is used as the learnable transformation, enabling an analytical computation of its Jacobian determinant and its invertibility.
CONTROLS: We compare with a default 1x1 residual flow, a variant with increased flow granularity using more gated linear layers, and a simple and naively learned affine transformation.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Our method reduces the performance drop in single-step sampling relative to the original AR model, and we observe that when it uses more gates in its residual flow, it approaches reliable performance compared to full distillation. However, the trained model might overfit when approaching some especially complex and unusual data, failing to capture certain edge cases and nuances of data.

TITLE: Accelerating Image AR Modeling through Grounded Sequence Learning
PROPOSAL: Investigate a novel one-step sequence generation method inspired by grounded language learning, where the one-step generator learns a ground truth sequence that directly maps from a prior distribution to the output distribution of the teacher AR model, using techniques such as pointer networks and unnormalized flow-based models to encode the target sequence and infer the mapping between the latent space and the output space.
CONTROLS: Compare against DD1 as the baseline, and also evaluate a vanilla flow-based model without any coupling to the teacher AR model.
COST: 48000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected results show that the proposed method can achieve comparable sample quality to the original AR model, with faster inference speed, but may struggle to preserve the important variations present in the training data, leading to mode collapse in certain scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing Noise-ulturality of Token-to-Token Mapping
PROPOSAL: Investigate how the quality of the noise-to-data mapping in the one-step generator is affected by the noise distribution, and whether different levels of noiseulturality impact sampling efficiency and output distribution matching with the teacher AR model. This is done by comparing the proposals across different noise distributions (e.g., IID Gaussian noise, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, etc.), and analyzing the effects of increasing noiseulturality on the generated sequence's diversity and fidelity.
CONTROLS: Test with the grounded sequence learning method from Proposal 1, and also compare against a simpler method that simply adds latent noise to the prior distribution.
COST: 82000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected results show that the choice of noise distribution has a substantial impact on sampling efficiency and quality, with some noise distributions yielding better or worse results than the others. However, excessive noiseulturality might reduce the output distribution matching with the teacher AR model, while under-desktopmirroring might lead to an over-reliance on the flow-based model during training, making the generator less flexible and more difficult to train.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Enhancing Flexibility with Uncertainty Modeling
PROPOSAL: Introduce uncertainty modeling into the one-step generator by incorporating a probabilistic representation of the noise-to-data mapping uncertainty, in order to allow the generator to learn more flexible and generalizable mappings. This is done by appending an uncertainty estimation to each output token, which is then used to adjust the generation process and enhance the overall flexibility of the generator.
CONTROLS: Examine the effect of different models for uncertainty estimation (e.g., MC dropout, Bayesian neural networks), and compare the results against a baseline that does not use uncertainty modeling.
COST: 95000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected results show that incorporating uncertainty modeling leads to better flexibility and generalizability, particularly in the presence of ambiguous or incomplete input data, but also requires careful hyperparameter tuning to balance flexibility and fidelity with the teacher AR model's output distribution.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Enhancing Flexibility with Uncertainty Modeling (Revise 3)
PROPOSAL: Modify proposal 3 by incorporating a second probabilistic model, which is used to alternate and interact with the one-step generator during training. This can enable the one-step generator to sample from a more diverse and informative prior, reducing overfitting and improving generalizability. Specifically, this is done by introducing an additional noise variable that, upon sampling, is fed into the generator, alternating between relying on the prior and on the probabilistically modeled interaction with the other model. 
CONTROLS: Examine the effects when using an ensemble model, a simple Markov process, or a predictor stage for the probabilistic interaction.
COST: 60000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expected results show that this ability to alternate, enables a generator that even on smaller data-sets can generalize significantly better and form novel outputs with respect to  new “genres” of previously unseen inputs for the one-step model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Non-Predefined Mapping (NPM) via Attribute Space Optimization
PROPOSAL: In this experiment, we propose a new method, Non-Predefined Mapping (NPM), that trains a generator to map a single latent variable to a complete token sequence without any predefined noise-to-data mapping. The generator is optimized to produce tokens in the attribute space, where each token is represented as a combination of its attributes. Our approach is based on minimizing a novel distance metric between the output distribution of the teacher model and the generator's output, at each token position. This is done by iteratively updating the generator's parameters, first to project the latent variable into the attribute space, and then to produce the next token. We leverage a dataset of images with their corresponding attribute annotations, such as style, color, and texture.
CONTROLS: We compare NPM with the DD1 method and also evaluate the original AR model's one-step performance as a strong baseline. Ablation studies will investigate the effects of different distance metrics and generator architectures.
COST: 33
PREDICTION: Our NPM method is expected to perform better than DD1, especially for complex datasets with a variety of attributes. However, it might suffer from mode collapse or failure to generalize when dealing with high-dimensional attribute spaces.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: GPU-Accelerated Knowledge Distillation for NPM
PROPOSAL: To speed up the training of NPM, we propose GPU-accelerated knowledge distillation. This involves distilling the knowledge of the teacher AR model into a smaller NPM generator using a distributed, batch-based approach that leverages the Multi-GPU architecture. We expect significant speed-up in training time and reduced memory requirements. To further accelerate NPM training, we will integrate our previous experiment's attribute space optimization with various GPU-based techniques, including parallelism and data parallelism.
CONTROLS: In addition to evaluating the original AR model's one-step performance, we will compare our NPM generator with the DD1 method, both with and without knowledge distillation. We will also conduct ablation studies to evaluate the effectiveness of different distillation techniques.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Our method is expected to speed up NPM training by at least 2-3 times, with minimal performance degradation. It may also alleviate issues related to convergence and stability in NPM training, although some minor complications might arise from balancing the needs of both teacher and student models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Regularized Learning of Conditional Token Mapping
PROPOSAL: Building upon NPM, we introduce a regularization term to improve the learning of conditional token mapping. The regularization term involves minimizing the difference between the conditional probabilities output by the teacher AR model and the unconditional probabilities output by our NPM generator. This helps the generator learn the conditional dependencies between tokens more accurately, leading to improved performance. To control the learning of conditional token mapping, we utilize a set of pre-defined tokens, such as spatial tokens, and encourage our NPM generator to output tokens that are conditionally independent given these tokens.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the impact of our regularized loss on the one-step performance of NPM, comparing it to both the original AR model and the DD1 method. We will also conduct an ablation study to investigate the effect of different types of regularization terms on NPM performance.
COST: 72.917
PREDICTION: Our regularized learning technique is expected to improve the one-step performance of NPM, especially for high-resolution images. However, the added regularization may lead to over-smoothing or loss of sharp features in the generated images if not properly calibrated.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improved Attribute Encoding for NPM
PROPOSAL: We propose an enhanced attribute encoding technique for NPM, which learns a hierarchical representation of the attribute space. This technique uses an auto-regressive model to sequentially generate the attributes of each token, enabling the NPM generator to capture complex correlations between attributes. To improve attribute learning, we employ a combination of attention-based and mask-based methods to selectively focus on relevant attributes. The resulting attribute representation is optimized for efficient encoding and decoding of complex image attributes.
CONTROLS: We compare our proposed attribute encoding with the original attribute space optimization employed in NPM, and also evaluate the performance of NPM using different attribute encodings.
COST: 100
PREDICTION: Our improved attribute encoding technique is expected to enhance the one-step performance of NPM, particularly for complex datasets with intricate attribute relationships. However, it might introduce new challenges related to attribute entanglement and redundancy if the hierarchical representation becomes too complex.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Early Stopping and Continual Learning for Instance-Specific NPM
PROPOSAL: To mitigate possible mode collapse and facilitate the exploration of instance-specific patterns in NPM, we introduce early stopping and continual learning protocols. When NPM training is early stopped, we select a subset of samples from the validation set that are most indicative of the instance-specific patterns. These selected samples are then used to fine-tune the NPM generator, leveraging experience replay and training from scratch techniques to improve its adaptability to new instances. The overall goal is to enable NPM to efficiently learn and adapt to diverse instances without extensive fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: We compare our early stopping and continual learning approach with the standard training protocol for NPM and also evaluate its performance in image-to-image translation tasks.
COST: 140
PREDICTION: Our approach is expected to improve the adaptability and instance-specific performance of NPM without requiring significant retraining. However, it may lead to increased training time and additional memory requirements, which should be carefully managed to maintain scalability.

TITLE: Multi-Tenant Architecture for NPM Training
PROPOSAL: We propose a multi-tenant architecture for NPM training, allowing multiple instances of the NPM generator to be trained concurrently on different subsets of the training dataset. This design enables the efficient exploration of different instance-specific patterns and models, while also reducing the overall training time by leveraging multi-GPU acceleration. We develop a novel tenant-aware diffusion policy to distribute the training load across tenants based on their demand and available resources.
CONTROLS: We compare our multi-tenant approach with the standard multi-GPU training protocol and evaluate its performance in low-resource settings and large-scale datasets.

PREDICTION: Our multi-tenant architecture is expected to improve the scalability and efficiency of NPM training, especially in resource-constrained settings. However, it may introduce additional complexity and require careful tenant management to optimize performance, which could lead to challenges in deploying and maintaining large-scale NPM models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Non-Predefined Mapping (NPM) via Attribute Space Optimization
PROPOSAL: In this experiment, we propose a new method, Non-Predefined Mapping (NPM), that trains a generator to map a single latent variable to a complete token sequence without any predefined noise-to-data mapping. The generator is optimized to produce tokens in the attribute space, where each token is represented as a combination of its attributes. Our approach is based on minimizing a novel distance metric between the output distribution of the teacher model and the generator's output, at each token position. This is done by iteratively updating the generator's parameters, first to project the latent variable into the attribute space, and then to produce the next token. We leverage a dataset of images with their corresponding attribute annotations, such as style, color, and texture.
CONTROLS: We compare NPM with the DD1 method and also evaluate the original AR model's one-step performance as a strong baseline. Ablation studies will investigate the effects of different distance metrics and generator architectures.
COST: 100
PREDICTION: Our NPM method is expected to perform better than DD1, especially for complex datasets with a variety of attributes. However, it might suffer from mode collapse or failure to generalize when dealing with high-dimensional attribute spaces.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: GPU-Accelerated Knowledge Distillation for NPM
PROPOSAL: To speed up the training of NPM, we propose GPU-accelerated knowledge distillation. This involves distilling the knowledge of the teacher AR model into a smaller NPM generator using a distributed, batch-based approach that leverages the Multi-GPU architecture. We expect significant speed-up in training time and reduced memory requirements. To further accelerate NPM training, we will integrate our previous experiment's attribute space optimization with various GPU-based techniques, including parallelism and data parallelism.
CONTROLS: In addition to evaluating the original AR model's one-step performance, we will compare our NPM generator with the DD1 method, both with and without knowledge distillation. We will also conduct ablation studies to evaluate the effectiveness of different distillation techniques.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Our method is expected to speed up NPM training by at least 2-3 times, with minimal performance degradation. It may also alleviate issues related to convergence and stability in NPM training, although some minor complications might arise from balancing the needs of both teacher and student models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Regularized Learning of Conditional Token Mapping
PROPOSAL: Building upon NPM, we introduce a regularization term to improve the learning of conditional token mapping. The regularization term involves minimizing the difference between the conditional probabilities output by the teacher AR model and the unconditional probabilities output by our NPM generator. This helps the generator learn the conditional dependencies between tokens more accurately, leading to improved performance. To control the learning of conditional token mapping, we utilize a set of pre-defined tokens, such as spatial tokens, and encourage our NPM generator to output tokens that are conditionally independent given these tokens.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the impact of our regularized loss on the one-step performance of NPM, comparing it to both the original AR model and the DD1 method. We will also conduct an ablation study to investigate the effect of different types of regularization terms on NPM performance.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: Our regularized learning technique is expected to improve the one-step performance of NPM, especially for high-resolution images. However, the added regularization may lead to over-smoothing or loss of sharp features in the generated images if not properly calibrated.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improved Attribute Encoding for NPM
PROPOSAL: We propose an enhanced attribute encoding technique for NPM, which learns a hierarchical representation of the attribute space. This technique uses an auto-regressive model to sequentially generate the attributes of each token, enabling the NPM generator to capture complex correlations between attributes. To improve attribute learning, we employ a combination of attention-based and mask-based methods to selectively focus on relevant attributes. The resulting attribute representation is optimized for efficient encoding and decoding of complex image attributes.
CONTROLS: We compare our proposed attribute encoding with the original attribute space optimization employed in NPM, and also evaluate the performance of NPM using different attribute encodings.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Our improved attribute encoding technique is expected to enhance the one-step performance of NPM, particularly for complex datasets with intricate attribute relationships. However, it might introduce new challenges related to attribute entanglement and redundancy if the hierarchical representation becomes too complex.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Early Stopping and Continual Learning for Instance-Specific NPM
PROPOSAL: To mitigate possible mode collapse and facilitate the exploration of instance-specific patterns in NPM, we introduce early stopping and continual learning protocols. When NPM training is early stopped, we select a subset of samples from the validation set that are most indicative of the instance-specific patterns. These selected samples are then used to fine-tune the NPM generator, leveraging experience replay and training from scratch techniques to improve its adaptability to new instances. The overall goal is to enable NPM to efficiently learn and adapt to diverse instances without extensive fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: We compare our early stopping and continual learning approach with the standard training protocol for NPM and also evaluate its performance in image-to-image translation tasks.
COST: 420
PREDICTION: Our approach is expected to improve the adaptability and instance-specific performance of NPM without requiring significant retraining. However, it may lead to increased training time and additional memory requirements, which should be carefully managed to maintain scalability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dynamic Routing Imbalance Loss for MoE Training
PROPOSAL: We investigate a new routing constraint, "Dynamic Routing Imbalance Loss (DRIL)", that dynamically computes the load-balancing loss for each expert on a local (micro-batch) basis, and regularizes the difference in this loss across experts. This DRIL constraint promotes routing adaptability and enables experts to develop specialized representations on diverse, rather than uniform, data distributions.
CONTROLS: We compare DRIL with standard load-balancing loss, global DRIL, and an empty routing strategy for an absolute lower bound.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Guided Routing with Cluster Assignment
PROPOSAL: We will design a new MoE training objective that encourages expert specialization by clustering similar tokens together. During routing, each token will be assigned to a cluster, and the load-balancing loss will be computed separately for each cluster. This will allow the model to develop distinct expert representations for different token clusters, promoting functional specialization among experts. We will use the English-language version of the Hugging Face Datasets' "BookCorpus" as the training data and evaluate our approach on language modeling and downstream knowledge question answering benchmarks.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to the standard MoE training with the global load-balancing loss as well as to MoE with a single shared expert for each sequence. We will also validate our approach by ablation studies to demonstrate that the cluster assignment and separate load-balancing losses are necessary for expert specialization.
COST: 8000
PREDICTION: Our approach should lead to improved expert specialization, and hence better language modeling and downstream performance compared to the standard MoE training. However, we risk over-expert-ization, where a few experts learn to serve overly specific token clusters, and neglect generalizing to new clusters.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Experts as Monotonic Regression Functions
PROPOSAL: We will propose a novel regularization term for the MoE router that encourages experts to learn monotonic regression functions with respect to the input token positions. This can be achieved by penalizing drops in the token probability distribution when the input position increases. Intuitively, this will allow the model to learn smooth and continuous distribution shifts across the input sequence, promoting the development of well-specialized and coherent expert representations. We will evaluate this approach on a range of mathematical reasoning tasks.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to the standard MoE model and to an MoE model with a regularizer that encourages orthogonality of the router's weight matrix, which would encourage the model to use more diverse expert combinations. We will also validate our approach by assessing the impact of the strength of the monotonic regression constraint on expert specialization and downstream performance.
COST: 10000
PREDICTION: Our approach should lead to improved expert specialization, particularly in tasks that require learning from continuous input sequences. However, we risk overly constraining the model's routing flexibility, which could limit its ability to generalize to diverse task distributions.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Experts as Monotonic Regression Functions
PROPOSAL: We will revise our previous proposal and further develop the monotonic regression function regularization for the MoE router. Specifically, we will experiment with replacing the standalone regularization term with a soft- constrained loss function, allowing the model to balance the need for monotonic behavior with the requirement to predict accurate output probabilities. Additionally, we will introduce a few orthogonal regularizers to compute and soften relationships to Hinge losses for each router unit that intersects a set of conditions between clause inputs' values, further mitigating per-image likeness. We will evaluate this approach on a range of reading comprehension tasks.
CONTROLS: We will compare our revised approach to the original monotonic regression function regularization and to an MoE model with no regularization. We will also validate our approach by assessing the impact of the strength of the soft-constrained loss function and the orthogonal regularizers on expert specialization and downstream performance.
COST: 11000
PREDICTION: Our revised approach should lead to improved expert specialization, preserving the model's ability to learn from continuous input sequences and adapting to diverse task distributions. However, we risk an increased risk of over-complexity due to the introduction of new regularizers.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Routing for Fast Expert Adaptation
PROPOSAL: We will design a hierarchical routing mechanism for MoE models that allows for rapid adaptation of expert representations to new tasks or data distributions. The idea is to employ a coarse-grained routing selector that identifies a few critical expert representations, which will in turn route to multiple specific fine-grained expert responders. This process decouples the coarse and fine adaptation, serving to allow numerous presses with different data sets. We will evaluate this approach on a range of exam-style knowledge question answering tasks that require rapid adaptation to new domains.
CONTROLS: We will compare our hierarchical routing approach to standard MoE routing and to an MoE model with always-active shared experts, comparing its performance on both the task of rapid adaptation and knowledge retention across related tasks. We will also validate our approach by assessing the impact of different numbers of coarse-grained expert selectors on expert specialization and downstream performance.
COST: 12635.93
PREDICTION: Our approach should lead to improved fast adaptation to new tasks and knowledge retention across related tasks, as the model can rapidly specialize to the most relevant experts for each new task. However, we risk the model neglecting generalization to unseen domains if it focuses on adapting too quickly within existing domains.

TITLE: Guided Routing with Cluster Assignment
PROPOSAL: We will modify the guided routing with cluster assignment to integrate the hierarchical routing mechanism. Specifically, we will combine both approaches, using the hierarchical routing selector to identify key expert representations at the coarse-grained level, and then assign the tokens within each cluster to a set of fine-grained experts that best capture the nuances of each cluster. We will evaluate this integrated approach on a range of English language modeling and Chinese language modeling benchmarks that require both rapid adaptation and specialized expert representations.
CONTROLS: We will compare our integrated approach to standard MoE routing, guided routing with cluster assignment alone, and hierarchical routing alone, as well as to an MoE model with always-active shared experts. We will also validate our approach by assessing the impact of different combinations of coarse-grained and fine-grained routing selectors on expert specialization and downstream performance.

PREDICTION: Our integrated approach should lead to improved expert specialization, rapid adaptation, and downstream performance across a range of tasks and languages, as it leverages the strengths of both approaches. However, we risk the model neglecting generalization due to over-specialization on specific clusters or languages.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Metric Learning-based Expert Initialization
PROPOSAL: We will introduce a new expert initialization method for MoE models that utilizes metric learning to achieve better clustering and specialization among experts. The idea is to learn a shared embedding space for all experts and the input tokens, and then initialize the experts based on their similarities to the input tokens in this space. This approach can help ensure that each expert is initialized with a well-defined and diverse set of representations. We will evaluate this approach on a range of downstream tasks that require knowledge retention and adaptation.
CONTROLS: We will compare our metric learning-based initialization approach to standard random initialization, guided routing with cluster assignment, and hierarchical routing for fast expert adaptation. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Guided Routing with Cluster Assignment
PROPOSAL: We will design a new MoE training objective that encourages expert specialization by clustering similar tokens together. During routing, each token will be assigned to a cluster, and the load-balancing loss will be computed separately for each cluster. This will allow the model to develop distinct expert representations for different token clusters, promoting functional specialization among experts. We will use the English-language version of the Hugging Face Datasets' "BookCorpus" as the training data and evaluate our approach on language modeling and downstream knowledge question answering benchmarks.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to the standard MoE training with the global load-balancing loss as well as to MoE with a single shared expert for each sequence. We will also validate our approach by ablation studies to demonstrate that the cluster assignment and separate load-balancing losses are necessary for expert specialization.
COST: 24000
PREDICTION: Our approach should lead to improved expert specialization, and hence better language modeling and downstream performance compared to the standard MoE training. However, we risk over-expert-ization, where a few experts learn to serve overly specific token clusters, and neglect generalizing to new clusters.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Experts as Monotonic Regression Functions
PROPOSAL: We will propose a novel regularization term for the MoE router that encourages experts to learn monotonic regression functions with respect to the input token positions. This can be achieved by penalizing drops in the token probability distribution when the input position increases. Intuitively, this will allow the model to learn smooth and continuous distribution shifts across the input sequence, promoting the development of well-specialized and coherent expert representations. We will evaluate this approach on a range of mathematical reasoning tasks.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to the standard MoE model and to an MoE model with a regularizer that encourages orthogonality of the router's weight matrix, which would encourage the model to use more diverse expert combinations. We will also validate our approach by assessing the impact of the strength of the monotonic regression constraint on expert specialization and downstream performance.
COST: 30000
PREDICTION: Our approach should lead to improved expert specialization, particularly in tasks that require learning from continuous input sequences. However, we risk overly constraining the model's routing flexibility, which could limit its ability to generalize to diverse task distributions.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Experts as Monotonic Regression Functions
PROPOSAL: We will revise our previous proposal and further develop the monotonic regression function regularization for the MoE router. Specifically, we will experiment with replacing the standalone regularization term with a soft- constrained loss function, allowing the model to balance the need for monotonic behavior with the requirement to predict accurate output probabilities. Additionally, we will introduce a few orthogonal regularizers to compute and soften relationships to Hinge losses for each router unit that intersects a set of conditions between clause inputs' values, further mitigating per-image likeness. We will evaluate this approach on a range of reading comprehension tasks.
CONTROLS: We will compare our revised approach to the original monotonic regression function regularization and to an MoE model with no regularization. We will also validate our approach by assessing the impact of the strength of the soft-constrained loss function and the orthogonal regularizers on expert specialization and downstream performance.
COST: 33000
PREDICTION: Our revised approach should lead to improved expert specialization, preserving the model's ability to learn from continuous input sequences and adapting to diverse task distributions. However, we risk an increased risk of over-complexity due to the introduction of new regularizers.

The idea is to employ a coarse-grained routing selector that identifies a few critical expert representations, which will in turn route to multiple specific fine-grained expert responders. This process decouples the coarse and fine adaptation, serving to allow numerous presses with different data sets. We will evaluate this approach on a range of exam-style knowledge question answering tasks that require rapid adaptation to new domains.
CONTROLS: We will compare our hierarchical routing approach to standard MoE routing and to an MoE model with always-active shared experts, comparing its performance on both the task of rapid adaptation and knowledge retention across related tasks. We will also validate our approach by assessing the impact of different numbers of coarse-grained expert selectors on expert specialization and downstream performance.

PREDICTION: Our approach should lead to improved fast adaptation to new tasks and knowledge retention across related tasks, as the model can rapidly specialize to the most relevant experts for each new task. However, we risk the model neglecting generalization to unseen domains if it focuses on adapting too quickly within existing domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: "Multiple-Metric Learning-Rate Policy for Multi-Label Image Classification"
PROPOSAL: Investigate whether a novel "multiple-metric" learning-rate policy, $\mathcal{S}_{lr}$, based on adaptive estimates of label class difficulty, feature-label co-occurrence, and regularization strength, can dynamically adjust the learning-rate for each individual label $\ell$ in a multi-label image classifier $M$, to balance exploration-exploitation trade-offs and reduce class imbalance. In the proposed setup, a fine-grained exploration-exploitation trade-off is achieved by assigning a unique set of learning rates $\{ \alpha^{\ell, iterations}_{M, \mathbf{C}, \mathbf{W}} \}$ at each iteration of training, where $\mathbf{C}$ denotes the current configuration and $\mathbf{W}$ the set of feature-label weights learned so far.
CONTROLS: a. Static learning-rate schedule: a naive learning-rate schedule $S_{lr}$ with a fixed learning-rate for all labels; b. Tri-stage learning-rate policy: a common multi-stage schedule $S_{lr}^{tri}$ with learning rates for exploration, exploitation, and a third intermediate stage.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: The multiple-metric policy will achieve higher combined loss, higher learned label accuracy, and shorter convergence time compared to static and tri-stage learning rate policies, especially for rare labels.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: "Joint Adaptive On-The-Fly Optimization of Augmentation Policies and Optimizers"
PROPOSAL: To jointly optimize augmentation policies and optimizers, we will design a meta-controller $\mathcal{M}$ that adaptively selects and adjusts data augmentation strategies $\{\mathcal{T}_{aug}^{\ell}\}$ from a pre-defined set of policies for each label $\ell$, while simultaneously coordinating the learning of a neural optimizer, $\mathcal{O}_{\vec{\theta}_t}$, that specializes in adapting to the evolving feature-label mappings and objective loss of the model. In the original model, the joint control logic $\mathcal{M}$ effectively learns a sequence of dynamic training configurations $\hat{\mathbf{C}}_t = \{\mathcal{T}_{aug,t}^{\ell}, \mathcal{O}_{\vec{\theta}_t}\}$ for each time step $t$, balancing exploration-exploitation tradeoffs for adapting to rapidly changing label distributions during training.
CONTROLS: a. $\mathcal{T}_{aug}$ static: fixation of an expert-designed augmentation strategy for all labels; b. Single-knob optimization: optimizing one knob (either augmentation or optimizer) while fixing the other to its expert-designed default.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: This design will improve model adaptability and earned label accuracy across all classes, particularly with respect to new or unseen labels, as compared to control setups, through a dynamically adaptive and intertwined interplay between augmentation policies and optimizers.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: "Task-Aware Loss Functions with Class-Dependent Weights"
PROPOSAL: In this proposal, we will use a framework to automatically discover task-aware loss functions $\mathcal{L}_{task}$ that incorporate label co-occurrences, class difficulties, and the interaction with selected neural network components. This is achieved by jointly optimizing for the learned class-dependent weights $\{w^{\ell}\}$ and the neural network itself, which enables a flexible loss weighting strategy that weighs each label $\ell$ according to its estimated importance. The parameterized class-weight version of the robust cross-entropy loss function, a generalization of the original robust cross-entropy, will be used for effectively learning these task-aware class weights.
CONTROLS: a. Fixed class-weight cross-entropy loss: fixed loss weights for each label through pre-defined knobs or grid search; b. "Hard" equality constrained loss weights: constraint of the loss weights to faithful replication of standard class frequencies.
COST: 1036.8
PREDICTION: Experimental evidence will demonstrate the empirical value of learned class weights in reducing the class imbalance and boosting accuracy for rare and frequently appearing labels.

TITLE: "ConfigSpace-Probabilistic Sampling: Meta-Learning for Adaptive Optimal Configuration Search in Multi-Label Image Classification"
PROPOSAL: We will introduce a novel meta-learning based probabilistic sampling, ConfigSpace-Probabilistic Sampling (CSPS), that efficiently samples high-dimensional and discrete (or hybrid) configuration spaces to guide the optimization of multi-label image classification models. CSPS employs a probabilistic model to estimate each component's contribution to the final performance and incorporates model-based uncertainty quantification to improve the exploration-exploitation trade-off, achieving highly efficient configuration search and more time-effective generalization to unseen test scenarios.
CONTROLS: a. Exhaustive brute-force search: manual grid search strategy across high-dimensional configuration spaces; b. Meta-learning baseline with fixed uncertainty models: rigid meta-learners where both the parameter estimation and uncertainty modeling part typically require repeated personal tuning efforts that specifically over-rides more meaningful improvements throughout our duration involving multiple trials in live-takes decision environments.
COST: 1263.593
PREDICTION: Configuration search will take significantly less time, yielding scalable performance evaluations in real-world image classification using a diverse and representative set of relevant tasks for model validation.

In the proposed setup, a fine-grained exploration-exploitation trade-off is achieved by assigning a unique set of learning rates $\{ \alpha^{\ell, iterations}_{M, \mathbf{C}, \mathbf{W}} \}$ at each iteration of training, where $\mathbf{C}$ denotes the current configuration and $\mathbf{W}$ the set of feature-label weights learned so far.
CONTROLS: a. Static learning-rate schedule: a naive learning-rate schedule $S_{lr}$ with a fixed learning-rate for all labels; b. Tri-stage learning-rate policy: a common multi-stage schedule $S_{lr}^{tri}$ with learning rates for exploration, exploitation, and a third intermediate stage.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The multiple-metric policy will achieve higher combined loss, higher learned label accuracy, and shorter convergence time compared to static and tri-stage learning rate policies, especially for rare labels.

PROPOSAL: To jointly optimize augmentation policies and optimizers, we will design a meta-controller $\mathcal{M}$ that adaptively selects and adjusts data augmentation strategies $\{\mathcal{T}_{aug}^{\ell}\}$ from a pre-defined set of policies for each label $\ell$, while simultaneously coordinating the learning of a neural optimizer, $\mathcal{O}_{\vec{\theta}_t}$, that specializes in adapting to the evolving feature-label mappings and objective loss of the model. In the original model, the joint control logic $\mathcal{M}$ effectively learns a sequence of dynamic training configurations $\hat{\mathbf{C}}_t = \{\mathcal{T}_{aug,t}^{\ell}, \mathcal{O}_{\vec{\theta}_t}\}$ for each time step $t$, balancing exploration-exploitation tradeoffs for adapting to rapidly changing label distributions during training.
CONTROLS: a. $\mathcal{T}_{aug}$ static: fixation of an expert-designed augmentation strategy for all labels; b. Single-knob optimization: optimizing one knob (either augmentation or optimizer) while fixing the other to its expert-designed default.
COST: 2700
PREDICTION: This design will improve model adaptability and earned label accuracy across all classes, particularly with respect to new or unseen labels, as compared to control setups, through a dynamically adaptive and intertwined interplay between augmentation policies and optimizers.

PROPOSAL: In this proposal, we will use a framework to automatically discover task-aware loss functions $\mathcal{L}_{task}$ that incorporate label co-occurrences, class difficulties, and the interaction with selected neural network components. This is achieved by jointly optimizing for the learned class-dependent weights $\{w^{\ell}\}$ and the neural network itself, which enables a flexible loss weighting strategy that weighs each label $\ell$ according to its estimated importance. The parameterized class-weight version of the robust cross-entropy loss function, a generalization of the original robust cross-entropy, will be used for effectively learning these task-aware class weights.
CONTROLS: a. Fixed class-weight cross-entropy loss: fixed loss weights for each label through pre-defined knobs or grid search; b. "Hard" equality constrained loss weights: constraint of the loss weights to faithful replication of standard class frequencies.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint Adaptive Optimization for Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We propose a meta-learning approach, "DYNOPT" (Dynamic Optimization of Training Parameters), which learns a jointly adaptive configuration of training components (augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, loss function) over the course of training. A model-agnostic controller observes the current training state, sampling candidates from a learned policy at each iteration to jointly update these components, allowing for coordination and adaptation to evolving training dynamics. Our DYNOPT controller is trained on a dataset of self-contained mini-train
ing experiments, using a doubly reinforced learning objective to balance on-policy and off-policy learning.
CONTROLS: We compare DYNOPT against a range of incremental single-component adaptations (auto-augmentation, adaptive optimizers, learning-rate scheduling methods, class-indexed loss reweighting) and baseline static configuration pipelines (tuned by grid search or Bayesian optimization) on the PASCAL VOC, iNat and COCO datasets.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: DYNOPT should outperform static configurations by 2-4% averaged over the three datasets, while demonstrating more stable training and adaptation abilities compared to current state-of-the-art incremental adaptations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: HYPER: Component-Interacting Hyperparameter Search for Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: To address the high dimensionality and potential inter-component interactions in multi-label image classification, we propose HYPER, a neural architecture search-based hyperparameter optimization method that discovers both component-wise and inter-component hyperparameters (augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, loss function). HYPER defines a unified latent space to explore hyperparameter combinations, exploring a massive, discrete or hybrid configuration space by learning a component-interacting policy using reinforcement learning and simulated annealing. To leverage existing knowledge and engineering expertise, HYPER also incorporates an adaptive knowledge distillation objective, passing pre-trained static configuration weights as soft targets to the policy.
CONTROLS: We evaluate HYPER against strong baselines, including state-of-the-art hyperparameter tuning methods (e.g., Spearmint, SMAC) and our own static configuration pipelines, on the PASCAL VOC, iNat and COCO multi-label classification datasets. 
COST: 2400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: HYPER should consistently outperform the baselines by 4-6% averaged over the three datasets, thanks to its capacity to jointly search across all components, capture their complex, nonlinear interactions, and build on pre-trained knowledge.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: LDIS: Label-Domain Interpolation for Efficient Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: To address the high computational cost of current approaches that search across large configuration spaces, we propose LDIS (Label-Domain Interpolation), a dimensionality reduction framework that approximates complete configuration search via interpolation across pre-learned statistics of label-domain patterns. Throughout training, LDIS estimates a latent encoding that represents the state of the training trajectory and relates it to pre-learned (meta)label-domain patterns, effectively sampling the original configuration space in a data-efficient manner. We leverage transfer learning and distant supervision to robustly learn the (meta)label-domain patterns, scaling LDIS to a variety of real-world and large-scale task domains.
CONTROLS: We compare LDIS to the two candidates we previously proposed, as well as ablated variants, on the PASCAL VOC, iNat, and COCO datasets.
COST: 1345.6 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: LDIS will achieve smaller compute costs and preserve performance accuracy when compared to the non-interpolative search methods.

TITLE: IDEAL: Interleaved Dynamic Exploration and Adaptation for Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We present IDEAL (Interleaved Dynamic Exploration and Adaptation), a novel strategy that leverages both active learning and adaptive learning to optimize the performance of multi-label image classification models. As the model trains, IDEAL dynamically identifies the most informative and uncertain samples and assigns a set of exploration weights to dynamically guide the learning process. Meanwhile, it adapts the loss function and sampling strategy during training to suit the evolving complexity and difficulty of the training and validation tasks. To strike a balance between exploration and exploitation, we incorporate a probabilistic model to effectively handle exploration weights, enabling the efficient discovery of promising configurations and maximal improvement in performance.
CONTROLS: Experiments are compared with our DYNOPT framework, to check local information place, reflecting what optimization uses.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: ODIN: Online Data-Driven Optimization for Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We present ODIN (Online Data-Driven Optimization), a novel approach to optimize multi-label image classification using a data-driven optimization strategy. ODIN exploits a sequential decision-making framework to iteratively collect highly informative samples, adapt the configuration space, and update the model, while ensuring exploration and exploitation balance. A new meta-learning approach adapts to changing data distributions and learns the policy of dynamic exploration, ensuring optimal performance under varying data characteristics. By integrating a probabilistic model that accounts for uncertainty, ODIN effectively discovers the "sweet spot" of exploration, significantly enhancing model adaptability and robustness without relying on suboptimal randomized search.
CONTROLS: The robustness of ODIN is evaluated through a comprehensive comparative study with existing adaptive optimization techniques (DYNOPT, IDEAL, HYPER, and static configurations) on diverse multi-label image recognition datasets (ImageNet, Scene15, and Caltech256).
COST: 4800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: ODIN efficiently optimizes multi-label image classification performance, showcasing robustness and adaptability to varying training data, and improving the performance by at least 7% over the state-of-the-art methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: FOCUS: Fully Online Learning for Unseen Classes in Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We propose FOCUS, a fully online learning approach for unseen classes in multi-label image classification, using a hierarchical classification strategy. FOCUS predicts the unseen classes by identifying relatively dominant classes and employing incremental learning for in-class samples, both guided by an uncertainty-guided sampling mechanism that balances exploration and exploitation. Our method dynamically updates the importance weights of samples based on the predictions from convolutional networks and the incorporated uncertainty estimates. Results are presented on the rapidly growing and shifting benchmark CIFAR100-S and incorporating robustness metrics.
CONTROLS: FOCUS is compared to emerging uncertainty-based and importance-weighted strategies for online learning methods from relevant literature.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: FOCUS achieves online class-agnostic learning gains on multi-label images up to 12% higher than some inductive benchmarks. By efficiently focusing efforts where they matter, per category content becomes essentially accurate and human curve relevant.

TITLE: Joint Adaptive Optimization for Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We refine the DYNOPT controller with CEPHYR's collaborative exploration and phase-period adaptation mechanism. The revised controller uses accurate phase and period determination to identify the most efficient configurations and adapt the exploration-exploitation trade-off in real-time. This enables the model to dynamically adjust to changing data distributions and optimize performance across various label spaces. We demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of the revised controller through extensive experiments on a range of multi-label image classification benchmarks.
CONTROLS: We compare the revised controller to the original DYNOPT, IDEAL, and ODIN methods, and CEPHYR on diverse datasets, evaluating their performance, adaptability, and scalability.
COST: 7200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised controller should significantly outperform the original DYNOPT and other methods, achieving faster convergence, better adaptability, and improved scalability in multi-label image classification tasks.

To leverage existing knowledge and engineering expertise, HYPER also incorporates an adaptive knowledge distillation objective, passing pre-trained static configuration weights as soft targets to the policy.
CONTROLS: We evaluate HYPER against strong baselines, including state-of-the-art hyperparameter tuning methods (e.g., Spearmint, SMAC) and our own static configuration pipelines, on the PASCAL VOC, iNat and COCO multi-label classification datasets. 
COST: 7200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: HYPER should consistently outperform the baselines by 4-6% averaged over the three datasets, thanks to its capacity to jointly search across all components, capture their complex, nonlinear interactions, and build on pre-trained knowledge.

PROPOSAL: To address the high computational cost of current approaches that search across large configuration spaces, we propose LDIS (Label-Domain Interpolation), a dimensionality reduction framework that approximates complete configuration search via interpolation across pre-learned statistics of label-domain patterns. Throughout training, LDIS estimates a latent encoding that represents the state of the training trajectory and relates it to pre-learned (meta)label-domain patterns, effectively sampling the original configuration space in a data-efficient manner. We leverage transfer learning and distant supervision to robustly learn the (meta)label-domain patterns, scaling LDIS to a variety of real-world and large-scale task domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Configuration Learning for Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: Implement a model-agnostic online learning framework, that dynamically adjusts the data augmentation, optimizer, learning rate schedule, and loss function based on the evolving validation performance and training dynamics. We'll leverage Attention mechanisms to model the interactions among components and determine the relative importance of each configuration dimension. The framework, called "AutoConfig", will utilize off-policy reinforcement learning to find the optimal configuration at each training round.
CONTROLS: We'll compare AutoConfig against static configurations (e.g. combining standard data augmentation techniques,  Adam optimizer, cosine learning rate schedule, and Focal Loss) and adaptive components (e.g. learned augmentation policies, adaptive optimizers) and a baseline of self-tuning methods (e.g. evolution strategies and gradient-based optimization methods)
COST: 1,680 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: AutoConfig should improve validation performance over the state-of-the-art on several multi-label image classification benchmarks, and provide better stability and convergence speed. It may fail if the computations for calculating Q values for the off-policy setting constitute a bottleneck, or if the exploration-exploitation trade-off isn't properly balanced.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ensuring Stability in Adaptive Configuration Learning
PROPOSAL: To prevent the model from oscillating between different configurations and ensure that the adaptive process converges to a stable solution, we'll implement a control mechanism based on spectral normalization and regularization to penalize large variations in the configuration space. This will be done by penalizing the difference between consecutive configurations, preventing the model from exploring the entire configuration space, but still allowing for adaptation.
CONTROLS: The impact of this regularization will be compared to the unregularized version, as well as to other regularization techniques, such as L1 and L2 regularization.
COST: 3,300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Regularization is likely to lead to improved stability and convergence of the adaptive configuration learning process, but may also limit its ability to explore the configuration space and potentially miss the optimal configuration.

We'll compare the performance of this transferable approach to the traditional approach of fine-tuning the model from scratch on the new dataset.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Adapting Data Augmentation Using Jointly-Trained Switching Policies
PROPOSAL: We propose to use jointly-trained switching policies for data augmentation, which adapt and switch between different augmentation strategies based on the self-monitoring of learned representations along the training process. Specifically, we train a switching model to predict which augmentation policy to apply given the current model's output and the training instance's information. We will explore simple policy switching between augmentation types with individuals settings, and a more complex sequence decoding strategy, where multiple augmentation policies are combined to construct sequential transformations.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to static data augmentation policies and ablate the effect of jointly-trained switching policies by comparing to randomly chosen static augmentation sequences. In addition, we will evaluate the sensitivity of our approach to different policy architectures and the scale factors of switching costs.
COST: 1440
PREDICTION: We predict that our approach will achieve significantly better performance on various multi-label image classification benchmarks, such as Pascal VOC, CUB and NUS-WIDE, and especially improve the performance of tail classes. However, our method might suffer from initial overfitting and inefficient exploration due to the lack of guidance on optimal policy switches.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Learning Intrinsic Curiosity Driven Learning Rate Adaptation
PROPOSAL: We propose a learning intrinsic curiosity driven learning rate adaptation approach, which encourages the model to explore different learning rates based on the intrinsic curiosity of the learning process. The intrinsic curiosity will be measured by an attention-based mechanism, which assesses the model's uncertainty in its output feature space and evaluates whether augmenting the current learning rate will lead to a more informative output. Our approach will explore a learnable inverse reinforcement learning framework to define the rewards and update the learning rate based on the learning progress.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate our approach by comparing it to static learning rate schedules and adaptively changing learning rates proposed by existing literature, such as one-cycle learning. In addition, we will ablate our approach by experimenting with different functions to measure intrinsic curiosity and validate our learnable inverse reinforcement learning framework with a fixed set of rewards.
COST: 2160
PREDICTION: We predict that our approach will converge faster and improve the final performance on various multi-label image classification benchmarks, such as PASCAL VOC and NUS-WIDE, especially under complex scenarios where multiple learning rates need to be adapted. However, our approach may suffer from over-exploration and suffer from the explosion of reward dimensions in citing more accurate intrinsic curiosity measurements.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Self-Modulating Optimizers for Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We propose a self-modulating optimizer that dynamically adjusts its parameters based on the learning process to adapt to the evolving label correlations and class difficulty in multi-label image classification. Our self-modulating optimizer consists of a meta-optimizer that updates the learning rate of the original optimizer, and a self-tuning module that learns the optimal schedule for releasing the updates to the original optimizer based on the change in the model's predictions and the confidence of the model. Our approach will explore different self-tuning mechanisms and evaluate their performance on a self-modulating scheme.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach to static optimizers, such as SGD and Adam, and the adaptive optimizers proposed by existing literature, such as AdaGrad and RMSProp. In addition, we will ablate our approach by removing the meta-optimizer, the self-tuning module, or the updates release schedule.
COST: 3240
PREDICTION: We predict that our approach will improve the performance on various multi-label image classification benchmarks, such as PASCAL VOC and NUS-WIDE, especially for tail classes. However, our approach may suffer from over-tuning of the self-modulating optimizer, requiring additional specialized techniques to avoid overfitting and achieve stable training.

CWB-JFlex will adaptively allocate computational resources to state-of-the-art region exploration based on confidence scores, solving problems like excessive local exploration or ineffective early exploitation exploration.
CONTROLS: Compare CWB-JFlex with the standard JFlex and various baselines on several standard benchmarks for multi-label image classification.

TITLE: Robust Quantization with Calibration-based Energy Regularization
PROPOSAL: Employ an adapted version of energy-based regularization to alleviate the issue of rare outlier samples in the calibration set. Design a calibration-specific energy term that encompasses the local and global variance of activations statistics from the calibration set, accounting for situations where the calibration data covers an extraordinarily small region of the overall data distribution. Apply the energy penalty to the calibration-forward pass, pre-learned special tokens, and image tokens jointly to comply with data-dependent transforms. Perform Bayesian optimization to determine the optimal energy weight through a grid search over a set of established performance metrics.

PREDICTION: The energy-based regularization term can significantly improve the robustness of the quantized VGGT model when faced with inadequate calibration data, and its efficiency will contribute substantially to achieving consistent performance across different bit-widths.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Tail-Optimized Quantization for 3D Reconstruction Transformers
PROPOSAL: Investigate the efficacy of tail-optimized quantization methods, such as histogram equalization and clipping, specifically tailored for addressing the heavy-tailed and high-variance characteristics of activations in 3D reconstruction transformers. Compare these optimized methods against standard quantization techniques (such as uniform or symmetric quantization) in the context of the VGGT model on the ScanNet dataset. Train calibration sets comprising diverse sets of scanned scenes and evaluate the resulting models under full-precision guidance.
CONTROLS: Plain uniform quantization (PUQ) with fixed bit-width as baseline control, plus a non-optimized histogram equalization (HEQ) as ablation control for evaluating the effect of tail optimization alone.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: Tail-optimized quantization methods will improve robustness to outlier samples in the calibration sets and generalize better to unseen scenes compared to standard uniform or symmetric quantization by up to 2-5% relative improvement in calibration benchmarks due to better intra-model capture of tail statistics and reduced likelihood-variance; however, expected performance in robust scenes may degrade when the seen calibration set includes rare but critical outliers that ill-represent the calibration-based quantization range.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Tail-Optimized Quantization for 3D Reconstruction Transformers
PROPOSAL: Investigate the efficacy of tail-optimized quantization methods, such as histogram equalization and clipping, specifically tailored for addressing the heavy-tailed and high-variance characteristics of activations in 3D reconstruction transformers. Compare these optimized methods against standard quantization techniques (such as uniform or symmetric quantization) in the context of the VGGT model on the ScanNet dataset. Train calibration sets comprising diverse sets of scanned scenes and evaluate the resulting models under full-precision guidance.
CONTROLS: Plain uniform quantization (PUQ) with fixed bit-width as baseline control, plus a non-optimized histogram equalization (HEQ) as ablation control for evaluating the effect of tail optimization alone.
COST: 36000
PREDICTION: Tail-optimized quantization methods will improve robustness to outlier samples in the calibration sets and generalize better to unseen scenes compared to standard uniform or symmetric quantization by up to 2-5% relative improvement in calibration benchmarks due to better intra-model capture of tail statistics and reduced likelihood-variance; however, expected performance in robust scenes may degrade when the seen calibration set includes rare but critical outliers that ill-represent the calibration-based quantization range.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Robust Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformers
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel post-training quantization framework, Robust Token Quantization (RTQ), which leverages a two-stage approach to adaptively learn quantization parameters from a small calibration set. In the first stage, a pre-quantization feature extractor is trained to identify the heavy-tailed and high-variance activation patterns associated with data-independent special tokens. In the second stage, a costly but robust single-sample learning algorithm - Iterative Theta-Prototype Refining (IGTR) - is applied iteratively to the pre-quantization features to adjust the quantization ranges dynamically.
CONTROLS: Comparisons with the following baselines: PTQ4DiT, KMeans++, and Legacy transformed quantization (default transformer QAT)
COST: 540
PREDICTION: RTQ is expected to outperform state-of-the-art quantization methods, particularly in preserving the accuracy of camera pose estimation, point map, and point cloud reconstruction. It might fail if the pre-quantization stage is not robust enough to correctly identify the unique patterns of special tokens.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Quantization-Aware Few-Shot Learning for Complex Multi-View Scenes
PROPOSAL: We propose a few-shot learning method, Meta-Quantizer (MQ), that fine-tunes a pre-trained quantizer on a small set of diverse calibration samples representative of varying camera poses, point of view angles and point density. MQ dynamically adjusts its search granularity to capture the underlying semantic space of 3D scenes and leverages a fast calibration process using representative samples from various distributions. By reconfiguring the quantizer within each few-shot learning cycle, MQ may adaptively address the varying degrees of distribution shift across scenes.
CONTROLS: Comparisons with the following baselines: standard PTQ and dynamic feedforward transformers with PTQ for adapter/ channel manner
COST: 827.17
PREDICTION: MQ is expected to show significant improvements over standard PTQ in real-world multi-view 3D scenes, particularly when the calibration set includes diverse sample populations. It might fail if the pre-trained quantizer is overly specialized to a particular task or lacks sufficient capacity to generalize across the population.
