PROPOSAL: We revise the Robust Token Quantization (RTQ) framework by incorporating a novel per-token variance normalization (PTV) module, which dynamically adjusts the variance of activation patterns associated with data-independent special tokens to align better with standard distributions. PTV is trained jointly with RTQ to improve its quantization-aware adaptation and reduce reliance on coarse calibration sets.
CONTROLS: Comparisons with original RTQ, PTQ4DiT, and state-of-the-art token variance reduction methods
COST: 812
PREDICTION: With PTV, RTQ is expected to exhibit improved performance and robustness across a range of calibration sets, achieving higher accuracy and better generalization in multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks. However, its increased capacity might come at a cost of higher computational overhead during deployment.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Progressive Teacher-Student Knowledge Distillation for Bidirectional Quantized 3D Transformers
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel bidirectional knowledge distillation method, Progressive Teacher-Student (PTS), to bridge the accuracy gap between the pre-trained 3D transformer student and a quantized teacher. PTS iteratively distills knowledge from a progressively quantized teacher with varying bit widths to adaptively retain the critical characteristics of the pre-trained teacher while minimizing the accuracy loss introduced by quantization.
CONTROLS: Comparisons with standard teacher-student knowledge distillation and visual transformers with dynamic channel pruning
COST: 1250
PREDICTION: PTS is expected to preserve the accuracy benefits of pre-trained 3D transformer while providing effective supervision for quantized student networks, achieving significantly better performance in multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks than state-of-the-art quantization methods. However, the teacher-student paradigm might also introduce new training requirements and potentially higher memory overhead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Robust Post-Training Quantization for Vision Transformers
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel post-training quantization framework, Robust Token Quantization (RTQ), which leverages a two-stage approach to adaptively learn quantization parameters from a small calibration set. In the first stage, a pre-quantization feature extractor is trained to identify the heavy-tailed and high-variance activation patterns associated with data-independent special tokens. In the second stage, a costly but robust single-sample learning algorithm - Iterative Theta-Prototype Refining (IGTR) - is applied iteratively to the pre-quantization features to adjust the quantization ranges dynamically.
CONTROLS: Comparisons with the following baselines: PTQ4DiT, KMeans++, and Legacy transformed quantization (default transformer QAT)
COST: 1620
PREDICTION: RTQ is expected to outperform state-of-the-art quantization methods, particularly in preserving the accuracy of camera pose estimation, point map, and point cloud reconstruction. It might fail if the pre-quantization stage is not robust enough to correctly identify the unique patterns of special tokens.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Quantization-Aware Few-Shot Learning for Complex Multi-View Scenes
PROPOSAL: We propose a few-shot learning method, Meta-Quantizer (MQ), that fine-tunes a pre-trained quantizer on a small set of diverse calibration samples representative of varying camera poses, point of view angles and point density. MQ dynamically adjusts its search granularity to capture the underlying semantic space of 3D scenes and leverages a fast calibration process using representative samples from various distributions. By reconfiguring the quantizer within each few-shot learning cycle, MQ may adaptively address the varying degrees of distribution shift across scenes.
CONTROLS: Comparisons with the following baselines: standard PTQ and dynamic feedforward transformers with PTQ for adapter/ channel manner
COST: 2475
PREDICTION: MQ is expected to show significant improvements over standard PTQ in real-world multi-view 3D scenes, particularly when the calibration set includes diverse sample populations. It might fail if the pre-trained quantizer is overly specialized to a particular task or lacks sufficient capacity to generalize across the population.

PTV is trained jointly with RTQ to improve its quantization-aware adaptation and reduce reliance on coarse calibration sets.
CONTROLS: Comparisons with original RTQ, PTQ4DiT, and state-of-the-art token variance reduction methods

TITLE: Progressive Teacher-Student Knowledge Distillation for Bidirectional Quantized 3D Transformers
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel bidirectional knowledge distillation method, Progressive Teacher-Student (PTS), to bridge the accuracy gap between the pre-trained 3D transformer student and a quantized teacher. PTS iteratively distills knowledge from a progressively quantized teacher with varying bit widths to adaptively retain the critical characteristics of the pre-trained teacher while minimizing the accuracy loss introduced by quantization.
CONTROLS: Comparisons with standard teacher-student knowledge distillation and visual transformers with dynamic channel pruning

PREDICTION: PTS is expected to preserve the accuracy benefits of pre-trained 3D transformer while providing effective supervision for quantized student networks, achieving significantly better performance in multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks than state-of-the-art quantization methods. However, the teacher-student paradigm might also introduce new training requirements and potentially higher memory overhead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Quantization-Aware Calibration Pretraining
PROPOSAL: Develop a calibration pretraining strategy that combines the benefits of model-agnostic calibration methods from the literature with the novel properties of multi-view 3D transformers like VGGT. This entails a two-stage approach, first pretraining a lightweight calibration model using the full-precision VGGT as a fixed feature extractor, then optionally fine-tuning the calibration model with a reconstructive loss on the target quantization task.
CONTROLS: Compare to naive PTQ methods, also to ablated versions of the calibration pretraining pipeline (e.g., no pretraining, no fine-tuning).
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Effective calibration pretraining should help reduce the variance in activation distributions and decrease the detrimental effects of quantization on accuracy, achieving up to 90% of the full-precision performance on complex 3D scenes. Failure might occur if the calibration task does not closely mimic the actual quantization task, causing the pretraining to focus on spurious correlations rather than relevant aspects of the activation distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Diverse Token Sampling for Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: Address the issue of biased activation distributions associated with data-independent special tokens by employing Diverse Token Sampling (DTS). With DTS, instead of considering all special tokens, sample a subset that is maximally distant in the learned token space. This aims to improve the representation power of the sampled token set and render the weight distribution of special tokens more representative of the overall data distribution, thus reducing quantization errors.
CONTROLS: Compare to random token sampling, also compare DTS to dataset-specific token sampling heuristics to ensure compatibility with real-world data.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: By promoting a more diverse special token set through balanced sampling, this approach is expected to maintain a significant portion (above 80%) of the original performance, especially when compared to simpler sampling methods; failure might occur if the learned token representation is dominated by idiosyncrasies specific to the training dataset.

TITLE: Activation-Distribution-Aware Quantization (ADAQ)
PROPOSAL: Design a novel activation distribution-aware quantization scheme that dynamically adjusts the number and granularity of quantization bins based on the complex, heavy-tailed activation probability distributions of VGGT. By iteratively splitting bins with high density and aggregating bins with low density, ADAQ aims to adaptively represent the activation distribution with minimal loss of information, enabling more efficient quantization.
CONTROLS: Compare to standard fixed-point quantization schemes, also compare ADAQ to memory-intensive techniques that require storing and processing dense probability distributions.

TITLE: Diverse Token Sampling for Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: Address the issue of biased activation distributions associated with data-independent special tokens by employing Diverse Token Sampling (DTS). With DTS, instead of considering all special tokens, sample a subset that is maximally distant in the learned token space. This aims to improve the representation power of the sampled token set and render the weight distribution of special tokens more representative of the overall data distribution, thus reducing quantization errors.
CONTROLS: Compare to random token sampling, also compare DTS to dataset-specific token sampling heuristics to ensure compatibility with real-world data.
COST: 2700
PREDICTION: By promoting a more diverse special token set through balanced sampling, this approach is expected to maintain a significant portion (above 80%) of the original performance, especially when compared to simpler sampling methods; failure might occur if the learned token representation is dominated by idiosyncrasies specific to the training dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Activation-Distribution-Aware Quantization (ADAQ)
PROPOSAL: Design a novel activation distribution-aware quantization scheme that dynamically adjusts the number and granularity of quantization bins based on the complex, heavy-tailed activation probability distributions of VGGT. By iteratively splitting bins with high density and aggregating bins with low density, ADAQ aims to adaptively represent the activation distribution with minimal loss of information, enabling more efficient quantization.
CONTROLS: Compare to standard fixed-point quantization schemes, also compare ADAQ to memory-intensive techniques that require storing and processing dense probability distributions.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: By minimizing loss of signal due to heavy-tailed activations, ADAQ is expected to increase the peak performance achievable under quantization by around 20%, but requires careful calibration to find a good trade-off between compression efficiency, accuracy, and computation time; ADAQ might degrade if not properly aligned with the distribution of activations from the photometric, geometric data.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Bit-Width on PTQ Performance
PROPOSAL: We will train and report the performance of VGGT on a 256x256 crop of the PlayStation dataset, at various fixed precisions: 5 bits, 8 bits, 16 bits (full precision).
CONTROLS: Baseline: full-precision VGGT; Baseline: correspondingly quantized VGGT (linear scaling of weights and activations to integers).
COST: 330
PREDICTION: Lowering bit-widths will gradually degrade accuracy and speedup, with 5-bit VGGT suffering noticeable drops in depth estimation and camera pose estimation tasks and 5-bit performance being significantly worse than both lower bit-widths compared to full-precision. However, with around 10-20x speedup, plenty of real-time applications will accept a substantial accuracy cost to run VGGT on anything below 8-bits.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Quantization-Aware Rank-Decay Regularization
PROPOSAL: We will modify the VGGT architecture by adding a rank decay penalty to the loss function, that increases loss with large singular values, thereby stabilizing the Hessian and inducing more robustness to low-precision evaluations. This is implemented by replacing the standard L2 loss with an adaptive weighted L2 loss function, depending on the magnitude of each singular value obtained from a snapshot of the model's weights.
CONTROLS: Baseline: regular VGGT; Ablation: VGGT with single precision weights only to ensure reliability of the additional loss term
COST: 660
PREDICTION: This approach should mitigate the loss of information associated with quantization of heavy-tailed special token activations, and improve the stability and stability of training the quantized VGGT in low bit-widths by allowing convergence of originally unstable data-independent special tokens, possibly even higher in cases of low learning rates, under 8-bit components, no substantial improvement or model instability at 5-bit.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Sample Selection for Calibration: Entropy-Based vs. Importance Sampling
PROPOSAL: We compare the effectiveness of two methods for selecting calibration samples for PTQ: 1) entropy-based importance sampling (EBIS), which samples from the input data distribution according to the entropy of each input view, and 2) uniform sampling with out-of-distribution (OOD) detection to generalize to novel unseen scenes.
CONTROLS: Baseline: no calibration (i.e. using a fixed, full-precision VGGT for PTQ); Baseline: uniform sampling calibration; Baseline: PTQ without specified calibration method.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: EBIS will yield better calibration performance and generalization to novel scenes than uniform sampling. However, it is not clear whether this improvement is big enough to compensate for the potential increase in computation time needed to compute the empirical entropy for each view across various depths.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Sample Selection for Calibration: Entropy-Based vs. Importance Sampling with Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: We extend the sample selection by using two methods: 1) entropy-based importance sampling (EBIS), and 2) a contrastive learning-based approach to learn an embedding of each input view and select samples across the learned semantic space, attempting to cover the full-range of possible scene configurations.
CONTROLS: Baseline: no calibration (i.e. using a fixed, full-precision VGGT for PTQ); Baseline: uniform sampling calibration; Baseline: PTQ without specified calibration method.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: Contrastive learning will perform better than entropy-based sampling, since it could capture the intrinsic semantic structure of the data, providing a more meaningful way to sample from unseen scenes and leapfrog the deficiency in capturing complex temporal relations or foreground objects separation in scenes; But we also anticipate some challenges in designing effective positive and negative pair functions.

PROPOSAL: We investigate the challenge of quantizing learned special tokens, such as the camera and register tokens in the VGGT, by developing a novel learned parameterization scheme, in which the pre-trained special tokens are adaptively linearly re-weighted, epoch-wise or by iteration count, instead of being frozen at the quantization stage, to mitigate extreme gradient unfolding while capturing valuable multi-view image correspondences for the scene and making adaptation to low-precision during inference more investigable.
CONTROLS: Baseline: PTQ for VGGT without learned special tokens; Baseline: pre-quantization special token freezing approach.

PREDICTION: This method will better deal with special token weights -- particularly camera tokens -- where the current fixed-assignment is most needed for prior targeting, leveraging conventional calibration advances; All language experiment are interested to make such adjustments. Additionally it could even offer higher stability against cross-epoch contamination or forward pass by synthesis acceleration on 16 bit acceleration, but achieving substantial step forward sacrifices.

TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Bit-Width on PTQ Performance
PROPOSAL: We will train and report the performance of VGGT on a 256x256 crop of the PlayStation dataset, at various fixed precisions: 5 bits, 8 bits, 16 bits (full precision).
CONTROLS: Baseline: full-precision VGGT; Baseline: correspondingly quantized VGGT (linear scaling of weights and activations to integers).
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: Lowering bit-widths will gradually degrade accuracy and speedup, with 5-bit VGGT suffering noticeable drops in depth estimation and camera pose estimation tasks and 5-bit performance being significantly worse than both lower bit-widths compared to full-precision. However, with around 10-20x speedup, plenty of real-time applications will accept a substantial accuracy cost to run VGGT on anything below 8-bits.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Quantization-Aware Rank-Decay Regularization
PROPOSAL: We will modify the VGGT architecture by adding a rank decay penalty to the loss function, that increases loss with large singular values, thereby stabilizing the Hessian and inducing more robustness to low-precision evaluations. This is implemented by replacing the standard L2 loss with an adaptive weighted L2 loss function, depending on the magnitude of each singular value obtained from a snapshot of the model's weights.
CONTROLS: Baseline: regular VGGT; Ablation: VGGT with single precision weights only to ensure reliability of the additional loss term
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: This approach should mitigate the loss of information associated with quantization of heavy-tailed special token activations, and improve the stability and stability of training the quantized VGGT in low bit-widths by allowing convergence of originally unstable data-independent special tokens, possibly even higher in cases of low learning rates, under 8-bit components, no substantial improvement or model instability at 5-bit.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Sample Selection for Calibration: Entropy-Based vs. Importance Sampling
PROPOSAL: We compare the effectiveness of two methods for selecting calibration samples for PTQ: 1) entropy-based importance sampling (EBIS), which samples from the input data distribution according to the entropy of each input view, and 2) uniform sampling with out-of-distribution (OOD) detection to generalize to novel unseen scenes.
CONTROLS: Baseline: no calibration (i.e. using a fixed, full-precision VGGT for PTQ); Baseline: uniform sampling calibration; Baseline: PTQ without specified calibration method.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: EBIS will yield better calibration performance and generalization to novel scenes than uniform sampling. However, it is not clear whether this improvement is big enough to compensate for the potential increase in computation time needed to compute the empirical entropy for each view across various depths.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Sample Selection for Calibration: Entropy-Based vs. Importance Sampling with Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: We extend the sample selection by using two methods: 1) entropy-based importance sampling (EBIS), and 2) a contrastive learning-based approach to learn an embedding of each input view and select samples across the learned semantic space, attempting to cover the full-range of possible scene configurations.
CONTROLS: Baseline: no calibration (i.e. using a fixed, full-precision VGGT for PTQ); Baseline: uniform sampling calibration; Baseline: PTQ without specified calibration method.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Contrastive learning will perform better than entropy-based sampling, since it could capture the intrinsic semantic structure of the data, providing a more meaningful way to sample from unseen scenes and leapfrog the deficiency in capturing complex temporal relations or foreground objects separation in scenes; But we also anticipate some challenges in designing effective positive and negative pair functions.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: PTQ for Vision Transformers with Learned Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: We investigate the challenge of quantizing learned special tokens, such as the camera and register tokens in the VGGT, by developing a novel learned parameterization scheme, in which the pre-trained special tokens are adaptively linearly re-weighted, epoch-wise or by iteration count, instead of being frozen at the quantization stage, to mitigate extreme gradient unfolding while capturing valuable multi-view image correspondences for the scene and making adaptation to low-precision during inference more investigable.
CONTROLS: Baseline: PTQ for VGGT without learned special tokens; Baseline: pre-quantization special token freezing approach.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: This method will better deal with special token weights -- particularly camera tokens -- where the current fixed-assignment is most needed for prior targeting, leveraging conventional calibration advances; All language experiment are interested to make such adjustments. ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Automated Multi-Bit Bit-Width Selection using Branch-and-Bound Search
PROPOSAL: We develop a branch-and-bound search algorithm to automatically determine the optimal multi-bit bit-width configuration for the VGGT. By leveraging the additive property of 3D reconstruction tasks, we decompose the globally optimal solution into multiple smaller sub-problems, each corresponding to a region or task within the overall scene, allowing for efficient and scalable exploration of the possible bit-width configurations.
CONTROLS: Baseline: manually configured bit-widths; Baseline: uniform bit-width across all components.
COST: 12500

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: A Pilot Study for Practical Implementation of PTQ-Equipped VGGT on Edge Devices
PROPOSAL: We prototype and evaluate the performance of the PTQ-equipped VGGT on a state-of-the-art edge device, such as a Google Coral or Raspberry Pi, to understand the practical feasibility and deployment challenges of large-scale 3D reconstruction models on resource-constrained devices. By comparing the model accuracy, inference speed, and memory footprint of the PTQ-equipped VGGT with its full-precision counterpart, we can demonstrate the potential of PTQ to enable real-time 3D reconstruction on edge devices.
CONTROLS: Baseline: full-precision VGGT on a powerful device; Baseline: PTQ-equipped VGGT on the same powerful device.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing Expressive Power of DPT for Multi-Modal Actions
PROPOSAL: Extend the DPT model by incorporating a normalizing flow module to transform the action space into a more latent, lower-dimensional representation. Evaluate this setup on a selection of synthetic continuous control tasks from the domains of robot manipulation and robot locomotion.
CONTROLS: Compare against vanilla DPT on the same tasks, as well as a strong ablated version incorporating a separate fixed-size action embedding learned through self-supervised objectives.
COST: 16,800
PREDICTION: The proposed extension should be shown to capture more nuanced, multi-modal action distributions, leading to improved performance across the evaluated tasks. If successful, this could serve as a foundation for further exploration into more intricate policy representations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Scaling of DPT to High-Dimensional Observations
PROPOSAL: Modify the DPT model to accommodate high-dimensional observation spaces encountered in domains like autonomous driving and industrial process control. Investigate employing techniques such as self-attention or recurrent layers to effectively aggregate information from the observation space.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the modified DPT on tasks with high-dimensional observations, comparing against the original DPT and a state-of-the-art offline reinforcement learning method on observational modifications.
COST: 21,645.808
PREDICTION: This adaptation should enable DPT to handle a broader range of tasks, and may reveal new challenges in distilling informative representations from high-dimensional data.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Augmenting DPT with Task-Invariant Features for Improved Transfer
PROPOSAL: Incorporate a task-invariant feature extractor into the DPT architecture, aiming to capture shared information across tasks that can aid transfer of learned policies. This could leverage architectures like convolutional neural networks or transformer encoders that are typically used for vision and NLP tasks but are effective at capturing diverse patterns.
CONTROLS: Ablate the task-invariant feature extractor and compare transfer performance between full DPT models with and without this component, against the control of using a strong offline reinforcement learning baseline.
COST: 25,000
PREDICTION: By extracting and combining task-invariant features, the agent should exhibit enhanced transfer capabilities, allowing it to adapt to entirely unseen tasks and novel versions of known domains with greater efficiency. This should mark significant progress towards real-world applicability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Role of Contextual Information in In-Context Learning for DPT
PROPOSAL: Design experiments to analyze how different types of contextual information (e.g., demonstration trajectories, task descriptions, and object-aware context) impact the performance and generalization of the DPT model in diverse, continuous-control settings.
CONTROLS: Compare the model's performance with and without access to contextual information, as well as against a baseline that only uses a static offline dataset.
COST: 30,000
PREDICTION: This investigation should provide valuable insights into the importance of contextual information for in-context learning and adaptation, and could inform the development of more effective contextual-aware architectures for DPT and similar models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing DPT with Algorithm Distillation on Realistic Multi-Domain Tasks
PROPOSAL: Implement and evaluate the DPT model alongside Algorithm Distillation on a selection of realistic, synthetic multi-domain tasks from the domains of robot manipulation and robot locomotion, and quantitatively compare their performance and adaptation efficiency under different conditions.
CONTROLS: Compare against strong offline reinforcement learning baselines, as well as various ablated versions of DPT and AD to isolate their respective strengths and weaknesses.
COST: 35,000
PREDICTION: This direct comparison should provide a clearer picture of the relative effectiveness of DPT and Algorithm Distillation on realistic multi-domain tasks, and shed light on the design choices that favor one approach over the other.

PREDICTION: We expect to see significant improvement over vanilla DPT on task-agnostic metrics due to the in-context learner's ability to adapt to new environments. Due to the limited capacity of current DPT models, we may struggle to achieve expert-level performance on tasks that require precise control, such as robot manipulation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Repository-based DPT for Scalable In-Context Learning
PROPOSAL: We will explore the extension of DPT to allow it to leverage the vast repository of transitions and policy evaluations generated by previous in-context learning attempts. Specifically, we propose to store these evaluations in a learned repository, which can be efficiently queried during new episode rollouts. At each time step, the agent will refer to both its own replay buffer and the repository to inform its decision-making process, allowing it to leverage previously evaluated policies without substantially increasing its memory usage.
CONTROLS: We will compare the repository-based DPT to both vanilla DPT and a version of DPT that uses a precomputed CDF of the action distribution; we will also evaluate the performance of each approach on a static subset of the repository, with and without online updates.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: By mitigating the issue of insufficient capacity in batch inference, we expect repository-based DPT to surpass vanilla DPT performance in a wide range of tasks, and maintain a stable level of performance in unconstrained environments, potentially allowing us to finally evaluate in-depth the theoretical benefits of in-context learning for reinforcement learners and cartfully contrast the learned model with methods with constant sample complexity in them theory (algorithm distillation being another related alternative!).

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Enabling Efficient Online Learning in DPT
PROPOSAL: We will propose a novel memory-efficient approach to enable DPT to learn and adapt to new environments in real-time, even with limited computational resources. Our approach will utilize a tiered buffer system that stores both the recent interaction history and the longer-term repository of transitions. We will develop a multi-resolution representation of the action distribution, allowing for efficient and on-the-fly updates during online learning.
CONTROLS: We will compare the memory-efficient DPT to vanilla DPT, a batch-trained variant of DPT that uses the full repository, and a meta-optimized variant of DPT that uses the repository with a hierarchical buffer structure.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: By leveraging the tiered buffer system and multi-resolution action representation, we expect to see significant improvements in online learning efficiency, enabling DPT to adapt to new tasks and environments in real-time. However, the memory-efficient approach may also introduce some degree of forgetting, which could impact overall performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Generalization and Robustness in DPT
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a comprehensive evaluation of the generalization and robustness of DPT to unseen tasks and environments, as well as to changes in the task distribution. Specifically, we will perform a family of tasks-based evaluation, where we transfer DPT to a succession of related and unrelated tasks, with varying degrees of similarity to the training tasks. We will also evaluate DPT's robustness to perturbations in the task parameters, observation space, and action space.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of DPT to a suite of baselines, including a variant of DPT that uses a frozen model, a classifier-based baseline, and a traditional (non-DPT) reinforcement learning algorithm.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: Our evaluation will reveal whether DPT's ability to generalize and adapt to new tasks and environments is truly robust, and whether it can effectively leverage the recently acquired task-agnostic experience. We anticipate that DPT will perform well on family of tasks-based evaluation, but may struggle with tasks that are significantly different from those seen during training.

We anticipate that our results will provide valuable insights into the design of future reinforcement learning algorithms, and shed light on the relationship between task-agnostic knowledge and adaptability in DPT.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Modal Action Distribution for Better In-Context Learning
PROPOSAL: We explore and propose a new action distribution formulation for DPT-style in-context learners, aiming to capture the complexity and multi-modality of continuous action posteriors. We introduce an attention-based neural network that incorporates both a deterministic policy and a stochastic policy to generate continuous actions. This multi-modal action distribution allows the agent to explore different possibilities and adapt to new situations effectively.
 The attention-based neural network receives the query state and the context (history of transitions) as input and outputs a normal distribution over actions, reflecting the probability of each action in the multi-modal action space.
 We train the model using a combination of rewards from the environment and a self-supervised policy loss, where the self-supervised loss function encourages the model to produce diverse action distributions when given different contexts.
 We anticipate that our proposed action distribution formulation will result in better performance on unseen tasks and improved adaptability in diverse environments, but we note that training could become unstable if the self-supervised policy loss overpowers the reward signal.
CONTROLS: Vanilla DPT, DPT with a deterministic policy only
COST: 600
PREDICTION: We expect significant improvements over existing methods, especially in multi-modal action spaces, but there's a possibility that the model might over-explore and struggle to converge.

TITLE: Augmented Transition Retrieval for DPT-style In-Context Learning
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel transition retrieval mechanism designed to augment the Decision Pretrained Transformer (DPT) for in-context learning. This mechanism, named ART (Augmented Transition Retrieval), incorporates the agent's interaction history, task metadata, and environmental context into the retrieval process.
 ART retrieves a diverse set of transitions from the agent's prior experience, including those from different tasks, settings, and expertise levels. This composite set of transitions serves as a knowledge base that the DPT can draw upon to inform its decision-making in new contexts.
 By incorporating ART, we enhance the DPT's capacity to adapt to novel tasks and situations, leveraging its learned knowledge to generalize effectively across diverse domains and scenarios.
 We anticipate that ART will significantly boost the performance of DPT-style in-context learners, but there's a risk of over-reliance on the retrieved transitions leading to suboptimal exploration-exploitation trade-offs.
CONTROLS: DPT with and without ART, DPT-MT with standard retrieval
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: We expect significant adaptability gains with ART, but potential overfitting concerns in high-dimensional or rapidly changing environments.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Evaluating the Robustness of DPT-style In-Context Learners to Task Parameter Variations
PROPOSAL: Revised to include experiment design for a more comprehensive evaluation of robustness to task parameter variations:
 We generate task parameters for robot manipulation, robot locomotion, and humanoid control environments based on a set of meta-parameters (e.g., task difficulty, obstacle density, and environment layout).
 We collect evaluation data for the model under these varying parameter settings and divide it into three groups:
   1. Adversarial testing: task parameters are constrained to be significantly different from the training distribution to assess robustness to unexpected situations.
   2. Gradual perturbation: task parameters are gradually varied from the training distribution to evaluate the model's ability to adapt to mild changes.
   3. Meta-task adaptation: task parameters are sampled from a moderate to difficult distribution, and the model is evaluated on its ability to generalize across these parameter variations.
 We compare the performance of DPT-MT with the proposed multi-modal action distribution against a set of baseline models, including a DPT variant that undergoes fine-tuning on specific task parameter sets, to assess the effectiveness of in-context learning in adapting to unseen parameters.
 By incorporating these more nuanced testing schemes, we aim to provide a more comprehensive evaluation of the proposed methods' robustness and adaptability.
CONTROLS: DPT-MT, DPT with fine-tuning on specific task parameters, Vanilla DPT
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: We expect significant improvements in robustness and adaptability for our proposed methods, with some potential issues in handling extreme or unforeseen parameter variations.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Augmented Transition Retrieval for DPT-style In-Context Learning
PROPOSAL: Revised to incorporate online transition retrieval and a novel indexation method for efficient retrieval:
 Instead of relying on a pre-retrieved set of transitions, we propose an online transition retrieval mechanism that continuously updates the indexation and retrieval process as the agent interacts with its environment.
 We introduce a novel indexation method using a structured hashing scheme that partitions the transition space efficiently, allowing for fast and accurate retrievals. This approach enables the agent to adapt to new situations and environments without relying on prior knowledge.
 We incorporate this online retrieval mechanism into the DPT framework, integrating it with the agent's decision-making process to enable real-time adaptation to new contexts and environments.
CONTROLS: DPT with standard retrieval, DPT-MT with ART, Vanilla DPT
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: We expect significant performance gains from online transition retrieval, particularly in dynamic or fast-changing environments, but may require additional computational resources to sustain complex indexing and retrieval processes in real-time.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Knowledge Distillation for Efficient DPT-style In-Context Learning
PROPOSAL: We investigate the application of knowledge distillation (KD) techniques to the DPT-style in-context learning framework, aiming to improve the efficiency and scalability of these models.
 By training a small student network to mimic the behavior of a large pre-trained teacher network (the DPT), we can distill the knowledge and expertise of the teacher into a more compact and efficient student model.
 We explore different KD techniques, including supervision, self-supervision, and adversarial distillation, to identify the most effective approach for DPT-style in-context learning.
 By leveraging KD, we anticipate being able to reduce the computational and memory requirements of our models while maintaining their performance and adaptability, enabling wider deployment and adoption in real-world applications.
CONTROLS: DPT-MT with and without KD, Vanilla DPT, a DPT variant retrained from the distilled model
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: We expect to achieve substantial reductions in model size and computation time while maintaining or improving in-context learning performance, but may require careful tuning of distillation hyperparameters to achieve optimal results.

TITLE: Multi-Agent and Hierarchical Frameworks for Scalable DPT-style In-Context Learning
PROPOSAL: We explore the scalability of DPT-style in-context learning by leveraging multi-agent and hierarchical frameworks, enabling the simultaneous learning and adaptation of multiple agents and levels of abstraction.
 We design and evaluate a multi-agent architecture where individual agents are trained to perform a set of tasks, while a high-level agent learns to coordinate and adapt to the behavior of the lower-level agents.
 We also investigate a hierarchical framework where a high-level agent provides abstract goals and constraints to a lower-level agent, which is responsible for executing the tasks in a more detailed and fine-grained manner.
 By combining the strengths of multi-agent and hierarchical learning, we aim to create scalable and efficient frameworks for DPT-style in-context learning that can tackle complex and dynamic real-world scenarios.
CONTROLS: DPT-MT with multi-agent architecture, DPT-MT with hierarchical framework, Vanilla DPT
COST: 21600
PREDICTION: We expect significant scalability gains through the use of multi-agent and hierarchical frameworks, particularly in complex and dynamic scenarios, but may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and coordination mechanisms to ensure effective adaptation and learning.

 By leveraging meta-learning, we aim to enable the DPT to continuously adapt and improve its performance in real-world scenarios, where changes in the environment, tasks, or agent capabilities may occur rapidly.

 We design and evaluate a multi-agent architecture where individual agents are trained to perform a set of tasks, while a high-level agent learns to coordinate and adapt to the behavior of the lower-level agents.
 We also investigate a hierarchical framework where a high-level agent provides abstract goals and constraints to a lower-level agent, which is responsible for executing the tasks in a more detailed and fine-grained manner.

TITLE: Investigating Vanilla DPT's Limitations on Continuous Action Spaces
PROPOSAL: Implement the Vanilla Decision Pretrained Transformer (DPT) on popular benchmark tasks, such as MuJoCo humanoids and robot manipulation domains, and measure its performance on continuous action spaces.
CONTROLS: Compare DPT with a policy that directly samples from a learned probabilistic model (GP), assessing whether posterior sampling over actions exploits the full multi-modality of the action space.
COST: 1800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect DPT to struggle on continuous-action tasks where the action space is highly multi-modal, struggling to capture local policy-dependent distributions. This will motivate further research into more expressive policy classes for DPT.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Modal Continuous Action Sampling for DPT
PROPOSAL: Extend Vanilla DPT to leverage multi-modal action distributions by integrating normalizing flows and Gaussian Mixture Models (GMMs) into its action sampling mechanism. This will enable DPT to capture complex, high-dimensional action spaces with a wide range of possible values and modes.
CONTROLS: Compare this extension with the original DPT architecture, as well as the policy that directly samples from a learned probabilistic model (GP).
COST: 5400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate this extension to improve DPT's performance in tasks with high-dimensional continuous action spaces, by more accurately capturing the full multi-modality of the action distribution, however, potential overfitting could hinder generalization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Effective In-Context Learning for Multi-Domain DPT
PROPOSAL: Design a task-specific prompt generator to create in-context prompts that effectively transfer knowledge across domains, using knowledge graph-based attention to dynamically select relevant experiences from the agent's offline dataset and auto-regressive prompts to adapt to the specific task. This generator will be trained on a few extra tasks and tasks from similar domains.
CONTROLS: Compare the effectiveness of this prompt generator to a random prompt sampler, and ablate the importance of knowledge graph-based attention.
COST: 7200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the generated prompts to improve DPT's transfer learning capabilities, enabling it to adapt more effectively to new tasks and domains without significant drop in performance, but might incur increased computation in longer prompts.

PROPOSAL: Revise the previous proposal: design an on-policy prompt generator that generates prompts based on the agent's own experiences during deployment, focusing on recent experiences to adapt to changing environments. The prompt generator will predict the optimal prompt given the current state and the entire offline dataset, using reinforcement learning to update the generator and align with the desired reward.
CONTROLS: Compare this on-policy approach with the previous task-specific generator, and ablate the importance of incorporating the entire offline dataset for prompt prediction.
COST: 8400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the on-policy prompt generator to further improve DPT's adaptation capabilities in changing environments and improve its real-time policy correction and adaptation, but might incur additional computation due to its real-time operation and need for frequent updates.
